docs.title: Modular OCR pipelines you can run anywhere
docs.text:
An Intertype C4 linecaster (1961), after a photograph in the Science Museum Group Collection, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Credit

Linecaster turns page images into text. You build an OCR pipeline from interchangeable steps (a model that reads the text, layout, tables, formulas, post-processing) and run it unchanged on a laptop, a GPU server, a Ray cluster or Hugging Face Jobs.

  • 🧩 Any step is replaceable. A vision-language model or a line recognizer reads the text; layout, table and formula models and rule-based post-processing are separate steps.
  • 🌍 Any machine. Only the command line changes, never the pipeline.
  • 🎯 The same result everywhere. A page's text depends only on that page and the pinned models.
  • 🔁 Built for long runs. Interrupted runs resume; failed pages are set aside with the reason.

📖 Docs: storytracer.github.io/linecaster: the reference, a page for every block and catalog entry, and llms.txt for coding agents.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick start
docs.text:
You need Python 3.12 and uv 0.13.6 or newer.

git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
uv run launch.py                               # list the recipes and models
uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/          # run a recipe
uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/   # run a vision-language model (needs vLLM and a GPU)

You get one page record per page in out/pages/. Add --files out/files --formats md,alto for per-page files.

Note

Every pipeline is a self-contained uv script with pinned dependencies and a lock file next to it. uv run installs what it needs on the first run; models download on first use.

docs.title: 🧭 Three ways to transcribe
docs.text:
1. A recipe: a tested combination of presets, one per step, with its own edition and evidence.

uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/

2. A vision-language model reads each page, or each layout region. It runs behind vLLM or SGLang, so it needs an NVIDIA GPU and the vllm command on the PATH.

uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0

3. The modular pipeline: layout, lines and a line recognizer, then post-processing. You choose a preset for every step; linecaster models lists them.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium \
  --typography ratios --recomposition unicode-recomposition --composition docling-composition
Flag Effect --layout single-region the whole page as one region, no layout model --tables, --formulas add table and formula recognition --typography headings and their levels --recomposition running text in paragraphs (without it, the page stays as laid out) --composition the page's document, for Markdown, HTML and JSON --set recognition.batch_size=4 change one option of a preset --files DIR --formats md,alto per-page files: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON --dry-run print the plan and its graph, run nothing

Options after a recipe's name override single steps; the run record lists them.

docs.title: 📥 Input
docs.text:
Pages from Flags a folder of images IMAGES (--item-from-parent: each subfolder is an item) a list of images IMAGES --paths-file pages.txt Parquet with an image column --parquet PATH (--image-key, --item-key, --sequence-key) IIIF or METS manifests --manifests FOLDER, --manifests list.txt, or --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url an earlier run --pages OUT/pages

Any fsspec path works: local, s3://, hf://. Manifests need the pybookget extra (pybookget); --existing-ocr also keeps the library's own OCR as ocr_original. PDF files are read by the PdfReader block (extra pypdfium2).

For large collections, fetch the images once, then transcribe, then bind the pages into items:

uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key url OUT --rate-limit 5/1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --recipe squiddle --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT2/pages OUT3 --recipe item-texts

docs.title: 📦 Output
docs.text:
Output For 🗂️ Page records (JSON Lines, Parquet) later pipelines: every intermediate result 🏛️ ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR libraries and viewers: every word with its position 📝 Markdown, HTML, DocLang, Docling JSON documents with headings, tables and formulas 📜 verbatim_txt per item the text as printed, for checking against a transcription 📖 readable_txt, readable_md per item reading and training: letterforms folded, hyphens joined, paragraphs flowed

The text as written is always kept; readable text is derived from it. All text is Unicode NFC; spelling is never modernized. Rejected pages go to rejects/ with the reason. Every run is traced with OpenTelemetry into OUT/traces/ (nothing is sent anywhere unless you set the OTEL_* variables), and linecaster traces OUT shows where the time went.

docs.title: 🌍 Run anywhere
docs.text:
Where Flags 💻 this machine none: models load inside the pipeline 🖥️ this machine, with a model server --backend served 🧮 a Ray cluster --on ray --tasks 64 ☁️ Hugging Face Jobs --on hf-jobs --commit <sha>

On Ray and HF Jobs every task gets one GPU and starts its own model server. A rerun into the same output folder runs only the tasks that didn't finish.

A model server that stays up 
P="--layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det --recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium"
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve $P
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1

For a vision-language model, --recognition-endpoint points transcribe_vlm.py at a running vLLM or SGLang. Servers listen on loopback only.

Ray

ray runs Ray's own command line with the pipeline's packages, so every machine has the same versions:

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ $P --on ray --tasks 64

Images and output must be on storage every machine can reach.

Hugging Face Jobs

One GPU per Job; each Job installs Linecaster at a pushed commit with the pipeline's pinned dependencies.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py s3://bhl-open-data/images hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/<run> $P \
  --paths-file hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>/pages.txt --env FSSPEC_S3_ANON=true \
  --on hf-jobs --commit <sha> --tasks 4000 --workers 64

--workers Jobs run at once. --flavor l4x4 --gpus 4 runs four tasks per Job. --dry-run launches nothing.

docs.title: ✍️ Your own pipeline
docs.text:
A pipeline is a list of blocks; datatrove runs it. This is the modular pipeline, cut down:

from datatrove.executor import LocalPipelineExecutor
from linecaster.backends import InProcess as P
from linecaster.blocks.composition import (
    Composer, Recomposer, Typographer)
from linecaster.blocks.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.blocks.lines import (
    LineAssigner, LineDetector)
from linecaster.blocks.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.blocks.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.blocks.text import UnicodeNormalizer
from linecaster.blocks.writers import PageFileWriter

pipeline = [
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLayoutEngine")),
    LineDetector(P("linecaster_paddlex:PaddleLineEngine")),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer(
        P("linecaster_kraken:KrakenRecognitionEngine")),
    UnicodeNormalizer(),
    Typographer("ratios@1"),
    Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1"),
    Composer("docling-composition@1"),
    PageFileWriter("out/", formats=("md", "alto")),
]
LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline, logging_dir="out/logs").run()

Every block declares what it reads and adds, so a pipeline is checked before it starts: a recognizer without lines fails at once, with every problem listed. Put the script in pipelines/ with the # /// script block of pipelines/transcribe_modular.py (it brings the engines) and build it with linecaster.runtime.run.main to get the pipelines' command line on every machine. The pipelines reference covers backends, partial runs (--until, --after) and the builder.

docs.title: 🧩 How it works
docs.text:
1. One record per page. Every step reads the page's Transcription and adds its part: regions, lines, text, tables, a document. Steps share the data model and nothing else.
  2. Contracts. Each block declares what it reads, adds, replaces or removes; the builder checks the pipeline and draws its graph from them.
  3. Backends. A model step runs InProcess, Served (a model server reached through saturate, which keeps the GPU busy) or Chat (a vision-language model behind an OpenAI-compatible server).
  4. Executors. datatrove splits the pages into tasks, runs them locally, on Ray or on HF Jobs, and resumes where a run stopped.

Models batch only the lines of one page, and model revisions and numerically relevant libraries are pinned, so a page's output never depends on the machine or on what else runs. Different GPU types can still differ in rare single characters.

docs.title: 🧰 Models and blocks
docs.text:
Every configuration is a preset in Linecaster's catalog: an engine, a model at a pinned revision with its original model card, and settings. Released editions never change. Vision-language models run behind vLLM or SGLang; the other models run inside the pipeline or behind linecaster serve, one package per engine: linecaster-kraken (kraken), linecaster-paddlex (PaddleX) and linecaster-tesseract (Tesseract).

The presets and recipes The blocks Family Block What it does Readers ImageFolderReader Reads one page per image file of a folder or bucket. Readers ImageParquetReader Reads one page per row of Parquet files with an image column. Readers ManifestReader Reads one page per image of each item's manifest: IIIF Presentation 2 or 3, or METS with MODS (also inside an OAI-PMH response). Readers PageRecordReader Reads the page records an earlier run wrote (JSON Lines or Parquet), so a pipeline can add one more part. Readers PdfReader Reads one item per PDF file, one page per PDF page in order, each rendered to a lossless WebP image. Layout LayoutDetector Detects the layout regions of every page, with their labels and reading order, by a layout engine. Lines LineAssigner Assigns the lines detected on the whole page to the layout regions and orders them row by row. Lines LineDetector Detects the text lines of every page, with their geometry, by a line detection engine. Recognition FormulaRecognizer Recognizes every formula region as LaTeX by a formula engine. Recognition LineRecognizer Recognizes the text of every line by a line recognition engine. Recognition PageRecognizer Recognizes every page with a chat VLM or a page engine, whose output becomes the page's transcription. Recognition RegionRecognizer Recognizes each layout region of every page with a chat VLM, one request per region crop. Recognition TableRecognizer Recognizes the structure of every table region by a table engine. Conversion ImageConverter Converts each page's delivered image into the working image with an image engine and writes it. Conversion ImageFetcher Loads each page's image again from its address, for the blocks that need pixels. Conversion TranscriptionConverter Reads the transcription file that comes with each page (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or plain text) into a named transcription. Text CharacterNormalizer Normalizes the texts of every line, paragraph and table cell by a normalization engine, next to the text as written. Text UnicodeNormalizer Normalizes the as-written text of every line and word to one Unicode normalization form, NFC by default. Composition Composer Composes the DoclingDocument of a page or an item by a composition engine. Composition Recomposer Recomposes the running text of a page or an item into paragraphs by a recomposition engine. Composition Typographer Determines the typographic hierarchy of every page by a typography engine. Binding Binder Binds each item's page records, in order, into one item record. Binding Splitter Splits each item record into its page records again, in the item's order, with what the item-level blocks added. Validation PageValidator Marks the page records that do not validate against Page or lack a required part with an error each. Validation RecipeStamper Stamps the recipe edition a run follows on every step of every transcription, of a page or of each page of an item record. Servers ChatModelServer Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine. Servers ModelServer Starts linecaster serve inside the task for its served model blocks, through saturate's Engine. Servers ServiceServer Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through. Writers ImageFilesWriter Writes each page's image bytes as they came, one file per page. Writers ItemDocumentWriter Writes the document of each item record, one file per format: Markdown, text, HTML, DocLang, JSON. Writers ItemTextWriter Writes the text variants of each item record as JSON Lines or as files. Writers PageFileWriter Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON and more. Writers PageJsonlWriter Writes the page records as JSON Lines, one file per task, or into item shards for a later stage. Writers PageParquetWriter Writes the page records as Parquet, one file per task. Writers RejectWriter Writes every page that carries errors to the task's rejects file and passes every page on. Composites ModularTranscriber Reads a page's lines the modular way: layout, lines on the whole page, line assignment, line recognition.

docs.title: 🛠️ Development
docs.text:
To Run or write test the core uv run pytest (GPU and network tests skip where those are missing) test an engine package uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests regenerate the docs uv run linecaster docs (--check in CI) check released catalog editions uv run linecaster catalog verify build the docs site uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict add a model linecaster catalog pin <id> --hf <repo>, a preset in presets/<step>/, linecaster catalog release <id> add an engine a package under engines/ that imports only linecaster.data and linecaster.engines.api; test it with linecaster.testing.check_engine add a block a PageBlock with process_page(doc, page) and a contract(); test it with linecaster.testing.check_block

The code lives in src/linecaster/, the catalog in src/linecaster/catalog/data/, the engine packages in engines/, the pipeline scripts in pipelines/. Measurements and decisions are in NOTES.md.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to linecaster. The format follows Keep a Changelog; each release lists upgrade notes first, then additions, changes, deprecations, removals and fixes. Versions follow the tags; the first is v0.1.0.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• pipeline_sha256 leaves an in-process engine's endpoint and timeout options out (ENGINE_OPERATIONAL: where its service is). A derivative's run whose engine has an option of either name gets another hash: a resume into its folder needs --new-pipeline. No released recipe is affected.
  • linecaster.testing.check_engine calls a page engine (recognition, unit page) with an empty transcription (no regions, no lines), not the sample layout's regions.
  • --rate-limit holds per worker (process), not per task: the tasks a worker runs one after the other share one fetcher and its limits (HTTPFetcher.shared), where each task started its limits afresh. A server sees the workers running at once times the limits, as before; the run now states it before it starts (run.rate_note).
  • --tasks and --workers default to an automatic choice (linecaster.runtime.run.allocate): a pipeline without engines (pipelines/harvest.py) runs tasks of about 1,000 pages (or 5 items) from its input, one worker with --rate-limit, one per CPU without; a pipeline with engines keeps one task, every task at once. Resuming a run started with the old default (--tasks 1) needs --tasks 1.
  • http(s) requests have a deadline per attempt (HTTP_DEFAULTS: pybookget's attempt_timeout=15 and attempt_min_rate=50_000, i.e. 15 s plus 1 s per 50 kB of Content-Length, counted after the rate limits): an attempt past it is cut and retried. A server that needs longer for a response without Content-Length needs http={"attempt_timeout": None} (or a longer one). linecaster pins pybookget bf8eee1, which has the setting.
  • --prefetch and the readers' prefetch= argument are gone: ManifestReader and ImageParquetReader request http(s):// pages ahead in a window that sizes itself; drop the option. linecaster.net.prefetched takes (entries, submit, cancel, future=, fetcher=).
  • ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader item tables divide rows, not files, over the tasks; ImageParquetReader no longer splits a task's rows by datatrove's ParquetReader.read_files_shard, so limit and skip apply before anything is fetched, and no Parquet file is a PipelineConfigError (was datatrove's RuntimeError). A table no longer needs splitting into one file per task.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Nothing to size for a harvest: pipelines/harvest.py --parquet TABLE ... OUT --rate-limit 150/60 reads any page table as it is, in tasks of about 1,000 pages, with one worker that keeps the rate limits busy. linecaster.blocks.readers.tables divides Parquet tables over tasks by rows in equal shards (by row group); ImageParquetReader.auto_tasks() and ManifestReader.auto_tasks() suggest a task count from the input.
  • ImageParquetReader requests http(s):// images ahead, pages in the rows' order. linecaster.net.prefetched, the window both readers use, grows while the first request is out and none waits for the rate limits (HTTPFetcher.waiting), up to MAX_AHEAD, so one task keeps any rate limit busy.
  • HTTPFetcher.shared(**config): one fetcher per process and configuration, which the readers use, so the rate limits (and the window learned) hold across the tasks a worker runs one after the other; close_shared().
  • --parquet takes one .parquet file as well as a folder.
  • pipelines/harvest.py runs one item per task (task_per_item of ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader): every item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item. Items are grouped by their --item-key value, so a table whose item rows are apart still gives one task per item (tables.item_runs). Other pipelines keep their task sizes. A harvest run folder started with the 1,000-page tasks has another task count: run into a new folder.
  • A resumed harvest does not fetch images again that an earlier launch wrote: ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader take reuse_folder (harvest.py: OUT/images), list an item's folder once when they reach it (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing.ExistingImages; names and sizes) and read a page whose file is there from the storage instead of fetching it from the source. Only pages of items whose task was interrupted are read back (with one item per task, at most one item per worker and restart), so storage egress stays small. Its record is complete (sha256, width, height) and says image.extra.reused; ImageFilesWriter leaves the file as it is; the reader counts it in pages, media_size (the bytes it read) and reused; the console counts it as done, apart from the downloads and their rate. Not with --existing-ocr. ImageFilesWriter writes local files as <name>.part and renames them when whole.
  • The console's size on a restart starts with the finished tasks' images: their readers' media_size from datatrove's stats files (linecaster.runtime.local.size_before), read in batches in the background while the run starts (size … until then).
  • --proxies FILE: http(s) requests through a list of proxies (one per line: a URL, or host:port[:user:pass] as Webshare lists them), with resilient-httpx (the extra resilient-httpx): each attempt through the next proxy, a proxy that fails an attempt left out for an hour (PROXY_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD 1, PROXY_BLACKLIST_TTL 3600 s), the attempt retried through another. Each proxy's client is pybookget's, so the rate limits (shared by all proxies), the deadline per attempt and the trace records hold as without; retries follow pybookget's counts and waits, without Retry-After. The progress line shows the proxies in rotation; credentials are never logged, and the run record keeps the file's name, not its lines.
  • --user-agent TEXT and --random-user-agent (a random browser User-Agent from pybookget's fake-useragent, a new one for each task, HTTPFetcher.new_user_agent) for every http(s) request. The default User-Agent is datatrove's, HF-Research/1.0 (linecaster.net.http.USER_AGENT), where it was linecaster (+https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster).
  • The console of a local run (linecaster.runtime.console, linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor): one line naming the pipeline, a live progress line for the whole run (pages of the total, rate, size, failed pages, task, time left), a line per finished task and a summary, in human units; a progress log line every 30 s off a terminal. datatrove's pipeline listing (with the builder's boundary steps) and stats blocks go only to the task logs. The completion markers are listed once per launch instead of looked up task by task. With several workers the worker processes report their counts to the console (a multiprocess manager's dict), and every worker's task lines show. On a terminal the progress line is pinned to the top row and everything else scrolls below it (a scroll region, console.Pinned), so log lines and output from worker processes or libraries never break it.
  • ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader pass pages on as their http(s) requests finish, not in row order, so a slow or retried request delays only its own page (prefetched(..., ordered=False)); pages read without a request keep their order. Requests in flight are capped at the rate limits times the deadline per attempt (HTTPFetcher.max_ahead). In a 2,000-page LoC smoke run the oldest request, being retried, held the window full of finished pages for minutes (94 pages/min against 150).
  • Fetch records and traces carry each attempt's outcome (tries, the span attribute http.tries): a status for a response read whole, <status>-cut for one the deadline cut, no-response for a timeout or a connection error.
  • --max-pages N (--parquet, IMAGES; max_pages of ImageParquetReader and ImageFolderReader): the first N pages of the input for the whole run, in the same automatic tasks, so a smoke test is the real setup stopped early (--limit counts per task).

  • A response that trickles no longer holds a task: the deadline per attempt (above) cuts it and fetches it again, usually through another proxy exit. In a LoC smoke run one such response took 150 s while the 199 pages behind it waited; the trace shows a cut attempt as http.attempts 2.

  • The four BHL OCR board models the catalog lacked, as the board's drivers run them, each run on the board's 60-page sample (NOTES.md): model entries surya-ocr-2.5, indra-ocr, oxr-1.0, falcon-ocr (Falcon OCR pinned at the revision its vendor image ships) and their presets surya-ocr-2.5@1, indra-ocr@1, oxr-1.0@1, falcon-ocr@1 (step recognition, unit page), with evidence records where they ran.

  • Page engines: PageRecognizer runs an engine whose unit is the page on the InProcess or Served backend (or a page engine's preset by name), besides a chat VLM on Chat. Engine packages linecaster-indra (indra.recognition.v1: the indra-ocr package on the CPU), linecaster-surya (surya.recognition.v1: the surya-ocr package's full-page path attached to vLLM) and linecaster-services (falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1: clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's page pipelines behind their own HTTP APIs).
  • ServiceServer (servers): starts the service a page preset's serve block names, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the fetched model pin, or a vendor image's entrypoint (serve.server: vendor with command, health, weights_dir, new optional fields of the preset schema), ready once its health URLs answer.
  • pipelines/transcribe_page.py (transcribe_page.v1): a page engine per page, with the service its preset names unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one; launch.py runs a page engine's preset there.
  • linecaster.testing: FakePageEngine (fake.recognition.page.v1) and fake_service(), an HTTP service on loopback answering given routes. tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py checks the page engines in the environment of pipelines/transcribe_page.py.
  • Versioned docs: the docs workflow publishes the site with mike to the gh-pages branch, served by GitHub Pages: every release tag as version <major>.<minor> (latest the newest release, the default), every push to main as dev; mike joins the dependency group docs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The rate limits started afresh with every task (each made its own fetcher), so a worker's next task could send a whole window's requests at once; and ImageParquetReader never closed its fetcher, leaving a thread per task. The readers share one fetcher per process and configuration (HTTPFetcher.shared).
  • ImageParquetReader: an image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after the retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) no longer fails the task. The page comes without image and with the error in doc.metadata["errors"] (field image, raw_value its URI), so the page records and rejects keep it and a rerun of the task does not fail on the same dead link again; the reader has an error budget (max_page_errors, set by --max-page-errors), so a server that is down still fails the task. ImageFilesWriter passes a page that carries errors and no image through without writing a file. A row with neither image bytes nor a path still fails the task.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
The first release, after the refactoring of November 2026 in six phases; each phase's renames are listed here, and all of them in one table at the end of these notes. There are no compatibility aliases: old imports, flags and ids fail.

Phase 1: layout and names

  • Packages: linecaster.transcription, linecaster.page → linecaster.data (data model) and linecaster.formats (ALTO, PAGE, hOCR; formats.docling was linecaster.document); text.py, unicode.py, reflow.py, retyper.py → linecaster.text.variants, .unicode, .recomposition, .typography; images.py, plots.py → linecaster.images; run, jobs, ray_executor, provenance → linecaster.runtime.* (run.rows() → run.pages()); linecaster.models → linecaster.adapters; blocks/http.py → linecaster.net; blocks by family under linecaster.blocks.<family> (old modules filters, media, models, serve, texts, document, readers, writers are gone); specs/ → docs/reference/.
  • Blocks: PageStep → PageBlock, ModelStep → ModelBlock, WorkingImages → ImageConverter, AttachImage → ImageFetcher, LayoutStep → LayoutDetector, LinesStep → LineDetector, AssignLinesToRegions → LineAssigner, RecognitionStep → LineRecognizer, ChatRegionStep → RegionRecognizer, ChatPageStep → PageRecognizer, TablesStep → TableRecognizer, FormulasStep → FormulaRecognizer, NormalizeUnicode → UnicodeNormalizer, Typography → Typographer, ComposePage → Composer, ValidatePages → PageValidator, RejectSink → RejectWriter, RecipeStamp → RecipeStamper, ServeModels → ModelServer, ServeChatModel → ChatModelServer, PageRowReader → PageRecordReader; writers: PageFilesWriter + PageExportsWriter → PageFileWriter (text_fallback=False is the old PageExportsWriter), ItemExportsWriter → ItemDocumentWriter, ItemTextJsonlWriter + ItemTextFilesWriter → ItemTextWriter(format=...). Datatrove display names changed with them (stats and logs).
  • Engines: …Model → …Engine (KrakenRecognitionEngine, PaddleLayoutEngine, ...); ids unchanged. Adapters: ChatModel → ChatAdapter, each VLM adapter X → XAdapter.
  • Pipeline scripts: transcribe_chain.py → transcribe_modular.py; ids chain.v1 → transcribe_modular.v1, vlm.v1 → transcribe_vlm.v1, new harvest.v1, bind.v1.
  • Flags: --recognizer → --recognition; --vlm, --vlm-endpoint → --recognition, --recognition-endpoint; --texts → --item-texts; --exports DIR → --files DIR --formats md,txt,json --naming squiddleocr --furniture; --rows → --pages.
  • Stored output: the default transcription ocr → ocr_new; page records in OUT/rows/ → OUT/pages/; item text fidelity normalised → normalized; typography measurement levelled → leveled. Page records written before phase 1 keep ocr; read them with transcription="ocr".
  • Catalog: no step page (page presets are step recognition, unit page, under presets/recognition/); entries are <id>.yaml with prose in <id>.md; YAML is read as YAML 1.2 with ruamel.yaml (replaces PyYAML); lock format linecaster.lock/2. Edition numbers are unchanged; 20 hashes were recomputed (the page presets and squiddle@1), so files stamped by a recipe carry the new hash; old hashes still resolve (previous_sha256).
  • American spelling throughout (e.g. normalize, NORMALIZE_MAP, quantize_confidence, COLORS).

Phase 2: contracts and the builder

  • Pipeline scripts check their pipeline before they launch: a pipeline whose contracts do not fit exits with code 2 and lists every problem. Own blocks without a contract() pass unchecked.
  • With --tasks over 1, a binder after the page blocks (--item-texts) cuts the run into two stages: page records in item shards (OUT/pages/<shard>/), then the item stage; their logs are OUT/logs/pages/ and OUT/logs/items/. One stage logs to OUT/logs/ as before.
  • --dry-run prints the plan under plan and the Mermaid graph after the JSON.
  • A page an in-process block fails on no longer fails the task: it carries the error (doc.metadata["errors"]: block, step, preset, type, error; served failures in the same shape, no longer {step, error}), later model blocks pass it on at once, and it is written to OUT/rejects/<rank>.jsonl and kept in the page records. More failures than --max-page-errors (1 % of a task's pages, counting at least 100) fail the task.
  • ImageConverter(output_folder, rejects_folder, ...) → ImageConverter(output_folder, ...) and PageValidator(rejects_folder, required, prefix) → PageValidator(required): they record why on the page and pass it on (no longer dropped); the RejectWriter (now a writer block, RejectWriter(output_folder, prefix=""), which the builder puts before the first writer of a run) writes the rejects. A derivative that used either adds a RejectWriter where it wants the file, or lets the builder add one.
  • Library code raises linecaster.errors (PipelineConfigError, CatalogError, PageError, ServerError) instead of SystemExit, ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError and TypeError for configuration, catalog, page and server errors (e.g. an unknown preset is a CatalogError, an unknown block option a PipelineConfigError); pipeline scripts raise PipelineConfigError from pipeline().
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit) without a script raises; give the pipeline's script, runtime.jobs.ENGINE_SCRIPT (the modular pipeline's engines) or engines=False (linecaster alone).
  • The run record's schema is linecaster.run-record/1 (was linecaster.run/1): pipeline lists the stages with every block's to_dict() and contract (was a list of block entries; the separate stages is gone), and pipeline_sha256 is new. A run into an OUT whose record has another pipeline_sha256 (or none: a record from before) is refused unless --new-pipeline; another --tasks always is.
  • Page records carry schema: linecaster.page/1 in their row. Records without one (written before phase 1) are read with ocr as ocr_new, and a pages/ folder without records is read from its sibling rows/: no transcription="ocr" needed any more.
  • Engines load in warm_up() before the first page, not on it: a page's measured seconds no longer include loading; the load time is the block's warm_up_seconds stat. ModelServer and ChatModelServer start their servers in warm_up() (stat warm_up_seconds, was the boot time stat).
  • engine_spec(ref) and preset_models(models) take installed=True; tests that replace engine_spec accept it.
  • On HF Jobs the tasks log JSON lines (LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1, runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor; the run record's executor is JobsExecutor).
  • Every run is traced (OpenTelemetry, a new required dependency: opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http): OUT/traces/ appears in every run folder, and a sampled page's record carries metadata.trace_id. Every stage with a run folder now has observers, so its pipeline has boundary steps.
  • Observers: on_task_end(error=None) (was on_task_end(); an own observer adds the parameter), and new hooks on_task_event, on_leave, environment(). Stream blocks notify request (with a carrier) after prepare, and done with tokens and finish_reason; PageRecognizer notifies prepare once (was twice).

Phase 3: rule-based steps, recomposition, binding

  • Text without geometry (lines without boxes, e.g. a delivered plain text): a paragraph now continues across a page break only after a division mark; before, the simple line flow joined such pages whenever the text did not end a sentence.
  • linecaster.blocks.writers.item_texts(doc, variants, transcription, token_counter) renders an item record's text variants as datatrove documents, for derivatives writing them in a format of their own; ItemTextWriter uses it.
  • linecaster.catalog.schema.RULE_STEPS lists the rule-based steps, to tell a recipe's rule-based slots from its model slots.
  • Data model: ModelInfo → StepInfo (new field engine, the engine's code id, filled by the model blocks, linecaster serve and the chat adapters), Transcription.model → Transcription.steps, ChatAdapter.model_info() → step_info(). New: Transcription.paragraphs (Paragraph, ParagraphRow, ParagraphRef, Decision), Line.normalized, and the measurements vocabulary linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS (the keys a step writes; an engine package in this repository adds a new key there first, a test checks it).
  • Page records are linecaster.page/2 (steps instead of model, paragraphs, normalized). PageRecordReader reads linecaster.page/1 records and those from before phase 1 as /2; code that reads the JSON itself reads steps.
  • The page files' step records (ALTO processingStepSettings, PAGE Labels, hOCR linecaster-step-<n>, METS agents) carry engine for steps an engine ran.
  • Catalog: the steps image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition with built-in engines in linecaster.engines, in-process only (linecaster serve refuses them); presets may name by_script strategies; capabilities.unit may be item and produces names parts (PARTS). preset-1.json gains them; no released hash changes. engine_spec(ref, installed=True, served=False) and preset_models(models, installed=True, served=False): tests that replace engine_spec accept served.
  • regex is a new core dependency (Unicode scripts).
  • The rule-based blocks take a preset or an engine spec, with options over it: Typographer() → Typographer("ratios@1"); Composer(text="reflow", sections=..., rtl=...) → Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", options={"rtl": ...}) + Composer("docling-composition@1", options={"sections": ...}), and text="lines" is a Composer without a Recomposer before it (the document is composed from paragraphs when there are, else from lines); ImageConverter(output_folder, effort=80) → ImageConverter(output_folder, "working-image@1", options={"effort": 80}). New blocks Recomposer (composition, unit="page"|"item") and CharacterNormalizer (text); Composer also takes unit="item".
  • DocumentBuilder(name, text=..., sections=..., rtl=..., stats=...) → DocumentBuilder(name, sections=...): it no longer recomposes, it composes a page's paragraphs when it has them (add_page(..., page_id=...) names the page for paragraphs continued across pages); build_docling(...) loses text, rtl and stats; formats.docling.TEXT_MODES is gone. In linecaster.text.recomposition, join_paragraphs → join (the joined text, the separator and the decision on the division mark), new break_reason, kept_reason, mark_decision, Thresholds (the geometric thresholds and the convention marks, parameters of reflow_rows, Margins.of, continues, ...); Row.bbox may be None (text only). text.typography.retype takes ratios (Ratios) and records no step (the engine does); typography.SETTINGS is gone.
  • Page records and page files: with a recomposition (--recomposition, the squiddle recipe) the transcription carries its paragraphs (with their decisions); the typography step is recorded by its engine (name and engine typography.ratios.v1, preset ratios@1 and its hash, every option as settings, seconds and datetime), and the recomposition and composition steps have step records of their own. The documents and their exports are unchanged.
  • Binding: BindItem and ItemTexts are removed. BindItem(text="reflow", sections=S) → Binder() + Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", unit="item") + Composer("docling-composition@1", unit="item", options={"sections": S}) (text="lines": without the Recomposer); the item documents are the same, the item document's metadata is the item record plus docling, region_of, item_id (no page_ids, pages, text_mode, sections). ItemTexts(variants=V, token_counter=F) → Binder() + Recomposer(..., unit="item") + CharacterNormalizer("latin-historic@1", unit="item") + ItemTextWriter(DIR, variants=V, token_counter=F): the writer renders the variants from the item record (one row per item and variant, the same columns). ItemDocumentWriter gains by_format (<format>/<item>.<ext>).
  • The readable variants (readable_txt, readable_md) are made from the item's recomposition and normalization (Paragraph.normalized) instead of text.variants' own line flow, so they change (paragraph breaks, kept hyphens; NOTES.md has the comparison). linecaster.text.variants: join_lines, page_blocks, item_blocks, continues, HYPHENS and SENTENCE_END are gone; variants(pages, page_ids=None) needs recomposed, normalized pages; body_blocks and Block.normalized are new. The normalization engines also set each table cell's normalized.
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py: --text lines|reflow → the slots --typography, --recomposition, --normalization and --composition (presets; an empty slot leaves the step out: --text lines is no --recomposition). Without a recipe the rule-based steps run only when picked (before: typography and composition always). --item-texts needs --recomposition and --normalization (the recipe squiddle has them). --set takes the rule-based steps too (--set composition.sections=true).
  • pipelines/bind.py (bind.v1, now with recipes): Binder → item recomposition → normalization → item composition, texts in OUT/texts/<variant>/ (JSONL; --files also one file per item there, was OUT/files/<variant>/) and item documents in OUT/documents/<format>/; slots --recomposition, --normalization, --composition (the new recipe item-texts@1 fills them), --variants, --formats, --furniture, --dividers, --no-texts, --no-documents, --set.
  • squiddle@1 names the rule-based presets (ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1, latin-historic@1, docling-composition@1) instead of the option text: reflow: a catalog migration, so its hash changed (files stamped by it carry the new one) and the lock's previous_sha256 lists both earlier hashes (previous_sha256 may now be a list, oldest first; Resolved.previous_sha256 is a tuple).
  • The builder carries the parts across a binder and a splitter (an item record holds its pages), apart from image and the item's document; the role splitter is new. Recomposer's contract replaces paragraphs too (it makes them anew). RecipeStamper has unit any (it stamps the pages of item records).

Phase 4: backends and families

  • VLMs are the Chat backend (linecaster.backends.Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None, headers=None, prefer="page")): PageRecognizer(spec, Served(endpoint, model=name, max_window=W, ...)) → PageRecognizer(Chat(spec, endpoint, served_name=name, max_window=W, ...)), the same for RegionRecognizer(spec, backend, labels=..., pad=...) → RegionRecognizer(Chat(...), labels=..., pad=...); either also takes a chat preset's ref (PageRecognizer( "dots-ocr"): on the task's ChatModelServer, port 8000). The adapter is block.adapter (was block.spec), the served name Chat.served_name (was the Served backend's model). Without an endpoint Chat asks http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1. The page records are unchanged.
  • The run record: a chat block's parameters are backend ({"backend": "chat", "adapter", "preset", "preset_sha256", "model", "revision", "served_name", "endpoint", ...}) instead of spec and a served backend; pipeline_sha256 covers the adapter, preset edition and hash, model and revision (no longer the served name), so a run of transcribe_vlm.py into an OUT of before is refused unless --new-pipeline.
  • ModelBlock streams for every served block, and a block names its requests with _rows, _unit, _request, _parse and _done (an own served block that overrode _run_served or RegionRecognizer._run_regions uses them). Model blocks also take a preset ref as their backend (LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3@1"): in-process).
  • SingleRegionLayout is removed: SingleRegionLayout() → LayoutDetector("single-region@1") (the built-in engine layout.single-region.v1; label and region_id are its options). The region is the same; the page now records a layout step for it (engine, preset, settings, seconds, datetime), which page files list too, and the block reads the page image instead of the record's size. ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition) needs its layout: ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition, "single-region@1").
  • pipelines/transcribe_modular.py needs --layout like --lines and --recognition: a run without one is --layout single-region. Presets of built-in engines stay in-process with --backend served (runtime.run.engines), and the pipelines' serve leaves them out.
  • ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) only fetches the library's OCR, as a document media with metadata["format"] (alto, hocr); its contract adds transcription_file (a new page-level part) instead of ocr_original:*. The TranscriptionConverter reads it into ocr_original: the builder puts one right after such a reader when no block reads the file, and pipelines/harvest.py has its own, so OUT/ocr/ and the page records are as before. Its hash changes (a new block), so a harvest into an OUT of before needs --new-pipeline. A file that cannot be read is now the page's error (it goes to rejects/; before, the page went on without it and ocr_failed counted it); a failed download is still counted as ocr_failed. hOCR files that state another image size are scaled to the page image (before: read as they were).
  • PARTS gains transcription_file (no released hash changes).
  • A new extra, [pypdfium2], for the PdfReader; the locks list it.

Phase 5: docs

  • linecaster catalog docs [--out docs/catalog] [--readme README.md] → linecaster docs [--out docs] [--readme README.md] [--check]: --out is now the docs folder (the catalog's pages go to <out>/catalog/). It also writes the block pages, the README's block table (between <!-- blocks:start --> / <!-- blocks:end -->), the site's docs/index.md and docs/changelog.md, and docs/llms.txt / docs/llms-full.txt; --check writes nothing and exits with 1, naming each file that differs. linecaster catalog no longer has the action docs.
  • Generated pages start with a comment saying so; their links to files outside docs/ (sources, pipeline scripts, model cards) go to GitHub. The evidence tables have two more columns, Hardware and Backend.
  • A new dependency group, docs (MkDocs and Material), not an extra: uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict.
  • CLAUDE.md holds rules only; what it described is in docs/reference/architecture.md, the data model and serialization pages.

Phase 6: tests and engine hygiene

  • Contracts name the parts a block removes (Contract.removes, parts_removed; the run record's contracts and schemas/run-record-1.json have removes). ImageConverter without keep_bytes removes image: a pipeline in which a later block reads the image (without an ImageFetcher in between) no longer passes the builder's check; it failed on its first page before.
  • RegionRecognizer(pad=None): an explicit pad wins over the adapter's region_pad, which is the default (else 8). Callers that passed pad with a preset that has a region_pad (minicpm-ocr-1.0: 0, lightonocr-2-1b-regions: 8) now get their pad. The run record names pad: null when none is given, so pipeline_sha256 of a pipeline with a RegionRecognizer changes (no released recipe has one): resuming into an older run folder needs --new-pipeline.
  • Engine packages are version 0.1.0 and depend on linecaster>=0.0.1,<0.2; they import from linecaster only linecaster.data and linecaster.engines.api. A derivative's own engine package should do the same.
  • Tests: pytest runs with --strict-markers; tests/conftest.py's make_transcription is linecaster.testing.sample_transcription.

Every rename, old → new

Blocks

Old New Family Phase PageStep PageBlock base 1 ModelStep ModelBlock base 1 WorkingImages ImageConverter (preset working-image@1 in phase 3) conversion 1 AttachImage ImageFetcher conversion 1 LayoutStep LayoutDetector layout 1 SingleRegionLayout LayoutDetector with the engine layout.single-region.v1 layout 4 LinesStep LineDetector lines 1 AssignLinesToRegions LineAssigner lines 1 RecognitionStep LineRecognizer recognition 1 ChatRegionStep RegionRecognizer (backend chat in phase 4) recognition 1 ChatPageStep PageRecognizer (backend chat in phase 4) recognition 1 TablesStep TableRecognizer recognition 1 FormulasStep FormulaRecognizer recognition 1 — TranscriptionConverter conversion 4 NormalizeUnicode UnicodeNormalizer text 1 (inside text.py) CharacterNormalizer text 3 Typography Typographer composition 1 (inside document.py, text.py) Recomposer composition 3 ComposePage Composer composition 1 BindItem, ItemTexts Binder (+ Recomposer, Composer at the item level, + item writers) binding 3 — Splitter binding 3 ValidatePages PageValidator validation 1 RejectSink RejectWriter writers 1 RecipeStamp RecipeStamper validation 1 ServeModels ModelServer servers 1 ServeChatModel ChatModelServer servers 1 PageFilesWriter, PageExportsWriter PageFileWriter writers 1 ItemExportsWriter ItemDocumentWriter writers 1 ItemTextJsonlWriter, ItemTextFilesWriter ItemTextWriter writers 1 PageRowReader PageRecordReader readers 1 other readers, PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter, ImageFilesWriter unchanged readers, writers — ModularTranscriber (composite) composites 2 — PdfReader (skeleton) readers 4

Engines, adapters

Old New KrakenRecognitionModel, PaddleLayoutModel, PaddleLineModel, PaddleRecognitionModel, PaddleTableModel, PaddleFormulaModel, TesseractRecognitionModel …Engine (ids unchanged) linecaster.models linecaster.adapters ChatModel, ChatPreset ChatAdapter, ChatPreset ChandraOCR, DeepSeekOCR, Dots, … (ADAPTERS) …Adapter; ADAPTERS stays the one registry

Pipeline scripts, ids, slots, flags

Old New pipelines/transcribe_chain.py, id chain.v1 pipelines/transcribe_modular.py, id transcribe_modular.v1 pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py, id vlm.v1 id transcribe_vlm.v1; slot vlm → recognition pipelines/harvest.py, no id id harvest.v1 pipelines/bind.py, no id id bind.v1 --recognizer --recognition --vlm, --vlm-endpoint --recognition, --recognition-endpoint --text lines\|reflow --recomposition PRESET --texts DIR --item-texts DIR --files, --exports --files with every per-page format --rows DIR, OUT/rows/ --pages DIR, OUT/pages/

Catalog

Old New STEPS = layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, page layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition presets/page/ presets/recognition/ <id>.md with YAML front matter <id>.yaml + <id>.md models/<id>/model.md models/<id>/model.yaml + model.md catalog.lock lock format linecaster.lock/2 "component" (the umbrella word) "catalog entry" "catalog" "catalog"

Data model

Old New Phase ModelInfo StepInfo 3 Transcription.model Transcription.steps 3 — Transcription.paragraphs (Paragraph) 3 measurements (free keys) a fixed vocabulary 3 transcription name ocr ocr_new 1

Modules

Old New transcription/model.py, page.py, geometry/ data/transcription.py, data/page.py, data/geometry/ transcription/alto.py, pagexml.py, hocr.py, _xml.py, _provenance.py formats/ document.py (DoclingDocument building and exports) formats/docling.py (exports); the building moves to engines/composition.py (phase 3) text.py, unicode.py, reflow.py, retyper.py text/variants.py, text/unicode.py, text/recomposition.py, text/typography.py images.py, plots.py images/convert.py, images/plots.py blocks/*.py (17 flat modules) blocks/<family>/ blocks/http.py net/http.py backends/ backends/in_process.py, served.py, chat.py models/ adapters/ run.py, jobs.py, ray_executor.py, provenance.py runtime/ — engines/ (built-in), tracing/, testing/, runtime/builder.py specs/ docs/reference/ tests/test_*.py (flat) tests/ mirroring src/linecaster/

Terms in prose

Old New chain, the chain pipeline the modular pipeline (transcribe_modular) document assembly, reflow composition, recomposition text version text variant axes dimensions book (generic) item page row, record page record model (for a page preset, an engine class or an adapter) page preset, engine, adapter connector reader British spelling American spelling

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• linecaster.testing: sample pages (sample_page, sample_boxes, sample_png, sample_layout, sample_document, sample_documents, sample_transcription); fake CPU engines (FakeLayoutEngine, FakeLineEngine, FakeRecognitionEngine, FakeTableEngine, FakeFormulaEngine), registered as fake.<step>.v1 by register_fakes() (catalog.registry.REGISTERED); fake_chat_server() and completion(); the conformance checks check_engine and check_block (with transcription_changes and page_changes); the pytest markers and hooks (linecaster.testing.markers). Every built-in engine and every public block has a conformance test.
  • linecaster.engines.api: the Engine protocol, Capabilities, weights_of, hf_file, hf_snapshot, model_entry.
  • Markers gpu, network, slow, parity; gpu and network tests skip where the device or the network is missing.
  • Tests of each engine package in engines/<engine>/tests/ (conformance on the CPU, and on CUDA for kraken, and units), run with uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests; the engine READMEs give the install and test commands.
  • A missing engine's CatalogError names the engine package that provides it and the pipeline scripts that install it (catalog.code.install_hint).
  • The CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml (CPU, no secrets): uv sync --locked --all-extras, the tests without gpu, network and parity, linecaster docs --check, linecaster catalog verify, the strict site build.

  • tests/integration/ray_data_spike.py: the squiddle blocks through Ray Data (NOTES.md, 2026-11-06).

  • The block pages (docs/blocks/): an index by family and a page per block with its contract, backends, catalog step and presets, where it comes in a pipeline, the pipeline scripts that use it, its options, behavior and example, all from code; blocks whose constructor needs arguments declare docs_args for them.

  • The docstring standard (docs/reference/conventions.md, "Docstrings") and tests/test_docstrings.py: every public block, built-in engine, backend, serializer, build, run_pages, runtime.run.main and public catalog function has a summary line and Args: for its whole signature; examples for the serializers, build, main and the catalog functions.
  • docs/reference/architecture.md, docs/reference/compatibility.md (what counts as a breaking change), READMEs for the engine packages, and the docs site (mkdocs.yml).

  • Tests: the generated docs are current, and the README's "Your own pipeline" builds and checks.

  • The Chat backend (linecaster.backends.Chat) for PageRecognizer and RegionRecognizer.

  • TranscriptionConverter(format="auto"|"alto"|"page"|"hocr"|"text", source="media"|"uri", transcription="ocr_original", uri_key=None) (conversion): a library's own transcription delivered with the page, or named by a URI in its metadata, read at the page image's size.
  • The engine layout.single-region.v1 and its preset single-region@1.
  • IIIF Collections (a skeleton): ManifestReader reads a collection entry as its manifests, one item each, one level deep (a collection in a collection raises NotImplementedError), with pybookget's read_collection (a pybookget that has it).
  • PdfReader(data_folder, paths_file=None, glob_pattern="**/*.pdf", dpi=300, ...) (a skeleton, extra [pypdfium2]): one item per PDF, its pages rendered as lossless WebP; the text layer (text_layer=True) raises NotImplementedError.
  • Block contracts (contract(), Part, Contract, PARTS), the builder (linecaster.runtime.builder: build, Plan, checks, branches with when=/group=, composites, stages, run_pages), observers (linecaster.runtime.observers), the composite ModularTranscriber, the error classes (linecaster.errors), partial runs (--until, --after, --tap-after), --page IMAGE and linecaster page; docs/reference/pipelines.md.
  • docs/reference/glossary.md and docs/reference/conventions.md.
  • warm_up() on every block and backend, with the observers' on_warm_up(block, seconds); per-page failures, RejectWriter as a block, the error budget (--max-page-errors, build(max_page_errors=...)).
  • to_dict() on every block, backend and chat adapter; the run record's pydantic model (linecaster.runtime.record.RunRecord, schemas/run-record-1.json); provenance.functional_pipeline and pipeline_sha256; --new-pipeline.
  • The describe mode (runtime.run.describe_script, describe_recipe, load_script, parse); a recipe edition's expanded pipeline in the lock (pipeline, pipeline_sha256), checked by catalog verify; catalog release --migrate-pipeline. squiddle@1 has its pipeline recorded.
  • Secrets as references: linecaster.runtime.secrets.EnvVar; Served(api_key=..., headers=...).
  • linecaster.runtime.logs (JSON-lines task logs), runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor.
  • Tracing (linecaster.tracing, docs/reference/tracing.md): task spans, page traces sampled by page id (--trace-sample, build(trace_sample=...), default 0.01) plus every failed page, OUT/traces/<rank>.jsonl.gz (OTLP JSON lines) and OTLP/HTTP when the OTEL_* variables say so; served blocks send the page's traceparent in the request body and linecaster serve continues it (--traces FILE, LINECASTER_TRACES); ChatModelServer starts vLLM with --otlp-traces-endpoint when OTLP is configured; fetch spans from net.http.HTTPFetcher (fetch_record); trace_id and span_id on log records; linecaster traces OUT [--by block|preset|task] [--slowest N] [--json].
  • Rule-based engines (linecaster.engines): image.webp-lossless.v1, normalization.latin-historic.v1, typography.ratios.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1, composition.docling.v1, the engine protocol for page and item units, and dispatch by script (ScriptDispatch, linecaster.engines.scripts, normalization.by-script.v1, recomposition.by-script.v1, a preset's by_script); their pages in docs/catalog/engines/. Every threshold of the typography and the recomposition is an option (today's values the defaults). The recomposition makes Transcription.paragraphs with their rows and decisions (division marks removed and hyphens kept with the reason, paragraph breaks, continuations with their separator), continues paragraphs across regions and, recomposing an item, across pages (a page number between them does not close one), grows the item's lexicon page by page, and recomposes text-only transcriptions (a region one paragraph); CharacterNormalizer fills Paragraph.normalized too.
  • Presets of the rule-based steps, edition 1: working-image, latin-historic, ratios, unicode-recomposition, docling-composition; pipelines/transcribe_modular.py runs ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1 (with --text reflow) and docling-composition@1.
  • Item records in a stream (linecaster.blocks.base.item: doc.metadata["item"], the pages in order) for the item-unit Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer; Binder (pages → item records) and Splitter (item records → pages, with what the item-level steps added); the recipe item-texts@1 (bind.v1).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• PageRecordReader(fetch_images=True), ImageFetcher and ImageConverter dropped the fragment of page.image.uri and fetched the whole file: for a PdfReader page (file.pdf#page=n) the PDF, for an ImageParquetReader row with embedded bytes the Parquet file. A PDF page is now rendered as PdfReader renders it (at the record's metadata["pdf"]["dpi"]), a Parquet row's image read (columns id and image), and any other fragment is the page's error (field image), never the wrong bytes (linecaster.blocks.readers.fragments).
  • ImageConverter without keep_bytes declared only metadata replaced although the page leaves without its image bytes: its contract now removes image, so the builder no longer treats the image as available after it.
  • ImageFilesWriter rewrites page.image.uri and extra (to name the copy) without declaring it: its contract now replaces metadata.
  • RegionRecognizer replaces the transcription's earlier lines but declared lines only as added: its contract now replaces lines and text, so it may follow a line step.
  • RegionRecognizer ignored an explicit pad when the adapter has a region_pad.
  • RegionRecognizer failed the task on a page without image bytes; the page now carries the error (found by check_block).

  • PageValidator(required=("image",)) declared that it reads the image bytes, although it checks the page record's image entry: a page field is now read as metadata, so the validator may follow an ImageConverter that removes the bytes.

  • PageParquetWriter writes a fixed schema: datatrove took a file's columns from its first row, so a page's errors were dropped when the first page of a file had none. Page records in Parquet now always have an errors column (null without errors).

  • Tracing holds no page documents: a page a block drops no longer stays in memory, with its image, until the task ends; its trace ends when the next page enters that block.
  • A sampled page's metadata.trace_id is derived from the run and the page id, so a rerun of a run writes the same page records.
  • runtime.jobs.dependencies() reads the pipeline script and its lock as they are at the commit the Jobs install, not as the checkout holds them (with a warning when the commit is not in the checkout).

docs.title: Binder
docs.text:
Block · binding · linecaster.blocks.binding

Binds each item's page records, in order, into one item record.

Unit page → item Role binder Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in bind.v1, transcribe_modular.v1 Source binder.py

The comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description count_key str 'item_page_count' the page metadata key that holds the item's page count; a page without it waits for the end of the input.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The item record is one datatrove document (doc.id the item id, doc.metadata["item"], linecaster.blocks.base.item) holding its pages in order (Page.sequence, then page id); a page without an item is an item of its own. The item-unit blocks after it (Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer with unit="item") and the item writers read it; the Splitter turns it back into pages. It changes the stream's unit from pages to items and touches no part: the item record holds its pages as they came, every transcription with every part (the builder's checks carry them past the binder), but not the page images' bytes.

A task must see whole items: linecaster's run layout buckets page records by item (one item in one file), and the pages of an item must arrive in one task (with several tasks the builder cuts the pipeline here: the page records in item shards, then a stage over whole shards). An item is emitted once all its pages have arrived (when its pages' metadata give the count) or when the input ends (stat incomplete_items: items the input ended in before their count).

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    B["Binder"]
    r0["page stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["item stream"]

It changes the stream's unit from items to pages. The item's own parts (its document) stay with the item; the pages carry no image bytes (PageRecordReader fetches them again by URI). A stream entry that is no item record is counted (no_item) and not passed on.

Composes the DoclingDocument of a page or an item by a composition engine.

Each page's transcription records the step.

docs.title: ImageConverter
docs.text:
Block · conversion · linecaster.blocks.conversion

Converts each page's delivered image into the working image with an image engine and writes it.

Unit page Role transform Reads metadata Adds - Replaces metadata Removes image Backends in-process only (a built-in engine) Catalog step image Presets working-image@1 Comes after any reader Comes before - Used in - Source images.py

The contract is that of ImageConverter(output_folder='out/images', preset='working-image@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the working images go to. preset required the image preset (id@edition, e.g. working-image@1) or an engine spec (InProcess("module:Class", **options)). keep_bytes bool False the WebP replaces doc.media, so later blocks need not read it again (it then also replaces image); without it the page leaves with no image bytes. options dict \| None None engine options over the preset's (recorded as the backend's overrides).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: With working-image@1 (engine image.webp-lossless.v1, linecaster.images.convert.to_working_webp) the working image is 8-bit sRGB, lossless WebP at full resolution, method 0, exact. It is written to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id>.webp (_/<page_id>.webp for a page without item), and page.image becomes the working image's PageImage (size, hashes, decoder): it reads and replaces metadata, and with keep_bytes replaces image; without it, it removes image (the page leaves with no image bytes, so a later block that reads the image needs an ImageFetcher first). The delivered file is only read (from doc.media when the reader brought it, else from its URI); its location, format, sha256, size and mode stay under page.image.extra["original"], the step (engine, preset edition and hash, settings) under page.image.extra["step"] (a StepInfo: the image belongs to no transcription). A page without an image address, over the size limit (check_size) or that cannot be decoded keeps its image and carries the reason as an error (field image), so later model blocks pass it by and the RejectWriter writes it. The engine runs in the pipeline's process only.

docs.title: TranscriptionConverter
docs.text:
Block · conversion · linecaster.blocks.conversion

Reads the transcription file that comes with each page (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or plain text) into a named transcription.

Unit page Role transform Reads metadata, transcription_file Adds ocr_original:* Replaces - Comes after any reader Comes before - Used in harvest.v1 Source transcriptions.py

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description format str 'auto' auto (the media's metadata["format"], else told from the content), alto, page, hocr or text. source str 'media' media (the page's first document media with bytes) or uri (the file named by uri_key). transcription str 'ocr_original' the name of the transcription it fills. uri_key str \| None None the key of page.metadata that holds the file's URI (any fsspec path or URL), a dotted path into nested metadata; needed with source="uri" and only then.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The file is a document media of the page (source="media": what ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) brings, the part transcription_file) or is named by a URI in the page's metadata (source="uri"). It is read with linecaster's from_alto / from_page / from_hocr (or as lines of plain text) at the page image's size: ALTO is scaled to the image by its own page size, PAGE-XML and hOCR by the image size they state, when it differs. It adds whatever the file holds (<transcription>:*) and replaces whatever the page had under that name; the transcription's source records the format, the file's URI and the page image (hash and size). A file that cannot be read is the page's error; a page without one passes unchanged (pages_without_file). The builder puts one after a reader that brings transcription files when the pipeline has none.

Assigns the lines detected on the whole page to the layout regions and orders them row by row.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Each line goes to the region it overlaps most; lines outside every region (a page number the layout model missed, marginalia) become their own text regions (orphan_<n>), one per visual row, slotted into the reading order; duplicates are dropped. Afterwards the list order of lines is the order a recognizer follows (regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region), reading_order is the reading rank (regions by reading order, then rows), and line ids are <region id>_l<n>.

Reads lines and regions; adds line_regions; replaces regions (the orphan regions), reading_order and lines (ids and order). Lines inside skipped regions are dropped (stat lines_in_skipped_regions); stat orphan_rows counts the rows that became regions.

docs.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the Parquet files. paths_file DataFileLike \| None None datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. glob_pattern str \| None '**/*.parquet' datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. recursive bool True datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before anything is read or fetched. batch_size int 64 the rows read at once from a file. id_key str 'id' the column with the page id. A table without it names its pages <item>_<0001> from item_key and sequence_key, which it then needs. image_key str 'image' the column with the image. item_key str \| None None the column with the page's item_id; default: pages without item. sequence_key str \| None None the column with the page's position in its item (Page.sequence). image_folder DataFolderLike \| None None the folder relative image paths are read from; default data_folder. read_metadata bool False the other columns go into the page's metadata; without it only the named columns are read. file_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's ParquetReader arguments. default_metadata dict \| None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False read the files of a task's shard in random order. http dict \| None None pybookget Config fields (rate limits, retries) for http(s):// image paths. Their images are requested ahead of the page being given on, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), and pages go on as their images arrive: a slow request (one being retried) delays only its own page. Rows read without a request (bytes, files) keep their order. max_pages int \| None None only the first max_pages rows of the input, for the whole run: the tables are read as if they ended there, divided over the tasks (and auto_tasks counted) the same way; default: every row. task_per_item bool False the tasks divide the items (the item_key values, needs it; an item's rows need not be together), not the rows, and auto_tasks is one task per item: each item whole in its task, a task that fails costs one item (pipelines/harvest.py). Default: rows in equal shards. reuse_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing: one listing per item), so a resumed harvest does not fetch it again; its record is complete and says image.extra["reused"]. A copy that cannot be read is fetched from the source. Default: none.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The rows of all files, in order, are divided over the tasks in equal shards, read by row group (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables), so any table works with any number of tasks; an item's pages can land in two tasks where a shard ends. auto_tasks is the task count for shards of about PAGES_PER_TASK pages, which linecaster.runtime.run uses for a pipeline without engines. Each row adds image and metadata (the page record). The image column holds the image as Hugging Face's Image feature stores it ({"bytes", "path"}: the bytes when present, else the path), as plain bytes, or as a path: absolute (any fsspec URI, http(s):// through pybookget) or relative to image_folder. A row with neither bytes nor a path fails the task (a PageError: the table is wrong).

An image that cannot be read (an http(s) error after pybookget's retries, a missing file, bytes that are not an image) makes a page without image whose doc.metadata["errors"] says why (field image, raw_value the image's URI), so the task goes on: later model blocks pass the page by, ImageFilesWriter writes no file for it, and the page records and rejects keep it. More such pages than max_page_errors (a share of the task's pages, judged from page 100 on, ErrorBudget) fail the task, so a server that is down does not mark every page failed.

    B --> a0["image"]
    B --> a1["metadata"]

Reads one page per image of each item's manifest: IIIF Presentation 2 or 3, or METS with MODS (also inside an OAI-PMH response).

Unit page Role reader Reads - Adds image, metadata Replaces - Comes after - Comes before LayoutDetector, LineDetector, FormulaRecognizer, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, TableRecognizer, ImageConverter, ImageFetcher, TranscriptionConverter, ImageFilesWriter, ModularTranscriber Used in - Source manifests.py

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description data_folder DataFolderLike '.' the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) of the manifests or item tables, and the base of relative links; default the current folder. paths_file DataFileLike \| None None datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. glob_pattern str \| None None the entries to read; default **/*.{json,xml} (manifests), **/*.parquet with manifest_key. recursive bool True datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. limit int -1 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. skip int 0 pages per task, as datatrove's count documents; they apply before downloading. manifest_key str \| None None the column of an item table that holds each item's manifest link; default: the entries are manifests. item_key str \| None None the column of an item table that holds each item's id; needs manifest_key. Default: the id from the manifest entry. read_metadata bool True an item table's other columns go into the metadata of each of the item's pages. manifest_format str \| None None iiif or mets forces the format; default: pybookget tells them apart by content. item_id_pattern str \| None None a regular expression whose first group, found in the manifest entry, is the item id (instead of the last path segment); an entry it does not match is a PipelineConfigError. existing_ocr bool False also fetch each page's own OCR file (transcription_file). manifest_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where every manifest read is saved as fetched, <item_id>.json / .xml; default: not saved. http dict \| None None pybookget Config fields over linecaster.net.http.HTTP_DEFAULTS (rate_limits of this task, timeout, proxy, iiif_format, iiif_quality, mets_image_groups, ...). file_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. doc_progress bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. default_metadata dict \| None None goes into every page's metadata. shuffle_files bool False datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments. task_per_item bool False auto_tasks gives one task per item (pipelines/harvest.py); default about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task. reuse_folder DataFolderLike \| None None where ImageFilesWriter writes the images (pipelines/harvest.py: OUT/images): a page whose file is already there is read from it instead of from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing); the manifest is still read. Not with existing_ocr (its OCR files would need fetching anyway).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Entries:

  • without manifest_key: manifests: the files under data_folder matching glob_pattern, or the lines of paths_file (a manifest URL, or a path relative to data_folder), distributed over tasks in turn ([rank::world_size]) the way datatrove distributes files;
  • with manifest_key: Parquet item tables (the files matching glob_pattern, or a paths_file listing them), one item per row: its manifest link in manifest_key (a URL, an absolute fsspec path, or a path relative to data_folder), its id in item_key (optional), and, with read_metadata, every other column in the metadata of each of its pages. The rows of all tables, not the files, are divided over the tasks in equal shards (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables), so one table works with any number of tasks.

auto_tasks is the task count for about ITEMS_PER_TASK items per task, or one item per task with task_per_item (pipelines/harvest.py), which linecaster.runtime.run uses for a pipeline without engines.

A manifest is one entry, so an item's pages stay in one task (whole_items). An entry that is a IIIF Collection stands for its manifests, each an item named by its own link (a table's item_key does not apply to them); a collection listed in it, or a paged one, raises NotImplementedError (one level).

Each page adds image and metadata; with existing_ocr also transcription_file. Pages: item_id from item_key, else from the manifest entry (manifest_item_id: the last path segment that is not a generic manifest name); sequence the page's 1-based position among the manifest's pages with an image; page_id <item_id>_<sequence:04d>; image.uri the URL the image came from. metadata["manifest"] keeps the format, the manifest's URL, id, label, rights, required statement, identifiers and descriptive metadata, the page's own id and label, and the image request. Images are requested at full size (IIIF through the image service, iiif_format/iiif_quality in http; METS from the first image file group in mets_image_groups), with the fallback URL on 404.

With existing_ocr, a page's own OCR (ALTO or hOCR the manifest links: METS FULLTEXT, IIIF seeAlso / rendering) is fetched too, as a second media of the document (type document, metadata["format"] alto or hocr): a TranscriptionConverter after the reader reads it into the transcription ocr_original (the builder puts one there when the pipeline has none), and ImageFilesWriter(ocr_folder=...) writes the bytes.

A manifest that cannot be read or parsed, an image or OCR file that fails after pybookget's retries, or a response that is not an image is logged and counted (manifests_failed, pages_failed, pages_not_images, ocr_failed), and the task goes on. Needs the extra [pybookget].

Pages are requested ahead, across manifests, as many as keep the rate limits busy (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one HTTPFetcher.shared per process and configuration, so the rate limits hold across the tasks a worker runs one after the other; they go on as their images arrive, so a slow request delays only its own page (an item's pages can leave out of order; sequence keeps their place).

    r0["page stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["image"]
    B --> a1["metadata"]

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Each pipeline of a workflow reads the previous one's pages/ folder (linecaster's page writers) and adds its part. The records bring metadata and, with fetch_images, image: page records never carry the image bytes, so they are read again from page.image.uri through datatrove DataFolders (http(s):// through pybookget); a URI with a fragment names a part of its file (file.pdf#page=<n>: that page rendered, file.parquet#<page_id>: that row's image, linecaster.blocks.readers.fragments), and one that cannot be resolved is the page's error (field image, stat image_errors), never the whole file. A page's errors come back as doc.metadata["errors"], so later model blocks pass it by.

Rows of an earlier format are read as today's (upgrade, by the row's schema): rows without schema name linecaster's transcription ocr (read as ocr_new), linecaster.page/1 rows a transcription's steps model (read as steps); a folder .../pages that holds no records but has a sibling rows (the folder's earlier name) is read from there.

Files are distributed over tasks in turn. With item_shards the page records were written into item shards (PageJsonlWriter(item_shards=N)): the shard folders are distributed instead, each read whole, so a task sees every page of its items (whole_items). No shard folder is a PipelineConfigError.
