Unit page Role model Reads image Adds ocr_new:markdown, ocr_new:text Replaces - Backends chat (Chat), in-process (InProcess), served (Served), a preset ref (id@edition) builds one Catalog step recognition Presets chandra-ocr-2@1, deepseek-ocr@1, deepseek-ocr-2@1, dots-mocr@1, dots-ocr@1, glm-ocr@1, lightonocr-2-1b@1, lightonocr-3-0.8b@1, lightonocr-3-4b@1, nemotron-3.5-parse@1, olmocr-2-7b-1025-fp8@1, ovisocr2@1, ovisocr3@1, paddleocr-vl-1.6@1, qianfan-ocr@1, qwen3.5-9b@1, smoldocling-256m-preview@1, unlimited-ocr@1, unlimited-ocr-2@1 Comes after any reader Comes before CharacterNormalizer, UnicodeNormalizer, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_page.v1, transcribe_vlm.v1 Source chat.py

The contract is that of PageRecognizer(backend='lightonocr-2-1b@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat \| InProcess \| Served \| str required a Chat backend, an InProcess or Served backend of a page engine, or a preset's ref: a chat preset's (or a model's Hugging Face id: its page preset) for Chat on the task's ChatModelServer, a page engine's for its engine in the pipeline's process; a preset of another unit or any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription the completion becomes. primary str \| None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build requests ahead of admission (decode, resize and PNG-encode the image; Pillow releases the GIL). name str \| None None the block's name in stats and logs; None: "page (<model>, served <endpoint>)".

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: On the Chat backend (served only) a stream transform: one request per page, built by the preset's adapter from the page image, the completion parsed into a text-only transcription that replaces transcription. The completion is kept verbatim (extra["raw"]); its finish_reason and token counts go to extra and the step's measurements, and a completion cut off at max_tokens is counted (stat finish_length). On the InProcess or Served backend it runs a page engine (an engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: a vendor package, or a client of a vendor's service) as every model block runs its engine: the engine gets the page image and returns the page's transcription. Either way it reads the page image and adds text and what the preset produces (lines, markdown, html, ...); the StepInfo records the preset edition and its hash. A failed request or call is the page's error.

    r0["image"] --> B
    B --> a0["ocr_new:markdown"]
    B --> a1["ocr_new:text"]

from linecaster.backends import Chat

PageRecognizer("lightonocr-2-1b@1")

Unit page Role model Reads image, ocr_new:regions Adds ocr_new:html, ocr_new:latex, ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Replaces ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Backends chat (Chat), a preset ref (id@edition) builds one Catalog step recognition Presets lightonocr-2-1b-regions@1, minicpm-ocr-1.0@1 Comes after any reader, LayoutDetector, ModularTranscriber Comes before LineAssigner, LineRecognizer, CharacterNormalizer, UnicodeNormalizer, Composer, Recomposer, Typographer, ItemTextWriter, PageFileWriter Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source chat.py

The contract is that of RegionRecognizer(backend='minicpm-ocr-1.0@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description backend Chat \| str required a Chat backend, or a chat preset's ref (a model's Hugging Face id picks its region preset) for one on the task's ChatModelServer; any other backend is refused (PipelineConfigError). transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription it reads the regions of and adds the lines to. labels frozenset({'caption', 'code', 'footnote', 'list_item', 'page_footer', 'page_header', 'reference', 'section_header', 'table', 'text', 'title'}) the region labels it reads (default: text-like regions and tables, no pictures or formulas). pad int \| None None pixels around each region's box at the page scale; None: the adapter's region_pad, else 8. primary str \| None None the transcription whose text becomes the datatrove document's text; None: transcription. skip_on_error bool True pass pages that carry errors through unprocessed. prepare_workers int 4 threads that build the requests (crops, PNG encoding) ahead of admission.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: The same saturate machinery as PageRecognizer, results collected per page; any layout step can come before it. Reads the page image and regions; adds lines, text and what the preset produces, and replaces lines and text (the transcription's earlier lines, with their text, are replaced). Crops are cut at the scale the model expects for a whole page (the adapter's page_longest: the page is scaled so its longest side has that length, and the region is cut from it, pad px around the region's box at that scale), so a small region is not blown up; the adapter decides which regions it reads. Every read region gets one line: the region's box and polygon, the completion as its text (verbatim; extra keeps raw and finish_reason), in reading order; the transcription's earlier lines are replaced. The StepInfo records the preset edition, the settings with pad, page_scale and labels, and the token counts, regions and failed. A page whose regions all failed is the page's error, and so is a page without image bytes (stat errors); a page without readable regions passes through unchanged (stat pages_without_regions).

docs.title: ChatModelServer
docs.text:
Block · servers · linecaster.blocks.servers

Starts a chat VLM server (vLLM or SGLang) inside the task for its Chat backends, through saturate's Engine.

Unit any Role server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_vlm.v1 Source serve.py

The contract is that of ChatModelServer(spec='lightonocr-2-1b@1'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description spec required the chat preset's adapter (linecaster.adapters.chat_model) or the preset's ref (id@edition). port int 8000 the port the server listens on; Chat without an endpoint asks on 8000. host str '127.0.0.1' the address the server binds to; default loopback only. gpu_memory_utilization float \| None None the share of GPU memory the server may take (for SGLang --mem-fraction-static); default the preset's flags alone. The deployment's choice. extra_args list[str] \| None None more server flags, after the preset's. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on PATH, e.g. from the job image or a uv run --with vllm==... environment). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the server may take to answer. outside_venv bool False start the server without this interpreter's virtual environment (VIRTUAL_ENV unset, its bin taken off PATH), for a job image whose own Python has the server while the pipeline runs in a uv environment on top (HF Jobs); the server's helpers (ninja, python) then come from the image. python str 'python3' the Python that has SGLang (default python3, looked up on the server's PATH, then in the usual image locations).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The command comes from the chat preset's serve block (server, flags, environment, packages), whose server picks it:

  • "vllm": vllm serve <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT <spec.vllm_args(...)> (behind bash -c when the preset has a setup script);
  • "sglang": PYTHON -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <spec.model> --host HOST --port PORT --enable-metrics <spec.sglang_args(...)> (metrics on: saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges).

The server starts in warm_up() and is ready when it answers a trial chat request (saturate's alive-only gate); it stops when the task's pages are through. Before it starts, the preset's server_packages are installed into the server's Python (uv pip install --python <that Python> ...), and for a preset with revision_flag: false (the server cannot be given --revision and loads the default branch) the block refuses to start unless the default branch's files equal the pinned revision's (check_default_branch); the preset's server_env goes into the server's environment. With OTLP configured, vLLM traces too (tracing_args). A server that does not start fails the task (ServerError).

Its role is server and its unit any: it touches no part. Like ModelServer, it goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written.

    B["ChatModelServer"]
    r0["any stream"] --> B
    B --> a0["any stream"]

docs.title: ServiceServer
docs.text:
Block · servers · linecaster.blocks.servers

Starts the service a page engine's preset names inside the task, and stops it when the task's pages are through.

Unit any Role server Reads - Adds - Replaces - Comes after - Comes before - Used in transcribe_page.v1 Source service.py

The contract is that of ServiceServer(preset='falcon-ocr'); the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description preset str required the page preset whose serve block names the service (id or id@edition); a chat preset (ChatModelServer starts its server), or a preset without such a block, is refused (PipelineConfigError). port int 8000 the port vLLM listens on (server: vllm); a vendor's entrypoint uses the image's own ports. host str '127.0.0.1' the address vLLM binds to; default loopback only. vllm str 'vllm' the vLLM command (default vllm on the service's PATH: the job image's). boot_timeout int 1800 seconds the service may take until it is ready.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The preset's serve block says what runs:

  • server: vllm (an engine package that attaches to vLLM, e.g. surya-ocr): the model pin is fetched (every pinned file checked) and served from that folder, vllm serve <folder> --host HOST --port PORT <flags> --served-model-name <the model's Hugging Face id>, ready once /health and /v1/models answer 200;
  • server: vendor (a vendor's page pipeline in its own image, e.g. Falcon-OCR, OXR): with weights_dir the model pin is downloaded there first (every pinned file checked); then command, the image's entrypoint, starts the service, ready once every health URL has answered 200, in order.

The service runs in its own process group with the preset's env, without the pipeline's environment (PIPELINE_ENV, and this interpreter's bin off PATH), so the image's own Pythons and servers run as the image has them. A service that exits or is not ready within boot_timeout fails the task (ServerError). Its role is server and its unit any: it touches no part. It goes last in the pipeline (after the writer): datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the ports the image sets (one service per machine).

A local file appears only once it is whole (written as <name>.part, then renamed), so a reader never takes a half-written file for a done page.

docs.text:
Block · writers · linecaster.blocks.writers

Writes one file per page and format: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, text, Markdown, HTML, DocLang, JSON and more.

Unit page Role writer Reads ocr_new:lines, ocr_new:text Adds - Replaces - Comes after LineDetector, LineRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer, ModularTranscriber Comes before - Used in transcribe_modular.v1 Source files.py

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description output_folder DataFolderLike required the folder (local path, fsspec URI or DataFolder) the files go to. formats tuple[str, ...] ('hocr', 'alto', 'page', 'txt') the formats to write, keys of PAGE_FILE_EXTENSIONS; an unknown one is a PipelineConfigError. transcription str 'ocr_new' the transcription written. suffix str '' added to each file's stem, before the extension (squiddleocr's names use ".paddle"). furniture bool False keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html. bucket_by_item bool True one folder per item; False writes <page_id><suffix>.<ext> flat, as squiddleocr names its files. Pages without item_id are always written flat. detail str 'word' word (lines and words) or line (text per line) for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE. dividers bool False put --- between layout regions in md. text_fallback bool True a page without a document still gets md and txt from Transcription.text; False writes them only from a document (the block then reads document).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Files go to <output_folder>/<item_id>/<page_id><suffix>.<ext> (any fsspec folder: local, s3://, hf://buckets/...). It reads the parts its formats are written from (FORMAT_PARTS: lines for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, text for md and txt, document for HTML, DocLang and JSON, image for plots) and adds nothing; pages pass through, so writers can be chained. A page without the transcription is counted (no_transcription) and passed on.

  • hocr, alto, page: linecaster's serializers (to_hocr/to_alto/to_page) at the page image's size; detail="line" leaves the words out (text per line);
  • md, txt, html, doclang, json: the DoclingDocument's exports (linecaster.formats.docling.export) when the transcription has one (Composer); without one, md and txt fall back to Transcription.text (lines in reading order, tables as Markdown/HTML; counted as <format>_from_page_text) and the others are skipped (counted as no_document);
  • transcription: the Transcription itself as JSON;
  • plot: a JPEG of the page image with the regions and lines drawn in (linecaster.images.plots).

docs.text: The file is <output_folder>/<prefix><rank:05d>.jsonl, opened on the first reject (a task without rejects leaves no file), one line per error of doc.metadata["errors"]: key (the page id), field (else the step or block that failed), error, raw_value, and the entry's other keys (block, step, preset, type). Engine · recognition · package linecaster

Base class of a chat-VLM adapter. A subclass sets adapter (its registry name) and implements request; parse has a text-only default. Every value comes from the preset:

  • model / revision: the Hugging Face id and pinned commit; served_name: the name the server hosts it under (options.served_name, default the Hub id);

docs.title: composition.docling.v1
docs.text:
Engine · composition · package linecaster

Composes a page's DoclingDocument from its regions, paragraphs or lines, and tables.

The document is built by linecaster.formats.docling.DocumentBuilder: titles and section headers at their heading levels, text items with Docling's labels, page headers and footers in the furniture layer, tables with their cells, formulas, pictures with the text read inside them, optionally one section group per heading; the map of items to regions in extra["docling_region_of"]. A text region is composed from its paragraphs when a recomposition made them (one item per paragraph, continued paragraphs in one item), else from its lines as laid out (one item per region, one row per line: diplomatic composition).

The page unit is the call (the document in Transcription.docling); an item's document (all its pages, in order, paragraphs continued across pages) is item_document. Each call records a StepInfo.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:DoclingCompositionEngine Source composition.py Reads pages Produces document Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

Normalizes each run of a text by the strategy for its script.

A run is the characters of one script with the Common and Inherited ones after them; a script without a strategy of its own goes to the default strategy ("*"). A preset names the strategies in by_script.

docs.title: normalization.latin-historic.v1
docs.text:
Engine · normalization · package linecaster

Normalizes historic Latin print by the explicit mapping table of linecaster.text.variants.

Long s, ligatures, r rotunda and superscript e over a, o, u are folded; æ, œ, ø, å and ß stay; NFC, never NFKC; spelling is never modernized. Every recognized line, paragraph and table cell gets its normalized next to its text; the step records how many changed (changed).

Engine · tables · package linecaster-paddlex

linecaster engine for the tables step: the cell structure of every table region, with the region's recognized lines placed into the cells (needs the recognition step first). docs.title: recomposition.by-script.v1
docs.text:
Engine · recomposition · package linecaster

Recomposes an item with each decision at a row end made by the strategy for the script around it.

A decision (a division mark, the separator between two rows) goes to the strategy for the script of the characters before the row end, else after it; a script without a strategy of its own goes to the default strategy ("*"), which also recomposes the item. A preset names the strategies in by_script.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:ByScriptRecompositionEngine Source recomposition.py Reads items Produces paragraphs Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description strategies dict[str, Strategy] ISO 15924 script code, or * for every other script -> the strategy (a preset's by_script, resolved)

docs.title: recomposition.unicode.v1
docs.text:
Engine · recomposition · package linecaster

Recomposes the rows of each text region into paragraphs from geometry and Unicode's character properties.

squiddleocr's recomposition (linecaster.text.recomposition): the rows of each text region joined into paragraphs, the typesetter's division marks removed, from geometry and Unicode's character properties (line, word and sentence breaks), never from a language name; the document's own words decide the one ambiguous case (a hyphen that may belong to the word). A paragraph left open at the end of a text region continues in the next one, and at the foot of a page on the next page of the item (a region of digits only between them, a page number, does not close it); the pages of an item share the lexicon, growing page by page in order. Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph, decided by the character rules alone. Covers every script whose text runs in horizontal lines.

Each decision is recorded on its paragraph (Paragraph.decisions); a continuation links the two paragraphs (continues, continues_from) and removes the division mark it decided on from the first one's text.

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

Class linecaster.engines:UnicodeRecompositionEngine Source recomposition.py Reads items Produces paragraphs Scripts all Runs in the pipeline's process

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description rtl bool False the writing direction is right to left (start and end margins) convention_marks str '¬' characters a transcription convention writes for a line-end hyphen, besides Unicode's hyphens indent float 0.8 a row indented this many ems from the start margin starts a paragraph; a region whose first row is, continues none gap_leading float 0.6 a gap above a row larger than this share of the leading ... gap_height float 0.5 ... and than this share of the taller row's height is a blank line: a paragraph break short_row float 1.5 in justified text a row ending this many ems short of the end margin ... short_row_width float 0.25 ... and this share of the region's width ends its paragraph end_margin float 0.6 a row ending within this many ems of the end margin reaches it (justification; a paragraph that reaches it may run on) justified_rows int 3 a region of at least this many rows ... justified_share float 0.6 ... of which this share reach the end margin is justified

docs.title: typography.ratios.v1
docs.text:
Engine · typography · package linecaster

Determines a page's hierarchy from its type sizes, every rule a ratio to the page's own body type.

squiddleocr's retyper (linecaster.text.typography). Heading levels from the type size, section headers in body type made text, headlines split off the text region they were merged into, drop capitals joined to their line, uncertain page numbers removed. The rules cover every script that is set in lines of type sizes. Every threshold is an option, squiddleocr's values the defaults. The step records its counts (leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped).

Args: **options: the engine's options, the fields of its Options model (described there); a preset's options construct it.

docs.title: falcon-ocr
docs.text:
Model · Falcon OCR · Apache-2.0

Falcon OCR is TII's early-fusion vision-language model for document OCR (plain text, LaTeX for formulas, HTML for tables), a crop model by design: whole pages go through the vendor's pipeline service (a layout model, then one request per crop with a category prompt, and the vendor's Markdown assembly) in the vendor image ghcr.io/tiiuae/falcon-ocr. The image ships its own copy of the weights (/models/Falcon-OCR). This pin is the revision those files are: in the image the BHL OCR board ran (ghcr.io/tiiuae/falcon-ocr@sha256:2ec80252..., the preset's serve.image), every file of /models/Falcon-OCR has the git blob of this revision, model.safetensors its sha256 (checked 2026-11-06; NOTES.md). The repository's later revisions (Falcon OCR v1.5, 2026-09-11) have other weights. The card at this revision names no parameter count or language list (the newer card says 270M parameters). License: Apache-2.0 (the card's front matter; the repository has no license file). The upstream card is in upstream/177110bf36f6fd492428215baf76d0618854bed3/README.md.

docs.text:
Model · GLM-OCR · MIT

GLM-OCR is Z.ai's (zai-org) 0.9B OCR model for complex documents, on the GLM-V encoder-decoder architecture: a CogViT vision encoder, a light connector and a GLM-0.5B language decoder (arXiv 2603.10910). docs.title: kraken-ppocrv6-medium
docs.text:
Model · PP-OCRv6 (medium) · Apache-2.0

Benjamin Kiessling's PP-OCRv6 (medium) line recognizer for kraken (ALMAnaCH, Inria Paris), as mirrored byte for byte on the Hugging Face Hub by Small Models for GLAM; the canonical release is the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.21788410, which is provenance only: linecaster always downloads from the mirror (Zenodo throttles). License, languages (44 plus mul) and scripts are the card's.

The card describes the model as trained from scratch by kraken's author on line images of historical, contemporary and born-digital documents, handwritten and printed, on an architecture adapted from PaddlePaddle's PP-OCRv6 (128 px line height, uncapped line width, Adam+Muon); it is not a conversion of PaddleOCR's PP-OCRv6_medium_rec weights, so derived_from names only the mirror relation. kraken's own code runs it (kraken.recognition.v1), on torch; the model was trained in bf16-mixed, which is why linecaster's presets run it in bf16-mixed on CUDA.

Model · LightOnOCR-2-1B · Apache-2.0

LightOnOCR-2-1B is LightOn's end-to-end 1B vision-language OCR model (arXiv 2601.14251): it turns a page image into clean, naturally ordered text (with LaTeX for math) without a separate layout pipeline. docs.title: bind.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · bind.py

The item stage (binding): an item's pages (book, issue, manuscript) bound into one item record, recomposed as one (paragraphs continued across page breaks), normalized and composed into the item's document; one text per item and text variant, and the item document in each format. It reads the page records of a transcribe run; written in item shards (--item-shards N), each task reads whole shard folders, so it sees every page of its items. No engine or GPU is needed: the steps are rule-based, each a preset (--recipe item-texts fills them).

uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recipe item-texts
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recomposition unicode-recomposition --normalization latin-historic \
    --composition docling-composition
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT1 ... --tasks 4000 --item-shards 64
uv run pipelines/bind.py OUT1/pages OUT2 --recipe item-texts --tasks 64
... --set composition.sections=true          # an option over the preset's
... --no-documents                           # texts only (then --composition is not needed)
... --on hf-jobs --commit <sha> --flavor cpu-upgrade --tasks 64

Texts in OUT2/texts//.jsonl.gz (with --files also OUT2/texts//.txt|.md), item documents in OUT2/documents//.. linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares (IMAGES is the page records folder here).

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
Each slot takes a preset of that step; a recipe fills them all.

Slot Option recomposition --recomposition normalization --normalization composition --composition

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Besides the options every pipeline shares (linecaster.runtime.run).

Option Values Default Description --recomposition recomposition preset: the item's pages as running text, paragraphs continued across page breaks (e.g. unicode-recomposition) --normalization character normalization preset of the readable texts (e.g. latin-historic) --composition composition preset: the item's document (e.g. docling-composition) --set [] an engine option over the preset's, e.g. composition.sections=true; repeatable --variants 'verbatim_txt,readable_txt,readable_md' text variants, comma-separated: verbatim_txt, readable_txt, readable_md --files flag also one file per item and variant: OUT/texts// --no-texts flag no item texts --formats 'md,txt,json' item document formats, comma-separated: md, txt, html, doclang, json --furniture flag item documents: keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html --dividers flag item documents: --- between the items of consecutive layout regions in md --no-documents flag no item documents

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: • item-texts

docs.title: harvest.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · harvest.py

The harvest stage: items' page images (and, with --existing-ocr, the library's own OCR) from their manifests (IIIF or METS; a folder, a list of links, or item tables with --manifest-key), or from http(s) image URLs in a page table (--parquet), downloaded once into item folders, with page records that keep where everything came from. No engine or GPU is needed; the transcribe stage then reads the page records without waiting on the libraries' servers.

uv run pipelines/harvest.py --manifests items.parquet --manifest-key manifest_url --item-key item_id OUT \
    --rate-limit 5/1 --existing-ocr
uv run pipelines/harvest.py --parquet pages.parquet --item-key book --sequence-key page --image-key url OUT \
    --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1
uv run pipelines/harvest.py ... SMOKE --rate-limit 150/60 --rate-limit 3/1 --max-pages 2000     # a smoke test
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --pages OUT/pages OUT2 --recipe ...                 # keeps the metadata
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py OUT/images OUT2 --item-from-parent --recipe ...   # or the plain folder

OUT/images//. as the server sent them; with --existing-ocr OUT/ocr//.xml|.html; the manifests as fetched in OUT/manifests/.json|.xml; page records in OUT/pages/.jsonl.gz (image.uri the copy, image.extra.source_uri the source, metadata.manifest the item's and page's manifest data, the transcription ocr_original with the existing OCR).

Nothing needs sizing: --rate-limit holds per worker, and with it one worker runs the tasks (the run states what a server sees before it starts). Each item is a task (a --parquet page table with --item-key: a run of rows with the same item, whatever the files; --manifests: a manifest or a row of an item table; without --item-key tasks of about 1,000 pages), so an item is whole in its task and a rerun into the same OUT repeats at most the item each worker was in (datatrove's resume is per task); its pages whose images are already in OUT/images are read from there instead of fetched again (one listing of the item's folder; their records are complete and say image.extra.reused). The worker's requests ahead (manifests' pages and http(s) images alike) grow until the rate limits are kept busy, and the limits hold across its tasks. --tasks and --workers still override; with --workers N a server sees N times --rate-limit, so give each worker its part. --max-pages N runs the first N pages of the input in the same automatic tasks, a smoke test of the real setup (--limit counts per task, as in datatrove). linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares.

docs.title: transcribe_modular.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_modular.py

The modular pipeline: smaller models, picked step by step from the catalog's presets (linecaster models): a layout (a layout model, or single-region for the page as one region), text lines and a line recognizer, optionally table and formula models after; then Unicode NFC and the rule-based steps, each a preset too: typography (--typography), recomposition (--recomposition; without one the page stays as laid out) and page composition (--composition). Page records in OUT/pages; with --files per-page files in the --formats asked for (--naming squiddleocr: flat <page>.paddle.<ext>, as squiddleocr names them), with --item-texts one text per item in each text variant (an item stage: the item recomposed as one, normalized by --normalization).

uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout single-region --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --recipe squiddle     # every slot from the recipe
... --typography ratios --recomposition unicode-recomposition --composition docling-composition
... --item-texts OUT/texts --recomposition unicode-recomposition --normalization latin-historic
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
    --recognition tesseract-best-latin --tables slanet-plus --formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l
... --set recognition.batch_size=4          # an option over the preset's
... --set composition.sections=true         # also for the rule-based steps
... --backend served                        # a server in the task
... --files OUT/files --formats md,txt,json --naming squiddleocr --furniture    # squiddleocr's per-page files
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py serve --layout pp-doclayoutv3 ...    # linecaster serve with the presets named
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py ray start --head --num-gpus 8        # then --on ray --tasks 64
... --on hf-jobs --commit <sha> --tasks 64

linecaster.runtime.run has the options every pipeline shares; --recipe fills the slots.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
Each slot takes a preset of that step; a recipe fills them all.

Slot Option layout --layout lines --lines recognition --recognition tables --tables formulas --formulas typography --typography recomposition --recomposition normalization --normalization composition --composition

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Besides the options every pipeline shares (linecaster.runtime.run).

Option Values Default Description --layout layout preset (needed; single-region: the page is one region) --lines line detection preset (needed) --recognition line recognition preset (needed) --tables table preset (reads the layout's table regions) --formulas formula preset (reads the layout's formula regions; without, they are read as text) --typography typography preset: headings and their levels, initials (e.g. ratios) --recomposition recomposition preset: the text regions as running text, in paragraphs (e.g. unicode-recomposition; none: the page stays as laid out) --normalization character normalization preset of the readable item texts (--item-texts; e.g. latin-historic) --composition page composition preset: the page's document, for md, txt, html, doclang and json (e.g. docling-composition) --set [] an engine option over the preset's, e.g. recognition.batch_size=4; repeatable --files per-page files here, one per format (--formats, --naming) --formats 'hocr,alto,page,txt,md,json' --naming 'item' --files names: item, /.; squiddleocr, .paddle. in one folder --furniture flag --files: keep page headers and footers in md, txt and html (as squiddleocr does) --item-texts per-item texts: /.txt|.md and /.jsonl.gz (needs --recomposition and --normalization) --window int 32 pages in flight per served step --endpoint-for [] a different server for one step

docs.title: transcribe_page.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_page.py

A page engine reads the whole page (PageRecognizer on its engine): a vendor's package in the pipeline's process (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). Each task starts the service the preset names (ServiceServer, last in the pipeline: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint, or the vendor image's entrypoint) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running one. Page records in OUT/pages; the engine's raw output is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition indra-ocr --tasks 8 --workers 8   # CPU, in-process
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition surya-ocr-2.5        # needs `vllm` (0.25.1) on PATH
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition falcon-ocr           # inside the vendor's image
uv run pipelines/transcribe_page.py IMAGES OUT --recognition oxr-1.0 --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000

--recognition takes a page engine's preset (linecaster models; id or id@edition); chat presets run in pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py. A vendor's service runs inside the vendor's image (the preset's serve.image): the pipeline runs there too, in its own uv environment, and the service in the image's own environments (ServiceServer leaves the pipeline's out of its environment). Its entrypoint listens on the image's ports, so one task per machine starts it; more tasks share one service with --recognition-endpoint. On HF Jobs the Job's image is the preset's serve.image unless --image is given; it needs uv (the vLLM and OXR images have it, the Falcon-OCR image does not).

docs.title: transcribe_vlm.v1
docs.text:
Pipeline · transcribe_vlm.py

A vision-language model reads the page: the whole page (PageRecognizer) or, with a --layout preset, each region it finds (RegionRecognizer, a region preset), on the Chat backend. Each task starts vLLM or SGLang for the model itself (ChatModelServer, last in the pipeline) unless --recognition-endpoint names a running server; with --layout it also serves the layout model (--backend, --endpoint as for any engine). Page records in OUT/pages; the model's raw answer is in each page's transcription.

uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr                     # needs `vllm` on PATH
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --recognition dots-ocr --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py IMAGES OUT --on hf-jobs --commit <sha> --recognition unlimited-ocr-2

--recognition takes a chat preset of the catalog (linecaster models; id or id@edition) or a Hugging Face id (that model's page preset, with --layout its region preset where it has one). On HF Jobs the server runs in the Job's image: the one the preset was validated with (its serve.image) unless --image is given. It has uv, Python 3.12 and vllm on PATH, so the pipeline runs in the uv environment the executor builds (linecaster alone for page presets; with --layout also linecaster-paddlex for the layout model), and ChatModelServer starts the image's own server. SGLang presets and region reading start it outside that environment (outside_venv), so neither the image's Python nor its CUDA libraries see the pipeline's packages. vLLM takes --gpu-memory-utilization of the GPU (0.8, the board's value; SGLang: the preset's own share); with --layout the layout server loads into the rest after vLLM's memory profiling.

docs.title: docling-composition
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · composition · core

squiddleocr's document: a DoclingDocument per page or item, in reading order. Titles and section headers become headings at the typographer's levels, text regions text items with Docling's labels (from their paragraphs when a recomposition made them, else as laid out, one row per line), page headers and footers go into Docling's furniture layer, tables keep their cells and spans, formulas their LaTeX, pictures the text read inside them.

  • sections false: no section groups. With it, every heading opens a section that holds everything up to the next heading (JSON and DocLang gain the tree; Markdown and text read the same).

docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · image · core

docs.title: pp-doclayout-plus-l
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · layout · experimental

PP-StructureV3's layout model, squiddleocr's earlier default (until 2026-09-07) and its --layout-model PP-DocLayout_plus-L. It gives boxes only, no polygons and no order; the engine orders the regions with linecaster's XY-cut. Post-processing as PP-StructureV3 configures it, written out: per-class score thresholds (0.3 for paragraph titles and formulas, 0.4 for text, 0.45 for seals, 0.5 elsewhere), layout NMS, large box merging. On squiddleocr's test scans its regions matched PP-DocLayoutV3's on 5 of 7 pages; the differences were table boxes and one heading label.

Labels: PaddleX's labels are mapped to DoclingDocument labels as linecaster_paddlex.layout.LABEL_MAP does; number (a page number) is not in labels: because the engine places it by position: page_header when its center lies in the top header_zone (15 %) of the page, else page_footer. seal stays seal, which is not a DoclingDocument label (the serializers write it as a picture). Regions contained in another by more than max_containment (80 %) of their area are dropped.

docs.title: pp-doclayoutv3
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · layout · core

The squiddle combination's layout step: PP-DocLayoutV3 (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's layout model) on ONNX Runtime. It replaced PP-DocLayout_plus-L as squiddleocr's default on 2026-09-07 because it predicts region polygons and the reading order itself: PaddleX returns the boxes sorted by the model's order, so the list position is the reading order (furniture included) and no XY-cut is needed.

Post-processing as PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's pipeline configures it, written out here so the edition does not depend on code defaults: score threshold 0.3 for every class, PaddleX's layout NMS, and per-class box merging (large for chart, display and inline formula, doc and paragraph title: classes 3, 5, 6, 15 and 17 of the model's 25; union elsewhere). These are what PaddleLayoutEngine(model_name="PP-DocLayoutV3") uses by default.

Labels: PaddleX's labels are mapped to DoclingDocument labels as linecaster_paddlex.layout.LABEL_MAP does; number (a page number) is not in labels: because the engine places it by position: page_header when its center lies in the top header_zone (15 %) of the page, else page_footer. seal stays seal, which is not a DoclingDocument label (the serializers write it as a picture). Regions contained in another by more than max_containment (80 %) of their area are dropped.

docs.title: pp-ocrv6-medium-det
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · lines · core

PP-OCRv6 medium text-line detection on the whole page, on ONNX Runtime; the squiddle combination's line step. PP-OCRv6 medium replaced PP-OCRv5 server as squiddleocr's detector on 2026-09-07 (PaddleX's own OCR pipeline moved to it); its finer boxes let the table step fill header cells that v5's whole-row boxes left empty, at the price of some Fraktur lines split at wide gaps.

unclip_ratio 1.5, PaddleOCR's own default: squiddleocr went back to it from 2.0 on 2026-10-20 because the 2.0 default rested on two Fraktur pages and one CER lane, and wider boxes shrink the glyphs in the recognizer's input (Fraktur n and u merged on a display line), while tighter ones clip descenders. The rule since: no change of this parameter without a run over a few hundred BHL pages with the frozen scorer, both CER lanes. box_thresh 0.6 and thresh 0.3 are PaddleOCR's defaults; detection runs on the whole page (per_region off), and the lines are assigned to the layout regions afterwards (LineAssigner).

docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · normalization · core

Character normalization for historic print in Latin script, the mapping table of the readable item texts: long s to s, the ligatures (ﬀ, ﬁ, ﬂ, ﬃ, ﬄ, ﬅ, ﬆ) spelled out, r rotunda to r, a superscript e over a, o or u to the umlaut. æ, œ, ø, å and ß stay, the text stays NFC (never NFKC) and spelling is never modernized. docs.title: chandra-ocr-2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

chandra-ocr-2, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it: a port of the vendor's own vLLM client, chandra-ocr v0.2.0 (chandra/model/vllm.py: generate_vllm) with the ocr_layout prompt of the CLI. Where driver and vendor differ, the driver wins.

  • The page image, then the ocr_layout prompt (verbatim from chandra/prompts.py at v0.2.0, hash-checked as the driver does).
  • RGB, the vendor's scale_to_fit (pixel count clamped to 3072 x 2048 and up to 1792 x 28, both sides snapped to multiples of 28, LANCZOS), PNG.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 12384 (the vendor's MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS); the chat template opens an empty <think></think>, so thinking needs no switch.
  • One attempt per page: the vendor client retries a page up to six times at a raised temperature when it detects a repetition loop; the board does not, so a loop shows as a loop.
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 20480 (the board's correction of the vendor's 18000: 6144 visual tokens at the cap + 12384 + the prompt do not fit in 18000), the vendor's --mm-processor-kwargs pixel bounds and --dtype bfloat16, one image and no video per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching; no --trust-remote-code. vLLM 0.26.0 (the vendor's launcher pins 0.17.0).
  • The model answers with HTML layout blocks (<div data-bbox=.. data-label=..>), stored verbatim; the board converts them to Markdown with the vendor's parse_markdown in its harness. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.8 on an A10G, at most 12 pages in flight).

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0190 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0197 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

uv run launch.py chandra-ocr-2 IMAGES OUT

docs.title: deepseek-ocr-2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

DeepSeek-OCR-2 in grounded document mode, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's deepseek-ocr2-vllm.py; the DeepSeek-OCR and DeepSeek-OCR-2 drivers are twins and differ only in the checkpoint).

  • The prompt <|grounding|>Convert the document to markdown. as a text part after the image (the recipe's raw <image>\n<|grounding|>... prompt becomes image + text; the chat template inserts the image token).
  • No resolution mode is passed (no mm_processor_kwargs), so vLLM's default applies: Gundam (base 1024, tiles of 640, crop mode, up to 6 crops), the mode the card recommends for documents.
  • Full resolution, no resize: RGB PNG/JPEG bytes as they are, anything else RGB PNG.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 4096 (8192 context minus the image), skip_special_tokens false so the grounding tags survive.
  • The card's n-gram repetition guard: --logits_processors vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_ocr:NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor at boot (last on the command line: the flag takes a list) and vllm_xargs per request (the whitelist is <td>/</td> in v1's tokenizer; v2 uses v1's processor and whitelist, as the v2 vLLM recipe does; that the ids are the same tokens in v2's tokenizer is not verified).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 8192 (the native context), --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt.
  • The completion is stored verbatim, grounding markup included; the board's deepseek_strip_grounding (postproc 3) stays in its harness, linecaster.adapters.deepseek_ocr.strip_grounding is the same rule. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.8 on an A10G).

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0576 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0628 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: dots-mocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

dots.mocr in plain OCR mode, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's dots-mocr.py; where the two differ, the driver wins).

  • Plain OCR only: the prompt Extract the text content from this image.; plain text out, no layout JSON.
  • The image, then a text part that starts with vLLM's dots placeholder <|img|><|imgpad|><|endofimg|> followed by the prompt (upstream's dots_mocr/model/inference.py server client); with --chat-template-content-format string vLLM adds no placeholder of its own.
  • Full resolution, no resize: RGB PNG/JPEG bytes as they are, anything else RGB PNG (the processor clamps to its own max_pixels 11289600).
  • Sampling from upstream inference.py: temperature 0.1, top_p 0.9; max_tokens 16384 (the driver's: a full-size page is at most 14400 image tokens, 14400 + 16384 < 32768).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 32768 --trust-remote-code --chat-template-content-format string (the card's vllm serve line), no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt.
  • The completion is stored verbatim; the board's strip and empty-completion check stay in its harness. The board ran vLLM 0.26.0 (Daniel's recipe has moved to 0.29.0); --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.6 on an L40S, 4 pages in flight). Not yet run by linecaster: experimental.

docs.title: dots-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

dots.ocr in plain OCR mode, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's dots-ocr.py; where the two differ, the driver wins).

  • Plain OCR (--prompt-mode ocr): the prompt Extract the text content from this image.; the output is plain text, not layout JSON, so there is nothing to convert.
  • The image, then the prompt as a text part, with no image placeholder in the text (unlike dots.mocr) and no --chat-template-content-format.
  • Full resolution, no resize: RGB PNG/JPEG bytes as they are, anything else converted to RGB PNG.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 8192 (no top_p).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 32768 --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt.
  • The scored board row ran with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6, at most 4 pages in flight and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True on an A10G (0.8 and 12 in flight ran out of memory in the vision encoder): deployment choices, not part of the preset.

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0170 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0170 for the board's own outputs on the same pages. Greedy decoding with identical requests reproduces the board exactly.

docs.title: falcon-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Falcon-OCR's whole-page product, as the BHL OCR board's driver runs it: the vendor's pipeline service (layout detection, one request per crop with a category prompt, the vendor's Markdown assembly) in the vendor's image, one page per request to POST /falconocr/parse. The engine (falcon.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: ServiceServer starts the image's own single-GPU entrypoint (/app/entrypoint_single.sh: vLLM with the model on port 8000, the pipeline on 5002, both on GPU 0 of the container) and waits until both answer /health. The image's entrypoint binds both to every address of the container. The weights are the image's own (/models/Falcon-OCR, the model pin's files); the image digest fixes what runs.
  • The request: the page as RGB, scaled down (LANCZOS) so its longest side is at most 2,048 px, JPEG quality 95, as a data URI, with skip_layout false (the vendor's full-page path; the direct VLM path is off-label).
  • Kept verbatim: markdown_result (extra["raw"], the text) and the layout regions (json_result). The service reports no finish reason, so no loop can be counted; its output tokens are the step's completion_tokens. The board strips leaked >>UNUSED_N<< vocabulary tokens in its harness (falcon_strip_unused_tokens).
  • The image has Python 3.10 and no uv: on HF Jobs the pipeline cannot run inside it as it is (not tried).

Apache-2.0. Run on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "The four board models the catalog lacked"): CER reading 0.0775 for linecaster's run on an RTX A6000 against 0.1301 for the board's own outputs on the same pages (the Markdown identical on 47 of 60 pages; one page the board's run looped on carries the gap). Not run on HF Jobs.

Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

GLM-OCR, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's glm-ocr.py).

docs.title: indra-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Indra OCR, as the BHL OCR board's driver runs it: the indra-ocr package (1.1.2) on the CPU, in the pipeline's process, each page through the package's own image path (Converter.convert(path), the call the indra-ocr command makes), so decoding to grayscale, orientation, deskew, detection, recognition, layout and reading order are the package's. The engine is indra.recognition.v1 (package linecaster-indra).

  • Settings: indra_ocr.load()'s defaults, written out: mode auto (an image is OCR'd), furniture false (page headers and footers dropped from the Markdown), math false, dpi 200 (PDFs only), one ONNX Runtime thread per task (the package's own workers are single-threaded, one per core: run as many tasks as cores).
  • The models: the pin of datalab-to/indra-ocr at the tag v1.1.0, the model set indra-ocr 1.1.2 is built against (indra_ocr/models.py: HF_REVISION), every pinned file checked.
  • The page goes to the package as its file's bytes, as the reader brought them (the engine's image_input is bytes), the board driver's way; the package decodes it in grayscale with OpenCV. The pipeline script resolves OpenCV 4.11 (surya-ocr's pin, in the same environment); the board's run resolved the newest release of its day.
  • Kept verbatim: the package's Markdown (extra["raw"], the text), with its layout blocks, rotation and skew. A page the package reports as failed is the page's error; an empty Markdown (a blank leaf) is a transcription without text. The board strips the outer whitespace only.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page). Run on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "The four board models the catalog lacked"): CER reading 0.0489 for linecaster's run on spark's CPU, as for the board's own outputs on the same pages (the Markdown identical on 54 of 60 pages).

docs.title: kraken-ppocrv6-medium
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

kraken's PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer through kraken's own code (RecognitionTaskModel), on every line of the page in the line step's order; the squiddle combination's recognizer, which reproduces squiddleocr's goldens line for line (1,560/1,560 lines on sample-60, spark and forge).

  • batch_size 8: the batch size squiddleocr's goldens were recorded with. kraken pads a batch to its widest line, so the batch size can move numerics; one page per request, batching only within the page.
  • precision auto: bf16-mixed on CUDA (the model was trained in bf16-mixed; recognition about 1.6x faster on the GB10; 79 of 3,673 lines on 100 BHL pages read differently from 32-true), 32-true on the CPU. Needs the kraken fork with the inference autocast fix (storytracer/kraken 3d235ee8); on upstream kraken 7.1 the setting is inert. T4-class GPUs have no bf16 tensor cores: use 16-mixed or 32-true there (a new preset).
  • text_direction horizontal-lr; right-to-left material wants horizontal-rl.

docs.title: lightonocr-2-1b-regions
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

LightOnOCR-2-1B on layout regions (RegionRecognizer after a layout step): each region is cut from the page scaled to LightOnOCR's 1540-px page size, 8 px around its box at that scale, and sent as it is, with the page preset's request and sampling.

LightOnOCR-2 is trained on whole pages. On the 60-page sample with PP-DocLayoutV3 regions it loops to its token limit on part of the region crops (page headers, footers, footnotes), and reads worse than the page preset on whole pages (the evidence, from NOTES.md, "Region recognition with a page model"). Kept as an experimental way to read regions with a page model; region reading wants a region-trained model (minicpm-ocr-1.0).

LightOnOCR-3-0.8B on whole pages, as the BHL OCR board ran it (one driver for both LightOnOCR-3 rows, following the model card; the two presets differ only in the checkpoint).

  • The completion is stored verbatim; --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.8 on an A10G). Not yet run by linecaster: experimental.

docs.title: lightonocr-3-4b
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

LightOnOCR-3-4B on whole pages, as the BHL OCR board ran it (one driver for both LightOnOCR-3 rows, following the model card; the two presets differ only in the checkpoint).

  • The page image only, no text part (the card's transcription call; grounding is another output, not run).
  • RGB, thumbnail((2048, 2048)), PNG: the card's target longest dimension. thumbnail only downscales, so a smaller page is sent as it is (unlike LightOnOCR-2's forced 1540 px).
  • Sampling from the card: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 4096; thinking off per request and server-side (--default-chat-template-kwargs).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 16384 (the board's; a 2048-px page is at most 4096 image tokens), one image and no video per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching; no --trust-remote-code.
  • vLLM 0.30.0, not the board-wide 0.26.0: LightOn's repository says 0.27.1 makes these models loop. The HF Jobs image is therefore vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (the recipe ran these on 0.26.0 before the presets).
  • The completion is stored verbatim; --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.8 on an A10G). Not yet run by linecaster: experimental.

docs.title: minicpm-ocr-1.0
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 as a region reader, run the way OpenBMB's SDK (minicpm-ocr 1.0.1) runs it: the SDK finds PP-DocLayoutV3 regions, crops each one from the full-resolution page and sends the crop with the prompt for its region type. Here the layout comes from linecaster's layout step and RegionRecognizer sends the crops.

  • Prompt and token cap per region type from the SDK's DEFAULT_PROMPT_MAP["element_prompts"], looked up by the layout model's own label (PP-DocLayoutV3's class name, the SDK's vocabulary): Text Recognition: for text-like regions, Table Recognition: (8192 tokens), Formula Recognition: for display formulas, Chart to Table:, Seal Recognition:; unknown types get the SDK default (Text Recognition:, 8192). Caps are clamped to max-model-len - 512 as the SDK does (no effect at 40960).
  • Request: the crop, then the prompt; mm_processor_kwargs {"downsample_mode": "4x", "max_slice_nums": 9}; thinking off; temperature 0.01, top_p 0.001, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.0, no_repeat_ngram_size 100; PNG.
  • Every region is read but the image types (image, header_image, footer_image); charts and seals are read (the SDK's chart and seal recognition are on).
  • Crop: from the full-resolution page (no page scaling, no padding), the box truncated to whole pixels as PaddleX's CropByBoxes does, pixels outside the region's polygon white.
  • Serve flags from OpenBMB's SDK tutorial (as in the board job), served as minicpm-ocr; DSpark speculative decoding with the matching draft model (minicpm-ocr-1.0-dspark, 15 speculative tokens; mean acceptance length about 7 on forge; --no-speculative in the recipe turns it off).
  • vLLM nightly 5d35ce3 (0.32.1rc1.dev602+g5d35ce393) with transformers at OpenBMB's pin: on HF Jobs the board's MiniCPM-OCR image. ninja must be on PATH or the engine fails at startup.
  • linecaster.adapters.minicpm_ocr.assemble_markdown assembles the page with the SDK's own code (extra linecaster[minicpm-ocr]); the board row kept footnote and aside_text.

Measured against OpenBMB's SDK on the same server and pages (the evidence, from NOTES.md, "MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 through RegionRecognizer"). Not reproduced: the SDK's PaddleX box filtering (filter_overlap_boxes) and its merging of aligned text blocks into one composite crop (merge_blocks); linecaster's layout step runs PP-DocLayoutV3's ONNX export with its own containment suppression. Experimental: validated against the SDK, not the board.

docs.title: nemotron-3.5-parse
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Nemotron 3.5 Parse, as the BHL OCR board's driver and its plugin install script ran it, both following the model card (docs/serving.md, "Generation contract" and the H100 vllm serve block).

  • The control-token prompt </s><s><predict_bbox><predict_classes><output_markdown><predict_text_in_pic> as a text part FIRST, then the page image (the vendor client).
  • RGB at the original size, PNG (the server-side processor fits it to 2048 x 1664; a client-side resize would resample twice).
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, max_tokens 8744, skip_special_tokens false (the reply's coordinate and class tokens are kept).
  • Serve flags, the card's H100 block: --max-model-len 16384 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend uni --max-num-seqs 192 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, no prefix caching, one image per prompt, --attention-config '{"flash_attn_version": 3}'. FlashAttention 3 is a Hopper kernel: the board ran on an H200, and an Ada or Ampere GPU (L4, A10G) cannot run these flags as they are.
  • The architecture (RadioMBartPrefixForCausalLM) is not in vLLM 0.26.0's registry. NVIDIA serves it through a vLLM general plugin (nemotron-parse 3.5.0.post7) shipped in the model repo; the adapter's serve_setup installs it into the vLLM image's own Python before vllm serve, as the board's install script does (the package source and NVIDIA's inference constraints from the model repo at the pinned revision, the lock's own nemotron-parse line dropped; the install fails if vLLM moved off 0.26.0). The plugin's one-token MTP speculative decoding stays on, as on the board. The image is the board's vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0 by its amd64 digest.
  • The completion (coordinate tokens, <class_*> tokens and Markdown text) is stored verbatim; the board renders it with the vendor's render_markdown from the model repo in its harness (linecaster.adapters.nemotron_parse35.to_markdown reproduces it).

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0403 for linecaster's run on an H200 against 0.0454 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: olmocr-2-7b-1025-fp8
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

olmOCR-2-7B-1025-FP8, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's olmocr2-vllm.py; where the two differ, the driver wins).

  • The olmOCR no-anchoring (v4, YAML) prompt as a text part, THEN the page image (text before image, as the driver sends it).
  • PNG with the longest side forced to exactly 1288 px, up or down (the olmOCR pipeline's target_longest_image_dim), LANCZOS.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.1, max_tokens 8192, repetition_penalty 1.05, stop <|im_end|>, <|endoftext|> (the recipe's values, recorded in the driver).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 16384, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt; no --trust-remote-code. vLLM 0.26.0 (the board's; Daniel's recipe has since moved to 0.29.0).
  • The model answers with YAML front matter (primary_language, is_rotation_valid, rotation_correction, is_table, is_diagram) above the page text. The completion is stored verbatim and the front matter also parsed into extra["front_matter"]; dropping it from the scored text is the board's post-processing, left to the harness (linecaster.adapters.olmocr2.body gives the same split). Not yet run by linecaster: experimental.

docs.title: ovisocr2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

OvisOCR2, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's ovis-ocr2-server.py; where driver and recipe differ, the driver wins).

  • The page image, then the card's Markdown OCR prompt as a text part. OvisOCR2's prompt starts with a newline (the server recipe's).
  • RGB, downscaled with LANCZOS to at most 8,294,400 px (2880 x 2880, the processor's max_pixels) and never upscaled, then JPEG quality 95 (every image, also when it fits).
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 16384, thinking off per request.

docs.title: oxr-1.0
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

OXR-1.0's whole-page product, as the BHL OCR board's driver runs it: the vendor's all-in-one service (D-FINE layout, the OXR VLM per region and its reading order, the vendor's oxr API assembling the page), one page per request to POST /v1/parse/sync. The engine (oxr.recognition.v1, package linecaster-services) is its client in the pipeline's process.

  • The service: an image built unmodified from the vendor's docker/Dockerfile.allinone at github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR@c1a1dcb3 (on the vendor's pinned vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1; the vendor's plugin and entrypoint require vLLM 0.25.1 and Transformers 5.13.1), the board's image by digest. ServiceServer downloads the model pin to /models/oxr-model (every pinned file checked; the board's driver did the same rather than mount the weights) and starts the image's entrypoint, which serves vLLM on 8080 and the layout model on 8081 (loopback) and the API on 8000 (OXR_API_HOST 127.0.0.1); the API answers /docs once both model services are ready.
  • The request: the page as RGB, lossless PNG at its own size, as the multipart file, with api_key and one output_formats field each for markdown and json (httpx's encoding of a list, which the board's saturate 0.2.0 used). No feature_config or element_formats: the vendor's defaults (page headers and footers dropped, the overlap clean-up full_overlap_dedupe off).
  • Kept verbatim: the API's Markdown (extra["raw"], the text), its blocks (JSON) and warnings. An answer with a non-zero code is the page's error. The service reports no finish reason or token counts (its per-region cap is 8,192 tokens in the vendor's configuration). The board drops the figure crops' image links in its harness (oxr_drop_image_links).

License: the OXR License (Apache-2.0 with additional terms; see the model's page). Run on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "The four board models the catalog lacked"): CER reading 0.0380 on an RTX A6000; the board's own outputs for these pages are not published (its full-benchmark number is 0.1104). Not run on HF Jobs.

docs.title: paddlex-ppocrv6-medium
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

PaddleOCR's own PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer on PaddleX's ONNX Runtime engine. Lines are cut as PaddleX's OCR pipeline cuts them (minimum-area rectangle of the polygon, warped upright), sorted by aspect ratio and read batch_size 8 at a time, as PaddleX's pipeline does. Words: the text split at whitespace, placed along the line by the CTC columns of their characters (PaddleX's return_word_box); PaddleX gives no per-word confidence.

On the 60-page BHL sample (2026-11-03, evidence/) the same modular pipeline with kraken's port of the model family read better on every volume but one; the likely difference is the line image (kraken's polygon-based extraction against PaddleX's rectangle warp). Not investigated further.

docs.title: paddlex-ppocrv6-small
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

PaddleOCR's own PP-OCRv6 small recognizer on PaddleX's ONNX Runtime engine. Lines are cut as PaddleX's OCR pipeline cuts them (minimum-area rectangle of the polygon, warped upright), sorted by aspect ratio and read batch_size 8 at a time, as PaddleX's pipeline does. Words: the text split at whitespace, placed along the line by the CTC columns of their characters (PaddleX's return_word_box); PaddleX gives no per-word confidence.

On the 60-page BHL sample (2026-11-03, evidence/) the same modular pipeline with kraken's port of the model family read better on every volume but one; the likely difference is the line image (kraken's polygon-based extraction against PaddleX's rectangle warp). Not investigated further.

docs.title: qianfan-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Qianfan-OCR, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (built from the card and the checkpoint's config rather than inherited from Daniel van Strien's qianfan-ocr.py).

  • The page image, then the card's prompt Parse this document to Markdown. (image before text).
  • The image bytes as they are, no resize and no conversion, the media type sniffed from the magic bytes: the card documents no pixel bounds and the processor tiles and RGB-converts itself (max 12 tiles + a 448-px thumbnail). The 60-page sample's lossless WebP decodes to the same pixels as the board's dataset bytes.
  • Layout-as-Thought off (enable_thinking false per request; the card: disable it for homogeneous pages such as book pages).
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0 (the card's do_sample=False), top_p 1.0, max_tokens 8192.
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 16384, one image per prompt, no multimodal processor cache, no prefix caching. Not --trust-remote-code (the repo ships no code) and not the card's --hf-overrides to InternVLChatModel (vLLM registers the model natively; the override would run the InternVL code path).
  • The completion is stored verbatim; the board's </think> strip stays in its harness. --gpu-memory-utilization is the deployment's choice (board 0.85 on an A10G).

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0482 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0491 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: qwen3.5-9b
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Qwen3.5-9B as a page reader: the BHL OCR board's "greedy + card penalties" row (its driver, written from the model card and the checkpoint's config, run with --prompt neutral --card-penalties; there is no uv-scripts recipe for this model).

  • The page image, then the prompt Transcribe all of the text in this image. (the driver's neutral variant; a house choice, the card documents no OCR prompt). The board names the row by this variant.
  • RGB and, only when it has more than 2048 x 1024 px (2048 visual tokens at 1024 px per token), downscaled to that area keeping the aspect ratio (int truncation, LANCZOS); JPEG quality 95. Smaller pages are not upscaled.
  • Sampling: greedy (temperature 0.0, the board's deliberate deviation from the card) with the card's penalties (presence_penalty 1.5, repetition_penalty 1.0); max_tokens 8192; thinking off per request (the shipped template opens a <think> block unless enable_thinking is false).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image and no video per prompt; no --reasoning-parser (the driver drops the card's, so the completion stays in content), no --trust-remote-code.
  • The completion is stored verbatim; the board's unwrap_fence stays in its harness (linecaster.adapters.qwen35.unwrap_fence is the same rule).
  • Memory: 18.0 GiB of bf16 weights. The board ran it on an L40S at 0.9; whether it fits a 24 GB card (L4, A10G) with room for the vision encoder and the KV cache is not tested.

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0358 for linecaster's run on an L40S against 0.0356 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: smoldocling-256m-preview
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

SmolDocling-256M-preview, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it (a port of Daniel van Strien's smoldocling-ocr.py; where the two differ, the driver wins). The repository is now docling-project/SmolDocling-256M-preview; linecaster pins the id the board used.

  • The page image FIRST, then Convert this page to docling. (the card's chat example). The order matters: the repo's chat template branches on content[0]['type'] == 'image'.
  • RGB, downscaled (never upscaled) so its longest side is at most 2048 px (LANCZOS; the processor's own size.longest_edge, so only the payload shrinks), JPEG quality 95.
  • Sampling: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 6144 (the driver's choice, not the card's 8192: the native context is 8192 and an image takes up to about 1600 tokens), skip_special_tokens false (DocTags' <doctag> and <loc_*> are added special tokens; vLLM's default strips them).
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 8192 (max_position_embeddings, not raisable), no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt; no --trust-remote-code (Idefics3 is registered in vLLM).
  • The model answers in DocTags. The completion is stored verbatim; parse also converts it the board's way (docling-core, body + furniture, no image placeholder) into extra["markdown"]. The board converted with docling-core 2.89; linecaster's lock has a newer one.

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0643 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0556 for the board's own outputs on the same pages. The largest gap of the table (3 against 5 truncated pages); the board copy compared against may not be the scored run. Worth a second look.

docs.title: surya-ocr-2.5
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · experimental

Surya OCR 2.5, as the BHL OCR board's driver runs it: the surya-ocr package (0.23.0, the release that shipped with the checkpoint) and its full-page path, the call its surya_ocr command makes (RecognitionPredictor(manager)([page], full_page=True)), with the package's parser, blank-region filter and block-mode fallback. The engine (surya.recognition.v1, package linecaster-surya) reimplements none of it.

  • The server: the package would start vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1 with docker run. ServiceServer starts vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint instead (fetched, every pinned file checked, and served under the package's model name datalab-to/surya-ocr-2.5), with the flags the package's launcher passes for VLLM_GPU_TYPE=a100-80 (the board's A100 80 GB): --max-num-seqs 104 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, the package's dtype, model length, memory share, prefix caching and image limits; no MTP flag (the checkpoint has no MTP head). The engine attaches through SURYA_INFERENCE_URL, the package's own attach path. The image is the package's pin, by digest.
  • Every package setting is its default: full-page mode, 12,288 full-page tokens, guided layout JSON, SURYA_FULLPAGE_REGEN off (Datalab's own benchmark harness turns it on; the board keeps the shipped default). The page goes in as an RGB image at its own size; the package scales it to fit 3072 x 2048 px.
  • The package and vLLM need separate environments (surya-ocr pins OpenCV 4.11, vLLM needs 4.13 or later): vLLM is the image's, surya-ocr the pipeline script's. surya-ocr declares pillow<11; the pipeline script overrides it with linecaster's Pillow pin (12.3.0), which the board's run did not have.
  • Kept verbatim: the page's blocks as JSON (extra["raw"], the board's raw format: label, raw label, reading order, HTML, skipped, error, confidence, box). The board renders them to Markdown with chandra's HTML converter, page headers and footers kept (surya_blocks_to_markdown in bhl-ocr-eval's normalize_outputs). finish_reason is length when the page keeps a capped block's partial HTML; a failed block request is the page's error.

Weights: modified OpenRAIL-M (see the model's page). Run on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "The four board models the catalog lacked"): CER reading 0.0262 for linecaster's run on an RTX A6000 against 0.0251 for the board's own outputs on the same pages (the blocks' HTML identical on 52 of 60 pages). Not run on HF Jobs.

docs.title: unlimited-ocr-2
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Unlimited-OCR-2 on Baidu's patched SGLang, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it. No vLLM support exists for it.

  • Server: SGLang in the image's own Python (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-cu130), with Baidu's wheel (sglang-0.5.20.dev10+g8d62f5fb9c, read from the model repo at the pinned revision) installed --no-deps and fastokens==0.3.2 first; served as Unlimited-OCR-2; the card's launch environment and flags, plus --enable-metrics (saturate reads SGLang's queue gauges). SGLANG_UOCR_EANABLE_DOC_LIMIT is upstream's spelling. serve.version is the wheel's version, which is the SGLang that runs.
  • No --revision: with it, Baidu's SGLang skips its tokenizer fix-up and fastokens refuses the tokenizer at boot, so the server loads the default branch. The board refused to start unless the default branch was the pinned commit; it has since moved on (README and a newer wheel only), so the serve block checks instead that every file on the default branch other than README, .gitattributes, wheel/ and the paper PDF equals the pinned revision's (git blob ids).
  • The image, then <PAGE><image>Multi page parsing. (card-verbatim, the same prompt for one page as for many); full resolution, the same passthrough rule as v1.
  • max_tokens 8000, temperature 0.0, skip_special_tokens false, images_config {"crop_mode": true} (gundam, the card's single-page default), and the card's no-repeat n-gram guard as an SGLang custom logit processor (DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor, by its dill pickle reference) with its parameters.
  • The completion (<BLOCK>type[x1, y1, x2, y2]<FORK>text blocks) is stored verbatim; the board scores it after Baidu's own Markdown converter, which stays in its harness. A response without content is an error.
  • The board ran it on an RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB) with the card's flags for an 80 GB A800 (--mem-fraction-static 0.7, CUDA graphs up to 16384 prefill tokens).

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0251 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0262 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: unlimited-ocr
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recognition · core

Unlimited-OCR on vLLM, as the BHL OCR board's driver ran it.

  • The image, then the text part document parsing. (the card's <image>document parsing. minus the image token: over /chat/completions the image is its own content part).
  • Full resolution, no resize (the gundam crop grid is chosen from the input pixels): RGB PNG/JPEG bytes as they are, anything else RGB PNG.
  • Temperature 0.0, max_tokens 8192, skip_special_tokens false (the grounding tags must survive), and the card's no-repeat n-gram guard per request (vllm_xargs, the single-image setting) with its logits processor registered at boot, last on the command line as the driver keeps it.
  • Serve flags: --max-model-len 32768 --trust-remote-code, no prefix caching, no multimodal processor cache, one image per prompt. vLLM 0.26.0: the card's dedicated vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr image is obsolete, the architecture is registered.
  • The completion (grounded output, <|det|>type [bbox]<|/det|> headers) is stored verbatim; the board's rule for this model stays in its harness. A response without content is an error, not an empty page.

Validated on the 60-page sample (NOTES.md, "Board models as chat specs"): CER reading 0.0429 for linecaster's run on an L4 against 0.0449 for the board's own outputs on the same pages.

docs.title: unicode-recomposition
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · recomposition · core

squiddleocr's recomposition (its --text reflow): the rows of each text region joined into paragraphs, from geometry and Unicode's character properties, never from a language name; the squiddle combination's recomposition.

  • Paragraph breaks: a row indented by indent (0.8 em) from the start margin, a gap above it of about a blank line (more than gap_leading 0.6 of the leading and gap_height 0.5 of the taller row), or, in justified text (at least justified_rows 3 rows, justified_share 0.6 of them ending within end_margin 0.6 em of the end margin), a row before it that stopped short_row 1.5 em and short_row_width a quarter of the width short.
  • Division marks (Unicode's hyphens by Line_Break, and convention_marks, the not sign some transcription conventions write) after a letter at a row end are removed unless the next row starts with a capital or a digit, a Hebrew letter is not followed by Hebrew, or the document attests the hyphenated form and not the joined one. The lexicon is the item's own words, growing page by page.
  • Rows join without a space where UAX #14 allows a break without one (ideographs, Thai), else with one.
  • A paragraph without sentence-final punctuation that ends with a division mark or reaches the end margin continues in the next text region whose first row is not indented and starts with a letter, and, recomposing an item, on the next page; a region of digits only between them (a page number) does not close it.
  • Without geometry (a text-only transcription) a region is one paragraph.
Step recomposition (reads items) Engine recomposition.unicode.v1 Produces paragraphs

docs.title: slanet-plus
docs.text:
Preset · edition 2 · tables · core

PaddleX's table_recognition_v2 pipeline on every table region, fed with the page's own lines and their recognized text instead of its own OCR (use_ocr_model=False with an external OCR result); the cells come back with our text in PaddleX's HTML. The squiddle combination's table step.

  • SLANet_plus end to end for both table classes (e2e: structure and cell boxes from SLANet_plus's own prediction, the RT-DETR cell detectors unused). Chosen 2026-09-07 from four variants on five BHL tables: PP-StructureV3's own choice (SLANeXt_wired + cell detector for what the classifier calls wired) merged body rows on old ruled tables; SLANet_plus end to end kept every body row apart and filled the most cells.
  • crop_pad 8: with the layout box exactly, the models can flip to a worse cell set (25 cells and 44 words on one table against 17 cells and 121 words padded); from 8 px the result is stable.
  • The pipeline's other models are its submodels, by PaddleX name: the wired/wireless classifier (PP-LCNet_x1_0_table_cls, which picks the branch) and the two cell detectors (loaded by the pipeline, unused with e2e), each a pin of its model entry, so their files are part of the edition's hash.

Edition 2 (2026-11-03): the same models at the same revisions, moved from the option submodel_revisions (edition 1) to submodels, so their file hashes count too. Edition 1 was dropped from the lock when the catalogs were merged into one (2026-11-04), before any run recorded it. - Unruled rows come back as one cell per column with every PaddleX table model.
