docs.title: ratios
docs.text:
Preset · edition 1 · typography · core

squiddleocr's retyper: the hierarchy of a page from its own type sizes, every rule a ratio to the body size (the median row height of the page's text regions); the squiddle combination's typography.

  • levels: a heading whose rows are at least 2.5 times the body size is level 1, 1.7 times level 2, else level 3.
  • demote 1.2: a section header set in about the body size is text (layout models often call a bold run-in heading a section header).
  • split 1.6, max_headline_rows 3: up to three leading rows of a text region this much taller than the rows after them and the body size are a headline the layout model merged into the text; they become a section header of their own.
  • page_number_min_conf 0.75: a page-number region read with a lower mean character confidence (or empty) is an ornament or a blob, and is removed (recorded in extra["retyper_dropped"]).
  • Drop capitals (a layout model's drop-capital class) are joined to the first line of the text region they belong to.
Step typography (reads pages) Engine typography.ratios.v1 Produces hierarchy

docs.title: item-texts
docs.text:
Recipe · edition 1 · pipeline bind.v1 · core

The item stage's default combination: each item's pages recomposed as one item (unicode-recomposition: paragraphs continued across page breaks, the item's own words as the lexicon), normalized for reading (latin-historic: long s, ligatures, r rotunda and superscript e folded) and composed into the item's document (docling-composition). It writes the text variants verbatim_txt, readable_txt and readable_md and the item document in md, txt and json.

  • The readable texts come from the recomposition since phase 3 of the refactoring; before, a simpler flow joined each region's lines (NOTES.md has the comparison on the BHL ground truth's whole items).
  • For historic print in Latin script; other scripts are recomposed by the same Unicode rules, and the normalization leaves their characters as they are.
uv run launch.py item-texts IMAGES OUT
Slot Preset recomposition unicode-recomposition@1 normalization latin-historic@1 composition docling-composition@1

docs.title: squiddle
docs.text:
Recipe · edition 1 · pipeline transcribe_modular.v1 · core

SquiddleOCR's combination: fast OCR for historical print from small models. PP-DocLayoutV3 finds the regions and their reading order, PP-OCRv6 medium detection finds the lines on the whole page, kraken's PP-OCRv6 medium recognizer reads them (batch 8, bf16 on CUDA), SLANet_plus rebuilds tables and PP-FormulaNet_plus-L reads formulas as LaTeX; squiddleocr's rule-based steps make the typography, recompose the text into paragraphs (ratios, unicode-recomposition) and compose the page document (docling-composition); the readable item texts (--item-texts) are normalized with latin-historic.

  • The settings squiddleocr 0.3 shipped and its goldens were recorded with; the modular pipeline reproduces those goldens line for line (see the evidence).
  • The recomposition is squiddle ocr's default (its --text reflow); the goldens compare lines, which it does not change.
  • Until phase 3 of the refactoring the recipe named the rule-based steps through the option text: reflow; naming their presets changes neither the pipeline nor its outputs, so the edition was migrated (its earlier hashes stay in the lock as previous_sha256), not renumbered.
  • squiddle ocr runs this recipe when its model options are left at their defaults; with other models it is a variation, not the recipe.
uv run launch.py squiddle IMAGES OUT
Slot Preset layout pp-doclayoutv3@1 lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det@1 recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1 tables slanet-plus@2 formulas pp-formulanet-plus-l@1 typography ratios@1 recomposition unicode-recomposition@1 normalization latin-historic@1 composition docling-composition@1

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: What linecaster is made of and how a run fits together. Terms are the glossary's; contracts, the builder, failures and the run record are in pipelines, models, presets, recipes and engines in the catalog, the page record in the data model.

docs.title: What linecaster is
docs.text: An open, modular text-recognition suite for print and handwriting (OCR and HTR, old and new documents). It combines layout, line, text, table and formula recognizers with post-processing (dehyphenation, recomposition, normalization) into reproducible datatrove pipelines that turn page images into text: the text as written, readable variants next to it, ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR on request. Everything that produces text from images lives here; evaluation (ocrscout, bhl-ocr-eval) and project pipelines (EBDC, FineBooks) are built on top of it.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Package Holds linecaster.data the data model: Item, Page, PageImage, Transcription, Text, StepInfo, the measurements vocabulary linecaster.formats ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR out and in; the DoclingDocument exports linecaster.text the text transforms: Unicode, typography, recomposition, the text variants linecaster.images the working image, plots linecaster.engines the built-in engines: the rule-based steps and the single-region layout linecaster.blocks the blocks by family (blocks) linecaster.backends InProcess, Served, Chat linecaster.adapters one adapter per VLM family, ADAPTERS linecaster.serve linecaster serve linecaster.runtime the builder, the pipelines' command line, executors, the run record, Jobs helpers, secrets, logs linecaster.catalog the catalog: its entries, schemas, lock, fetching pins, the docs of its entries linecaster.tracing tracing (OpenTelemetry) and linecaster traces linecaster.docs linecaster docs: the generated pages linecaster.testing test helpers: sample pages, fake engines (fake.<step>.v1, the page engine fake.recognition.page.v1), a fake chat server, a fake HTTP service, the conformance checks check_engine and check_block, the pytest markers

The first five load neither datatrove nor saturate, nor linecaster's blocks or runtime (tests/test_import_rule.py), so derivatives can use the data model and the formats without the pipeline machinery. datatrove and saturate are required dependencies; engines, Ray, pybookget, resilient-httpx (proxy lists) and PDFium are not (engine packages and extras).

docs.title: Blocks and backends
docs.text:
A block is a datatrove PipelineStep with a contract; a pipeline is a list of blocks run by a datatrove executor. Each family is a subpackage of linecaster.blocks (blocks has a page per block).

Model blocks (ModelBlock: LayoutDetector, LineDetector, LineRecognizer, TableRecognizer, FormulaRecognizer, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer) each have a backend:

  • InProcess("pkg:Class", **kwargs) (or a preset ref) loads the engine in the worker, in warm_up() before the first page; a loaded engine is never pickled. In-process is always available and is the parity reference.
  • Served(endpoint, model=name) and Chat(preset, endpoint) (a VLM) stream pages through saturate (AdaptiveClient and through()): a window of pages in flight, adapted to the server's queue gauges and 429s; results passed on as they finish; secrets as EnvVar. The streaming exists once, in ModelBlock.

A page that failed a step carries doc.metadata["errors"], passes later model steps at once and goes to rejects/; more failures than the error budget fail the task (pipelines). Library code raises linecaster.errors, never SystemExit.

Rule blocks (RuleBlock: Typographer, Recomposer, Composer, CharacterNormalizer; and ImageConverter) run a built-in engine of a rule-based step in the pipeline's process, picked by a preset.

docs.title: One page per request
docs.text: A request carries one page; engines batch only within a page (kraken batches a page's lines). A page's result depends only on the page, never on what else is in flight, so runs are deterministic whatever the executor, the number of tasks or the backend.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text:
• linecaster serve hosts engines: stateless (no state between requests), one worker per model (several replicas per model were measured at +7–10 % and removed; NOTES.md), each with a bounded queue (--max-queue; a full queue answers 429 with Retry-After). Routes: POST /v1/linecaster/{step} (the image and the transcription so far in, the transcription with its part added out), GET /v1/models, /health and vLLM-shaped /metrics (the gauges saturate reads). Built-in engines are not served: they run in the pipeline's process.
  • VLMs run behind OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, SGLang, hosted endpoints): PageRecognizer and RegionRecognizer on the Chat backend, on /v1/chat/completions, served only. PageRecognizer also runs a page engine (an engine whose unit is the page) on the InProcess or Served backend: a vendor's package in the worker (Indra OCR), a vendor's package attached to a vLLM server (Surya OCR), or a client of a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API (Falcon-OCR, OXR). A VLM is a catalog preset (engine chat.v1; its data: revision, prompt, sampling, serve block) plus an adapter in linecaster.adapters.ADAPTERS (its code: the request, the parsing; chat_model(<preset>)).
  • Servers inside a task (one GPU per HF Job): the server blocks ModelServer (linecaster serve) and ChatModelServer (vLLM or SGLang) start the server through saturate's Engine and go last in the pipeline, after the writer: datatrove chains generators, and only the last one lives until every page is written. Each task starts its own servers. ModelServer(script=...) starts a pipeline script's serve with uv run --script. ServiceServer starts the service a page preset's serve block names: vllm serve on the pinned checkpoint (fetched and checked) for an engine package that attaches to vLLM, or a vendor image's entrypoint (with the weights downloaded to the folder it reads first), ready once its health URLs answer; it runs without the pipeline's environment, in the image's own. A vendor's entrypoint listens on the image's fixed ports: one service per machine.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text: An engine is a class with a versioned id (catalog). Engine packages live in engines/<engine>/, each its own package: linecaster-kraken, linecaster-paddlex, linecaster-tesseract, and the page engines' linecaster-indra, linecaster-surya and linecaster-services (the clients of Falcon-OCR's and OXR's services). An engine class (<Provider><Step>Engine) has engine_id (the entry point's name in linecaster.engines), step, capabilities (unit, produces), an Options model (its keyword arguments; a preset's weights besides), load() and __call__(image, transcription, **params) -> Transcription (the page image as an RGB array, or the image file's bytes for an engine whose image_input is "bytes", and the transcription so far, returned with its part added). Engines with weights load exactly the pin (weights, linecaster.catalog.fetch). PaddleX's models load from the pinned snapshot (create_predictor(model_dir=...)); small-models-for-glam/kraken-blla-base (the BLLA base model of September 2026) is pinned in linecaster_kraken.models, and no engine uses it. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in linecaster's catalog. They import from linecaster only linecaster.data and the engine API (linecaster.engines.api: the Engine protocol, Capabilities, the weight helpers), have versions of their own with a range of linecaster releases, and their tests in engines/<engine>/tests/ (catalog).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: uv run pytest runs the core's tests; tests marked gpu or network (linecaster.testing.markers: gpu, network, slow, parity; --strict-markers) skip where the device or the network is missing. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml, CPU only, no secrets) runs uv sync --locked --all-extras (the extras' readers are tested and documented too), uv run pytest -m "not gpu and not network and not parity", linecaster docs --check, linecaster catalog verify and the site's strict build. The docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) publishes the site with mike on the gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves (https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/): a release tag v<major>.<minor>.<patch> as version <major>.<minor>, with latest (the site's default) moved to it, and every push to main as version dev. The engines' environments are too large for it (torch): their tests (engines/<engine>/tests/) and the PEP 723 test scripts (tests/test_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py, tests/test_line_recognizers.py) run locally, the goldens compare (tests/parity/compare_goldens.py) on the machines that have the goldens. Every built-in engine and every public block passes the conformance checks of linecaster.testing (check_engine: the engine protocol; check_block: the contract against what the block does to sample pages, to_dict(), pickling, warm_up(), failed pages).

docs.title: Pipeline scripts
docs.text:
There are no environment folders: a pipeline is a self-contained uv script in pipelines/ (a PEP 723 block, a <script>.py.lock next to it, uv run <script>) that builds one pipeline shape with slots, one script per shape, never one per machine:

Script Pipeline id Does harvest.py harvest.v1 downloads page images (and a library's OCR, manifests) once into item folders, plus page records transcribe_modular.py transcribe_modular.v1 lines and a recognizer, optionally layout, tables, formulas, then post-processing; every step a preset the user picks transcribe_vlm.py transcribe_vlm.v1 a VLM per page or per layout region transcribe_page.py transcribe_page.v1 a page engine per page, with the service its preset names bind.py bind.v1 item texts and item documents from page records

linecaster.runtime.run.main gives every pipeline the same command line: --on local|ray|hf-jobs, --backend in-process|served, --endpoint (a running server), serve (linecaster serve with the script's models), ray (Ray's CLI from the script's environment). Slots have no default presets: every slot is picked, or a recipe fills them (--recipe); launch.py runs a recipe or a page preset by name (catalog). Each script's page in the catalog's docs lists its slots and options.

Script environments: the repository is not a uv workspace (engine pins conflict). Sources apply only to a script's direct dependencies, so scripts with kraken list the fork directly; the numerically relevant versions are pinned with constraint-dependencies, the same list in every engine script. tests/test_scripts.py checks pins, sources, locks and wheels for both machines (uv's required-environments does not work in scripts). PaddleX's GUI OpenCV pin is satisfied by stubs/opencv-contrib-python (the headless build of the same version; one cv2).

docs.title: Executors and Jobs
docs.text:
--on Executor local datatrove's LocalPipelineExecutor ray RayGPUExecutor for stages with servers (one task per GPU), datatrove's RayPipelineExecutor otherwise (extra [ray]) hf-jobs JobsExecutor: datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor with JSON-lines logs; GPUJobsExecutor for multi-GPU flavors

datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor is experimental and dill-pickles the pipeline, so the launching machine and the Jobs run the same Python minor version (3.12). uv run --with drops [tool.uv.sources]: linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script) spells out a pipeline's dependencies, sources (as URLs; the commit must be pushed) and pins (pipelines). A private derivative ships its code as a wheel mounted from a bucket folder (WheelJobsExecutor, wheel_volume).

docs.title: The run layout
docs.text:
One job is one pipeline for one batch on one executor; resume is datatrove's, per task, so tasks stay small. A pipeline reads the previous folder and writes complete page records with one more part filled in:

Folder Holds originals/ the delivered images and files; never modified OUT/pages/ page records (PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter), bucketed by item id: a whole item in one file, so no joins OUT/rejects/ every page that carries errors (RejectWriter, put before the first writer by the builder): key, field, error, raw value OUT/logs/ datatrove's completion markers, logs and stats OUT/traces/ the traces (tracing) OUT/run.yaml the run record (pipelines)

PageRecordReader reads page records of linecaster's writers, fetching images again by URI (uri_map for local copies). Checks like PageValidator record on the page why it failed.

Readers follow datatrove's conventions (BaseDiskReader: data_folder, paths_file, glob_pattern, limit/skip per task; files distributed over tasks in turn, Parquet tables by rows in equal shards, linecaster.blocks.readers.tables, so a table needs no splitting): ImageFolderReader (image files), ImageParquetReader (an image column: bytes, an HF image struct or a path), ManifestReader (IIIF or METS, parsed by pybookget, extra [pybookget], which also fetches http(s):// images through linecaster.net.http; a manifest, or a row of a Parquet item table, is an entry, so an item stays in one task; a IIIF Collection entry is its manifests, one level; existing_ocr fetches a library's OCR as a document media, which a TranscriptionConverter reads as ocr_original, the builder adding one when missing), PdfReader (PDF files as items, pages rendered with pypdfium2, extra [pypdfium2]) and PageRecordReader. Readers that fetch over http(s) request ahead in a window that grows while no request waits for the rate limits (linecaster.net.http.prefetched), through one fetcher per process and configuration, so the limits hold across a worker's tasks; ImageParquetReader and ManifestReader suggest a task count from their input (auto_tasks), which a pipeline without engines runs with (pipelines).

The workflow is harvest → transcribe → bind: pipelines/harvest.py downloads images (and OCR, manifests) once into item folders plus page records, the transcribe pipelines read those with --pages, pipelines/bind.py makes item texts and documents. An item's pages can land in different tasks; item-level steps are a second stage over item shards (--item-shards N writes OUT/pages/<shard>/<rank>, pipelines/bind.py reads whole shards), as datatrove's own multi-stage pipelines read per-bucket folders (pipelines).

docs.title: The catalog: models, presets, recipes, evidence
docs.text:
The catalog describes every model Linecaster can run, how it runs it, the tested combinations, and the measurements behind them. Its entries live in one folder, src/linecaster/catalog/data/, shipped with linecaster; linecaster.catalog reads, validates and resolves them.

src/linecaster/catalog/data/
  models/<id>/model.yaml, model.md        # + upstream/<revision>/ (the upstream card, verbatim)
  presets/<step>/<id>.yaml, <id>.md       # one folder per step (STEPS)
  recipes/<id>.yaml, <id>.md
  evidence/<date>-<subject>-<dataset>.yaml
  catalog.lock
src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json    # generated from the Pydantic models

docs.title: What the catalog holds
docs.text:
The catalog and its docs are organized by five kinds: engines and pipelines (code, by versioned id) and three kinds of catalog entry (models, presets, recipes; a YAML file each).

Kind Is Named Lives in engine code that implements one step: runs a model, or applies rules versioned id: kraken.recognition.v1, typography.ratios.v1 engines/<engine>/ (a package each); chat.v1 and the rule-based engines in linecaster (linecaster.engines) model one upstream artifact at pinned revisions, with its card slug: kraken-ppocrv6-medium models/<id>/model.yaml preset an engine, a model pin and the engine's options, ready to use slug, with an edition: kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1 presets/<step>/<id>.yaml pipeline code: a shape with slots and the run-anywhere command line versioned id: transcribe_modular.v1 (the script's name) pipelines/<name>.py recipe a named combination: a pipeline, a preset edition per slot, options slug, with an edition: squiddle@1 recipes/<id>.yaml

Besides these: evidence records (catalog entries too: one measurement of a preset or recipe edition), the lock (released editions) and the run record (OUT/run.yaml, and per page in each StepInfo: what a run resolved).

docs.title: Ids and versions
docs.text:
Term Whose Meaning Example version upstream what upstream calls it, verbatim, never parsed PP-OCRv6 medium, Chandra 2 revision upstream the exact identity of the files HF commit, version DOI, git commit, sha256 edition linecaster integer per preset or recipe, raised when outputs can change edition: 3 .v<n> linecaster the contract of an engine's options or a pipeline's slots and options transcribe_modular.v1 schema linecaster the format of a YAML file linecaster.preset/1 release linecaster the package version (run records only) 0.4.0
  • Slugs (models, presets, recipes): lowercase [a-z0-9.-]. They may contain upstream names (deepseek-ocr-2), never our versions. Ids are unique across presets and recipes, so a name means one thing.
  • Code ids (CODE_ID): lowercase dotted names ending in .v<n>. An incompatible change is a new id (.v2); the old one stays registered. Adding an option is compatible when its default keeps the old behavior; changing a default, removing or renaming an option is not.
  • A reference is id@edition; id alone means the current edition. Run records always store the explicit edition and its hash.
  • A tag or branch is resolved to a commit when a model is pinned; the tag is kept as tag: for information. Zenodo: the version DOI identifies the files, the concept DOI is information. Downloads without a commit: the file's sha256 is the revision.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A model, preset or recipe is a YAML file, the data, validated strictly by linecaster.catalog.schema (unknown keys are errors), and a Markdown file of the same name next to it, the prose for people (why these settings, limitations, changes), without front matter. Tools read only the YAML; the docs generator also includes the prose. The prose is optional, except for presets and recipes with support: core. Evidence and the lock are YAML only. Bulk data (page records, exports) is JSON Lines or Parquet, not catalog data.

Format Schema id JSON Schema model linecaster.model/1 schemas/model-1.json preset linecaster.preset/1 schemas/preset-1.json recipe linecaster.recipe/1 schemas/recipe-1.json evidence linecaster.evidence/1 schemas/evidence-1.json lock linecaster.lock/2 schemas/lock-2.json run record (OUT/run.yaml, not catalog data; its schema ships here) linecaster.run-record/1 schemas/run-record-1.json

Every YAML file names its format twice: its first line is # yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json> (for editors), and its field schema holds the schema id (for tools). The JSON Schemas are generated from the Pydantic models (linecaster catalog schemas); the test suite fails when a committed one differs from a fresh one.

YAML has 1.2 semantics, read with ruamel.yaml through linecaster.catalog.yamlio: only true / false are booleans (NO stays Norwegian), and a duplicate key is an error. Values that look like numbers or versions are quoted ("1.0"). Commands that write a file back (release, pin) keep its comments.

docs.title: Model (models/<id>/model.yaml)
docs.text:
Field Meaning id, version our slug; upstream's name, verbatim source kind (hf, zenodo, git, url) and ref (repo id, concept DOI, repository URL, download URL) pins one entry per upstream revision: revision, tag, doi, pinned (date), files (name → sha256:<hex>), card, card_sha256, license_file license SPDX id where there is one, else the license's own name languages, scripts ISO 639-3 (mul for many), ISO 15924 params parameter count, as upstream states it derived_from ref and relation (mirror, converted, quantized, finetuned)

The upstream card is always copied, verbatim, at the pinned revision, whatever its license: Hugging Face README.md, the HTRMoPo record, a repository README; a separate license file next to it. Its sha256 is in the pin. Cards are never edited; license, languages and scripts in model.yaml are taken from them where they say. A new upstream revision is a new entry in pins, with its own upstream/<revision>/ folder. Model entries are written by linecaster catalog pin.

docs.title: Preset (presets/<step>/<id>.yaml)
docs.text: Field Meaning id, edition, step the step must match the folder model id and revision of a model pin submodels further pins of a multi-model engine, by role engine the engine's id: engine: kraken.recognition.v1 options the engine's options (its Options model) settings prompts, sampling and other request settings (chat presets) labels native layout label → DoclingDocument label; unmapped labels are text by_script a by-script engine's strategies: ISO 15924 script code → preset id@edition of the same step, and "*" → the default for every other script (required) serve the server it was validated with: server (vllm, sglang, linecaster, vendor), version, image (with digest, for HF Jobs), flags, env, revision_flag, pin_ignore, server_packages, draft (speculative decoding); a vendor's service also command, health, weights_dir (page engines) capabilities unit (line, region, page, item) and produces (the parts it adds, vocabulary PARTS) provenance derived_from (sources of the settings, each at a commit or revision), authored_by, created support, superseded_by see Support

docs.title: Recipe (recipes/<id>.yaml)
docs.text:
Field Meaning id, edition pipeline the pipeline it fills: pipeline: transcribe_modular.v1 presets slot → preset id@edition (always an explicit edition) options the pipeline's options, by name provenance, support, superseded_by as for presets

Measurements of a whole run (goldens, the pipeline's CER) are the recipe's evidence. A derivative's recipe lives in this catalog too (squiddleocr's squiddle); the derivative names it by id.

docs.title: Evidence (evidence/<date>-<subject>-<dataset>.yaml)
docs.text: One measurement per file: preset: id@edition or recipe: id@edition, context (for a preset measured inside a pipeline: the rest of it), source (own-run, board, card-claim, vendor-benchmark), dataset (repo@revision, or a description for claims), metrics, date, hardware, software (linecaster commit, server version, backend: in-process or served), run, notes. Claims are never measurements; the docs show the source of every number.

docs.title: Released editions are immutable
docs.text:
linecaster catalog release <id> writes the current edition's resolved functional content and its sha256 into catalog.lock (per entry: sha256, previous_sha256 where a catalog migration changed it (a list, oldest first, after several), released, linecaster commit, resolved; a recipe edition also pipeline and pipeline_sha256, below).

  • A preset's functional content is what can change outputs: step, the model pin and every submodel pin (id, revision, files), engine, options, settings, labels, by_script (each strategy's edition with that edition's hash, as a recipe names its presets) and serve. A by-script preset is released only on released strategies. Only what the YAML file states counts, so a new optional schema field changes no hash. The Markdown prose, provenance, support level and capabilities are not part of it.
  • A recipe's functional content is its pipeline, each slot's preset edition with that edition's hash and the options it states. A recipe is released only on released preset editions, so one recipe edition pins a whole run down to the weights' files.

linecaster catalog verify (and tests/catalog/test_catalog.py) fails when a released edition's content changed; such a change is a new edition. Old editions stay resolvable from the lock after the file moves on. Unreleased editions are drafts.

docs.title: A recipe edition's expanded pipeline
docs.text:
A recipe names a pipeline id, presets and options; what runs is the pipeline its script builds from them. The lock keeps that too: release builds the recipe's pipeline (its pipeline script with --recipe id@edition on placeholder folders, in-process, one task) and records pipeline, every block with its class and its functional parameters (engines with their options, presets with their hashes; pipelines), and its pipeline_sha256, the hash a run record of that recipe names. verify builds every released recipe edition's pipeline again and reports drift: a block, a parameter or a default that changed in code changes the hash, and verify names the blocks that differ.

Building it needs no engine: the describe mode (linecaster.runtime.run.describe_script) loads the pipeline script as a module of the current process (its PEP 723 environment is not used), and blocks and backends import no engine before warm_up(); a preset whose engine is not installed names the engine's class from the repository's engine packages (catalog.code). So verify runs in the core environment, and its hash is the one a run of the script with its engines records. It needs the pipeline scripts of the checkout.

Drift is resolved like any change of a released edition: a change that can change outputs gives the recipe a new edition; a change of the code that keeps behavior (a renamed parameter, a new option whose default keeps the old behavior) is recorded anew with linecaster catalog release <id> --migrate-pipeline. A recipe edition released before pipelines were locked gets its pipeline on its next release (a catalog migration: the edition and its sha256 stay). The lock format stays linecaster.lock/2: the two fields are optional, and only recipe entries have them.

docs.title: Catalog migrations
docs.text: A change of the catalog's own vocabulary or format that keeps every output as it was (a renamed step, a renamed pipeline id, a new file format) is a catalog migration: every released edition keeps its number, its resolved content is rewritten in the new terms and its hash recomputed, and the hash it had before stays in the lock as previous_sha256 (after a second migration a list of both, oldest first). A run record names id@edition and that edition's hash at the time; it resolves by either hash (Catalog.resolve(ref, sha256=...), resolve_recipe, by_sha256, linecaster catalog show sha256:<hex>). A change that can change outputs is never a migration: it is a new edition. A recipe that comes to name, as presets, what its pipeline already ran (squiddle@1 naming the rule-based presets its pipeline ran through the option text: reflow) is a migration too: the pipeline it expands to is the same blocks with the same parameters, so the edition keeps its number, and catalog release --migrate-pipeline records the expanded pipeline again (the recipe stamp carries the new hash).

docs.title: Steps, capabilities, labels
docs.text:
Steps (STEPS): layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, whose engines run models, and the rule-based steps (RULE_STEPS) image (the working image), normalization (character fidelity: as written → normalized), typography (the hierarchy from type sizes), recomposition (running text from the rows: paragraphs) and composition (the document). Recognition reads a unit (capabilities.unit): line (kraken, PaddleX, Tesseract), region (a VLM per layout region) or page (a VLM or a page engine reads the whole page: a page preset, which launch.py runs by name); a rule-based engine reads a page or an item (the pages of one item, in order). OCRD_STEPS maps the steps to OCR-D's functional steps for METS agents where OCR-D has one (image: preprocessing/optimization, typography: layout/segmentation/classification, composition: layout/analysis); the others are post-processing (recognition/post-correction).

What depends on the code belongs to the engine (capabilities on the class), e.g. kraken's word boxes with confidences. What depends on the weights belongs to the model or preset: languages, scripts, output format.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
An engine is a class registered under its id in the entry-point group linecaster.engines ("kraken.recognition.v1" = "linecaster_kraken:KrakenRecognitionEngine"), or one of linecaster's own (BUILTIN_ENGINES): chat.v1 (VLM presets, served only: SERVED_ONLY; the Chat backend), the single-region layout and the rule-based engines. It declares engine_id, step, Options (a Pydantic model whose fields have descriptions; the docs come from it) and capabilities, and takes the pin as weights (and submodel_weights), fetched and checked by linecaster.catalog.fetch. Engine packages carry code only; their presets and models are in this catalog.

Engine packages (engines/<engine>/: linecaster-kraken, linecaster-paddlex, linecaster-tesseract, linecaster-indra, linecaster-surya, linecaster-services) have versions of their own and a range of linecaster releases they work with (linecaster>=0.0.1,<0.2), and import from linecaster only the data model (linecaster.data) and the engine API (linecaster.engines.api): the Engine protocol, Capabilities, and the weight helpers weights_of (a model pin as weights), hf_file and hf_snapshot (a Hugging Face pin's files, checked) and model_entry (a model's catalog entry); tests/test_import_rule.py reads the packages with ast and fails on any other import. They are not on PyPI: a preset whose engine is not installed is a CatalogError that names the package that provides it and the pipeline scripts whose environments install it (catalog.code.install_hint). Each package has its tests in engines/<engine>/tests/ (conformance through linecaster.testing.check_engine, and its own units), run in an environment that has it (uv run tests/test_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests; the page engines' packages: uv run tests/test_page_engines_catalog.py engines/<engine>/tests, the environment of pipelines/transcribe_page.py).

docs.title: Page engines and their services
docs.text:
A page engine is an engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page (capabilities.unit: page): it gets the page image and returns the page's transcription, text-only, its raw output verbatim in extra["raw"], as a chat preset's completion is kept. PageRecognizer runs it like any model block (InProcess, or Served through linecaster serve); pipelines/transcribe_page.py is its pipeline. Where the engine talks to a service, its preset's serve block names it and ServiceServer starts it in the task:

serve.server The service Fields vllm vllm serve <the model pin, fetched> --host --port <flags> --served-model-name <the Hugging Face id>, for an engine package that attaches to vLLM (surya.recognition.v1) version, image, flags vendor a vendor's page pipeline in its own image (falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1): the image's entrypoint image (by digest), command (the entrypoint), env, health (loopback URLs that must answer 200, in order), weights_dir (where the model pin is downloaded first, when the image reads the weights from a folder)

The engine's endpoint option (where its service is) is operational: presets leave it to its default (the service's loopback port), a pipeline sets it for a running service (--recognition-endpoint), and the pipeline's hash leaves it out.

docs.title: The single-region layout
docs.text: layout.single-region.v1 (linecaster.engines:SingleRegionLayoutEngine, preset single-region@1) is a layout engine without a model: one region covering the page image (label text, id page, reading order 0; both options), recorded as a layout step. It has the model engines' call (__call__(image, transcription)), so LayoutDetector("single-region@1") runs it, and like the rule-based engines it is built in and runs in the pipeline's process only. pipelines/transcribe_modular.py --layout single-region reads a page as one region.

docs.title: Rule-based engines
docs.text:
The engines of the rule-based steps (strategies) live in linecaster.engines, are pure Python and run in the pipeline's process only (IN_PROCESS_ONLY; linecaster serve refuses them): image.webp-lossless.v1, normalization.latin-historic.v1, typography.ratios.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1, composition.docling.v1, and the by-script engines normalization.by-script.v1 and recomposition.by-script.v1. Each has no weights; its Options turn the rules' thresholds into options whose defaults are the values the rules have always had, and it declares scripts: the ISO 15924 scripts it covers (Latn, Hebr, ...), "*" for all. The rules themselves stay in linecaster.text, linecaster.images and linecaster.formats; the engines are thin.

The call per unit (linecaster.engines.base): page unit __call__(t: Transcription, **options) -> Transcription; item unit __call__(pages: list[Transcription], **options) -> list[Transcription] (an item's pages in order; a page is an item of one page); the image step takes and returns the image's bytes (__call__(data, **options) -> (bytes, info)). Options given to a call override the engine's for that call. Each records a StepInfo with its engine id, its options as settings and its counts as measurements; the block that runs it adds the preset edition and its hash, seconds and datetime. The item unit of the composition is item_document(pages, name, ...): an item's document is no transcription.

Their blocks take a preset (id@edition) or an engine spec (InProcess("module:Class", **options)), with options over either, like model blocks but without a backend choice: ImageConverter(output_folder, preset) (image), CharacterNormalizer(preset) (normalization), Typographer(preset) (typography), Recomposer(preset, unit="page"|"item") (recomposition), Composer(preset, unit="page"|"item") (composition). The presets that reproduce squiddleocr's rules: working-image@1, latin-historic@1, ratios@1, unicode-recomposition@1, docling-composition@1. Running text or the page as laid out is the presence of a Recomposer: the Composer composes from paragraphs when there are, else from lines (diplomatic composition).

docs.title: Scripts and dispatch
docs.text:
A preset whose engine is a by-script engine names its strategies in by_script: an ISO 15924 code per script that needs its own rules, "*" for every other script.

id: hebrew-latin-recomposition
step: recomposition
engine: recomposition.by-script.v1
by_script:
  Hebr: hebrew-recomposition@1
  "*": unicode-recomposition@1

engine_spec resolves them into the engine's strategies (each strategy's engine, options, edition and hash). The engine (ScriptDispatch) routes each decision to the strategy of the script around it: for a decision at a row end (a division mark, the separator between two rows) the script of the last character before the row end that has one, else of the first after it (characters of the scripts Common and Inherited, such as spaces, hyphens, digits and combining marks, have none); for a normalization, each run of a text in one script (Common and Inherited characters stay with the run before them). A script without a strategy of its own goes to "*". Scripts are Unicode's Script property, matched with the regex package's \p{Script=...}. verify checks that every strategy is an edition of the same step and covers its script.

docs.title: Pipelines, recipes and launch.py
docs.text:
Every pipeline script declares PIPELINE, its id: its file name with .v<n> (harvest.v1, transcribe_modular.v1, transcribe_vlm.v1, transcribe_page.v1, bind.v1). A script with slots also declares SLOTS (slot → option; the option is the step's name: --layout, --lines, --recognition, ...; the rule-based steps are slots too: transcribe_modular.v1 has --typography, --recomposition, --normalization (the readable item texts' normalization, for --item-texts) and --composition, bind.v1 --recomposition, --normalization and --composition; a slot left empty leaves its step out, e.g. no recomposition: the page stays as laid out). It has no default presets: the user fills every slot, or names a recipe (--recipe id[@edition]), with single flags on top recorded as overrides in the run record (recipe: the edition, the pipeline id, the hash and the overrides).

The recipes: squiddle (transcribe_modular.v1: squiddleocr's models and rule-based steps) and item-texts (bind.v1: unicode-recomposition@1, latin-historic@1, docling-composition@1, the item stage's default combination).

uv run launch.py NAME IMAGES OUT [options] launches a recipe or a page preset by name: it finds the script whose PIPELINE the recipe names (transcribe_vlm.v1 for chat page presets, transcribe_page.v1 for page engines' presets) and runs it in that script's own environment with --recipe or --recognition. serve and ray pass through for recipes. A preset that is one step of a pipeline gets a hint instead: the pipeline, the flag and the recipes that use it.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: core (maintained, validated), experimental (works, may change), legacy (kept resolvable; superseded_by: names the replacement).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Does linecaster models [--step STEP] lists the presets (and the recipes) linecaster catalog pin ID --hf REPO [--revision REV] pins a Hugging Face model: model entry, card, file hashes linecaster catalog pin ID --github OWNER/NAME --revision COMMIT --file F [--tag T] pins files of a GitHub repository linecaster catalog release ID [--commit SHA] [--migrate-pipeline] freezes the current edition of a preset or recipe in the lock, a recipe with its expanded pipeline linecaster catalog verify checks the files (schema lines, prose next to its YAML file), the JSON Schemas against the models, cards, pins, released editions and their hashes, recipes and their expanded pipelines, and evidence linecaster catalog show REF the resolved functional content of a preset or recipe edition (id@edition, or a hash, today's or a previous one), with its hash linecaster catalog schemas [--out DIR] regenerates the JSON Schemas (default src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/) linecaster docs [--out docs] [--readme README.md] [--check] the generated docs (the catalog's pages among them) and the README's tables; --check writes nothing and fails naming each file that differs

The catalog's generated pages are grouped by kind: docs/catalog/{engines, models, presets/<step>, pipelines, recipes}/ and an index. Engine and pipeline pages are read from the source (linecaster.catalog.code, with ast), so the engines need not be installed. The evidence tables on preset and recipe pages name each record's source, hardware and backend.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: What linecaster keeps stable for derivatives, pipelines and stored outputs, and how a change that breaks it is announced. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: What counts as a breaking change
docs.text:
A change is breaking when code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference that worked before stops working or starts to mean something else:

Surface Breaking Not breaking blocks a block renamed or removed; a constructor argument renamed, removed or made required; a default that changes what a run writes a new block; a new argument whose default keeps the old behavior backends InProcess, Served, Chat renamed or removed, or an argument as for blocks a new argument with a default that keeps the old behavior commands and flags a linecaster command or a pipeline script's option renamed, removed, or given another meaning or default a new command or option pipeline ids and slots a pipeline id or a slot renamed or removed, a slot's step changed a new pipeline script; a new slot that can stay empty page records and item records a field renamed, removed or given another meaning; a schema id (linecaster.page/2) whose records a reader no longer reads a new optional field; a new schema version that PageRecordReader reads together with the older ones the run layout a folder or file name under OUT (pages/, rejects/, logs/, traces/, run.yaml) or its format changed a new file or folder the catalog a catalog id (model, preset, recipe) renamed or removed; a released edition changed; the lock format changed without a migration a new entry or edition; a catalog migration that keeps every output engines an engine id removed; an option renamed or removed, or a default changed (a new code id, .v2, instead) a new engine; a new option whose default keeps the old behavior (the same id)

Internal modules and names with a leading underscore, log messages, stats and the generated docs are not part of it.

docs.title: While the version is 0.x
docs.text: There is no deprecation period and there are no aliases: a breaking change takes effect in the release that makes it, and every breaking change is an upgrade note in CHANGELOG.md (what changed, who is affected, what to do), listed first.

docs.title: Released catalog editions
docs.text: A released edition never changes (catalog): a change that can change outputs is a new edition, and the old one stays resolvable from the lock. A catalog migration (a change of the catalog's vocabulary or format that keeps every output) recomputes an edition's hash and keeps the old one as previous_sha256, so run records written before it still resolve. Engine and pipeline code ids follow the same rule: an incompatible change of options or slots is a new id, and the old one stays registered.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Rules that hold across the repository. Each rule is followed by its reason. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
What Pattern Examples block <Object><RoleNoun>; readers and writers <Object><Format>Reader / Writer LineRecognizer, Typographer, Composer, Binder, ManifestReader, PageJsonlWriter composite block <Purpose><RoleNoun> ModularTranscriber block base classes <Kind>Block PageBlock, ModelBlock, RuleBlock engine class <Provider><Step>Engine KrakenRecognitionEngine, UnicodeRecompositionEngine engine id <provider>.<step>.v<n> kraken.recognition.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1 VLM adapter <Model>Adapter ChandraOCRAdapter pipeline script a verb, <verb>[_<kind>].py harvest.py, transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, transcribe_page.py, bind.py pipeline id the script's file name, .v<n> transcribe_modular.v1 slot and its flag the step's name --layout, --lines, --recognition catalog step a noun for the activity layout, recognition, recomposition transcription names ocr_new, ocr_original, ground_truth, or <source>

Reason: one pattern makes names guessable, and role nouns say what a block is in a pipeline. Pipeline scripts are verbs because they are what one runs.

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
American English everywhere: code, flags, docs, commit messages (normalize, recognizer, behavior, license, color, catalog). Upstream text copied verbatim (model cards) keeps its spelling.

Reason: one spelling for everything typed, matching Python and its ecosystem.

docs.title: YAML and Markdown
docs.text:
• Data that tools read is YAML; prose for people is Markdown. A catalog entry is <id>.yaml, optionally with <id>.md next to it; tools never read the Markdown. Reason: Markdown renders cleanly, data validates, and diffs of the two do not mix.
  • Every YAML file names its format twice: a first line # yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json> (editors validate and complete) and a field schema: linecaster.<kind>/<n> (tools check it). Reason: mistakes show while editing, not at run time.
  • The schemas are generated from the pydantic models (model_json_schema()) into src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/ (shipped with the package; linecaster catalog schemas rewrites them), and a test fails when a committed schema differs from a fresh one. The pydantic models are the only source of truth. Reason: one definition, used by tools and editors alike.
  • YAML is YAML 1.2, read with ruamel.yaml: true/false are the only booleans (NO stays a string), duplicate keys are errors, and tools that write files back keep their comments.
  • An edition's hash covers its functional content (what changes behavior: step, engine, options, pins, settings, labels, serving), read from the YAML. The Markdown prose and descriptive fields (support, provenance) are not part of it, so they can be corrected without a new edition; git keeps their history.

Schemas: preset, recipe, model, evidence, run-record, lock. Stored page records name their format in a schema field of their row (linecaster.page/2).

docs.title: Docstrings
docs.text:
Google style, checked by tests/test_docstrings.py (with ast, no extra tool) for every public block, built-in engine, backend, serializer, build, run_pages, runtime.run.main, public function of linecaster.catalog and public name of linecaster.engines.api and linecaster.testing:

  • Summary line: what the block or function does, in the present tense, starting with a verb, one sentence: "Recognizes the text of every line with its engine." It may wrap; it ends at the first blank line. The block index and the README's block table show it.
  • Body: the contract in words (what it reads, adds and replaces), edge cases, what it records (step infos, stats, errors on the page).
  • Args: names every parameter of the signature (a class documents its constructor's), and no other: one entry each, name: meaning, the effect of the default, constraints., continuation lines indented. Several parameters may share an entry (data_folder, paths_file, ...: datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments.), as datatrove's inherited reader and writer arguments do; **kwargs is an entry too. A class that keeps its base's constructor keeps its base's Args:.
  • Example: (indented Python code) is required for runtime.run.main, build(), the serializers (to_alto, from_alto, ...) and the public functions of linecaster.catalog; optional for blocks, whose generated pages show it.
  • Inline code in double or single backticks; the generated pages render both as code. Engine options are described in their Options model (Field(description=...)), not in a docstring.

Reason: the generated block pages and tables come from the docstrings, so the reference is only as good as they are, and a test keeps them complete as signatures change.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
• Every block declares its unit and what it reads, adds and replaces (pipelines). A part of the record is added by one block only, unless a later block declares that it replaces it. Reason: the builder can then check a pipeline before it runs and derive its graph.
  • Blocks are pure transforms of their unit; only readers and writers know about tasks, ranks and files. Reason: the same blocks run on any executor and in run_pages().

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Every built-in engine passes linecaster.testing.check_engine and every public block check_block (tests/testing/test_conformance.py); an engine package checks its engines the same way in engines/<engine>/tests/. Reason: the protocol and the contracts hold for every implementation, not only the ones a pipeline happens to run.
  • A test that needs a CUDA device is marked gpu, one that downloads weights or reaches the internet network, one over about 10 s slow, one that compares against the goldens parity (--strict-markers). Reason: the default run skips what a machine cannot run, and CI runs what a CPU can.
  • Tests use the fake engines, the fake chat server and the fake service of linecaster.testing, not copies of their own. Reason: one fake per step behaves the same in every test.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
• Tracing (OpenTelemetry) is always on. Spans per task always; spans per page for a sample chosen by page id, plus every page that failed. Reason: where a run loses time is only visible per page and across processes.
  • A page carries its trace context from the reader on; blocks open spans as children of the page's context, never of "the current span". Reason: pages are interleaved in the stream.
  • Attributes are identifiers and numbers under linecaster.*, never content (text, images). Reason: content belongs in the rows, which the page id links to.
  • Traces are written to OUT/traces/ and, when the standard OTEL_* variables are set, exported to a backend (tracing).

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: linecaster sends nothing to anyone that the user did not configure. No usage data, no phoning home, not even opt-in. Reason: libraries and archives run it on their own infrastructure under their own rules.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: loguru (datatrove's), with {placeholder} templates and named values, never formatted strings: logger.warning("page {page_id} failed in {block}: {error}", page_id=..., block=..., error=...) (the values land in the record's extra). JSON lines on Jobs: the pipeline scripts set LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1 in their Jobs, where the tasks (linecaster.runtime.jobs.JobsExecutor) and linecaster serve log with loguru's serialize=True (linecaster.runtime.logs). Log records carry trace_id and span_id. Reason: logs can be filtered and joined to traces.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Library code raises the classes of linecaster.errors (PipelineConfigError, CatalogError, PageError, ServerError, all LinecasterError), never SystemExit; only the command line (linecaster, a pipeline script's main) turns them into exit codes, and a test fails on any other exit. Pure functions of the data model, the formats and the text transforms keep Python's own ValueError for a wrong argument. Reason: a derivative that embeds linecaster can catch what went wrong, and a run's exit code says whether anything was launched.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: A credential is never a value in a pipeline: it is an EnvVar("NAME") (linecaster.runtime.secrets), read in the task. Reason: datatrove pickles the pipeline for every executor, and the run record lists every block's parameters.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text: CHANGELOG.md in the Keep a Changelog format, with upgrade notes first. NOTES.md is the log of measurements and decisions; reference documents (docs/reference/) describe what is, without history.

docs.title: The data model
docs.text: linecaster.data holds what a page's text recognition produces; linecaster.data.page the page record it travels in. Importing either needs neither datatrove nor saturate nor an engine.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Is Key Item any multi-page unit: book, issue, manuscript, file item_id Page one page record: the page image and its named transcriptions page_id = item_id + sequence PageImage the image's location, size, format and hashes Transcription OCR, HTR or ground truth of one page Text one text per item and variant (linecaster.text.variants)

docs.title: A page in a pipeline
docs.text: A page is one datatrove Document: id is the page id, text the primary transcription's text, media[0] the image bytes, metadata["page"] the page record.

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text:
Part Holds regions the layout: id, label (a DoclingDocument label), raw_label (the producer's), polygon, bbox, score, reading_order, heading_level, extra lines id, region_id, reading_order, row, bbox, polygon, baseline, score, text, normalized, confidence, alternatives, words, extra paragraphs the running text recomposed from the rows (Paragraph, below), in reading order docling the page's composed DoclingDocument, as docling-core dumps it language steps one StepInfo per step that worked on it, in order (below) source kind (produced, converted, ground_truth), format, uri, image size derived text (as written, as laid out, full page; tables as Markdown), confidence (line confidences weighted by length)
  • regions are the contract between steps. Lines and recognizers need the layout (label, polygon, reading order, score) long before a DoclingDocument can be built, so regions are a primary part next to lines; docling is composed from regions, lines and tables. Region ids are the producer's own (PP-DocLayout: <raw label>_<index>; rows outside every region: orphan_<n>); lines refer to them with region_id.
  • Words are the finest level; there is no glyph level. Engines with character positions turn them into words by the engine's own rule (kraken: split at whitespace, a word's box the bounding box of its cuts).
  • A line's text is None until a recognizer ran; an empty string is a line recognized as empty. Its normalized is None until the CharacterNormalizer ran; text is never overwritten.
  • Text-only transcriptions (a delivered plain text) are lines without geometry (bbox and polygon None), one per text line, source.kind = "converted", source.format = "text". They cannot be written as ALTO, PAGE or hOCR.

docs.title: Steps (StepInfo)
docs.text:
Every step that worked on a transcription adds one StepInfo, model steps and rule-based steps alike:

Field Holds step the step: layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, unicode, typography, recomposition, normalization, composition, ... name the model (kraken-ppocrv6-medium, PP-DocLayoutV3); for a step without a model, what ran (unicodedata, retyper, the engine's id) engine the engine's code id (kraken.recognition.v1, typography.ratios.v1); None for a step no engine ran (unicode) revision the model's revision preset, preset_sha256 the preset edition it ran as, and its hash recipe, recipe_sha256 the recipe edition the run followed, and its hash (RecipeStamper) backend in-process, or served with the server's address settings what decided the output besides the preset: the engine's options, a VLM's prompt and sampling measurements numbers of this page, in the measurements vocabulary (below)

The model blocks and linecaster serve fill engine from the engine's engine_id, preset from the backend, and seconds and datetime. The page files (ALTO, PAGE, hOCR) carry every field but measurements (datetime aside) and read them back (serialization).

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS is the vocabulary of StepInfo.measurements, key → meaning; linecaster code writes no other key (a test reads the code for every place that writes one). Values vary from run to run.

Key Meaning seconds wall time of the step on the page (the engine's call, in-process or in the server) datetime when the step started on the page, ISO 8601 in UTC device the device the step ran on prompt_tokens, completion_tokens a VLM's tokens, summed over the page's requests finish_reason why generation stopped: stop, length, content_filter, tool_calls, function_call, abort (FINISH_REASONS), or None regions, failed regions sent to a VLM one by one, and those whose request failed tables, formulas table regions given a structure, formula regions read changed strings a normalization changed body_size, leveled, demoted, split, drop_capitals, numbers_dropped typography: the body type size in pixels, headings given a level, section headers made text, headlines split off, drop capitals joined, page numbers removed paragraphs, continuations, marks_removed, marks_kept recomposition: paragraphs made, paragraphs continued into the next region or page, division marks removed, hyphens kept

A new key is added to the vocabulary before code writes it. Page records of other producers are read with whatever keys they carry (unknown_measurements lists them).

docs.title: Paragraphs (Paragraph)
docs.text:
Running text recomposed from the rows of one region (the Recomposer), with the decisions that made it.

Field Holds id, region_id <region id>_p<n>, and the region rows one ParagraphRow per visual row with text: lines (the ids of every line on the row, as Line.row groups them, empty ones too) and start, end (the row's characters in text) text as written, flowed: the rows joined, the division marks the recomposition removed gone normalized the same text normalized (the CharacterNormalizer), else None continues, continues_from the paragraph it runs on into, and the one it continues (ParagraphRef: id, and page_id for a paragraph on another page of the item) decisions Decisions: kind and reason (DECISIONS), row (the index into rows), separator (for a continuation: what joins it to the paragraph it runs on into)

The rows are what a document's provenance needs: an item made from a paragraph has one provenance entry per row, whose box is the union of the row's lines' boxes (derived from their polygons, geometry.bbox_of) and whose charspan is start, end, shifted by the text before it when the item continues a paragraph of an earlier region or page. Rows without text belong to no paragraph; text-only transcriptions have rows without boxes (each line a row of its own, a region one paragraph; a page without regions is one region).

Decision kind Reasons mark_removed letter_follows: the next row starts with a lowercase or caseless letter hyphen_kept capital_follows, digit_follows, no_letter_follows, script_change (a mark after a Hebrew letter before a row in another script), attested (the document has the hyphenated form and not the joined one) paragraph_break indent, gap (about a blank line), short_row (justified text: the row before stopped short of the end margin) continuation division_mark, end_margin (the last row reaches the end margin), without sentence-final punctuation

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text: Every bbox is [x, y, width, height] in pixels of the received image. Polygons and baselines are float lists exactly as the engine returned them. Algorithms derive boxes from the polygon (geometry.bbox_of), so their arithmetic matches the engine's (no x + width rounding). Transcription.scaled(sx, sy) moves every coordinate to another image size.

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
• Processing order is the list order of Transcription.lines after the line steps: regions in the layout step's order, orphan rows last, rows within each region. A recognizer processes and batches lines in this order.
  • Reading order is separate: reading_order ranks the lines on the page (regions by their reading order, then rows); row is the visual row within a region.

docs.title: Unicode
docs.text: The as-written layer is NFC, made by a step of its own: UnicodeNormalizer (linecaster.text.unicode) right after recognition, recorded as StepInfo(step="unicode", name="unicodedata", settings={"form": "NFC", "unicode_version": ...}). Each engine's raw output stays exactly what the engine produced. Only canonical forms (NFC, NFD) are allowed; never NFKC, whose folding is the readable variants' job (linecaster.text.variants).

docs.title: Typography (linecaster.text.typography)
docs.text:
The retyper edits regions and lines in place:

  • A split-off headline is region <region id>_head (raw label <raw>/split); its lines keep their ids and get the new region_id.
  • Removed regions (drop capitals, uncertain page numbers) leave regions with their lines and are recorded in Transcription.extra["retyper_dropped"] (id, labels, text, line ids, reason, confidence).
  • A drop capital's letter is prepended to the target line's text (line.extra["drop_capital"]); words are not touched.
  • Regions are re-ranked and lines re-ordered afterwards.

docs.title: Documents (linecaster.formats.docling)
docs.text:
• Page composition (Composer, DocumentBuilder): docling from regions, paragraphs or lines, and tables; page headers and footers always in Docling's furniture layer. Exports choose whether to include them (furniture=True). A text region with paragraphs (a Recomposer ran) is one item per paragraph, one provenance entry per row; a paragraph that continues another (continues_from) is appended to that one's item, its rows' character spans after the text before it (a division mark removed at the continuation stays in the span of the row it ended, as squiddleocr's builder had it); a region of one paragraph without a letter (a page number) is an item of its own. Without paragraphs a text region is one item, one row per line, with the region's box (diplomatic composition).
  • Item composition (Composer(unit="item"), DocumentBuilder): an item's pages composed into one DoclingDocument whose page n is the item's n-th page (by sequence, then page id). Recomposed as an item (a Recomposer(unit="item") before it), paragraphs continue across page breaks; sections are optional (options={"sections": True}); region_of (item ref → "<page_no>:<region id>") travels with the document for Markdown dividers.

docs.title: Item records (linecaster.blocks.base.item)
docs.text: An item travels as one datatrove Document: id is the item id, metadata["item"] the item record, {"item_id": ..., "pages": [...]}, its page records (as JSON-compatible dicts) in order (sequence, then page id), without the image bytes. The Binder makes it from a page stream (gather: an item is complete when its metadata["item_page_count"] pages have arrived, or when the input ends; a task must see whole items, so the run layout buckets page records by item, and with several tasks the builder writes them in item shards first). The item-unit blocks change the page records inside it: Recomposer(unit="item") (the paragraphs of the whole item, a ParagraphRef.page_id naming the other page of a continuation), CharacterNormalizer(unit="item") (normalized), Composer(unit="item") (the item's document next to the record: metadata["docling"], ["region_of"], ["item_id"]; text its plain text). The ItemTextWriter renders the text variants from it, the ItemDocumentWriter writes the document's exports, and the Splitter passes its pages on as page documents again, each with what the item-level blocks added.

docs.title: Text variants (linecaster.text.variants)
docs.text:
The vocabulary is era-neutral, on three independent dimensions: character fidelity (as written, normalized, expanded, regularized), flow (as laid out, flowed) and scope (full page, body only). Each transform moves one step on one dimension; the as-written layer is never overwritten. All text is NFC; the normalization folds ſ, ligatures, r rotunda and superscript e over a, o, u by an explicit mapping table, and keeps æ, œ, ø, å and ß; never NFKC; spelling is never modernized.

Three variants per item:

Variant Made from verbatim_txt as written, as laid out, full page: each page's Transcription.text (lines in reading order, tables as Markdown or HTML tables), pages joined with a form feed readable_txt normalized, flowed, body only: the item recomposition's paragraphs (Paragraph.normalized; a paragraph continued from another, also across a page break, appended to it with the continuation's separator), tables one row per line with tab-separated cells (each cell's normalized), a formula region's LaTeX; page headers, page footers, pictures and charts left out readable_md the same as Markdown: # title, ## section header (by heading level), - list item, tables as pipe tables (HTML when a cell spans)

The normalization engine (normalization.latin-historic.v1) sets normalized on every line, paragraph and table cell (Region.extra["table"]["cells"][i]["normalized"]); the as-written texts stay.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The terms linecaster uses, one meaning each. Where a word means something else elsewhere (in datatrove, Haystack, everyday use), the not column says so. Code, docs and commit messages use these terms and no others; a new term is added here before it is used.

docs.title: Running things
docs.text: Term Meaning Not block One processing unit of a pipeline: a datatrove PipelineStep. Blocks are named as role nouns (LineRecognizer, Composer, PageJsonlWriter). not a "step" (that is a catalog term), not a "component", not a "module" role What a block does, defined by its contract; implementations and strategies of one role are interchangeable. family A group of roles of one kind: readers, layout, lines, recognition, conversion, text, composition, binding, validation, servers, writers, composites. One subpackage of linecaster.blocks each. contract What a block reads, adds, replaces and removes in the page record (or item record), and its unit. The builder checks contracts before a run. not a Python type signature part One named piece of the page record (or item record) a contract names: page-level (image, metadata), or of one transcription (ocr_new:lines); the vocabulary is PARTS (below). not a datatrove Document field unit What one call of a block or engine processes: line, region, page or item. per-unit transform, stream transform The two shapes of a block: a per-unit transform processes one unit per call and its base class owns the loop; a stream transform takes the whole stream and passes each unit on when it is done, possibly out of order (served model blocks). condition A picklable predicate on the page record with a describe(); a block with one (when=) processes only the pages it accepts, the others pass unchanged. Blocks sharing a group are alternatives: each page goes through one of them. composite block A named group of blocks with its own outward contract (e.g. ModularTranscriber). The builder expands it into its blocks. pipeline An ordered list of blocks that a stream of pages (or items) passes through, run by an executor. datatrove's sense. not a graph of components as in Haystack graph The dependencies between a pipeline's blocks, derived from their contracts by the builder: for checking, drawing, and cutting into stages. It is not executed as a graph. builder The code that turns a pipeline definition into stages: derives the graph, checks it, expands composites, cuts it at unit changes. stage One datatrove pipeline run as part of a longer computation; stages run one after another and hand over through files (e.g. page records written in item shards, read by the next stage). not a "phase" pipeline script A self-contained uv script in pipelines/ (PEP 723 metadata, a lock next to it) that builds one pipeline shape and runs it on every executor. Named as a verb: harvest.py, transcribe_modular.py, transcribe_vlm.py, bind.py. pipeline id A pipeline script's versioned id, its file name plus .v<n>: transcribe_modular.v1. Recipes name the pipeline they run by it. workflow The sequence of pipeline scripts for a collection: harvest → transcribe → bind. not one pipeline; not a GitHub Actions workflow (say "CI workflow" for that) executor, job, task, worker, shard datatrove's terms: the executor runs a pipeline as tasks; a job is one launch (one HF Job, one Slurm job); a task is one unit of work with its own rank; workers are tasks running at once; a shard is the part of the input one task reads. item shard A folder of page records holding every page of a set of items, so that a later stage reads whole items. not a datatrove shard backend Where a model block's engine runs: in-process, served (a server reached through saturate), or chat (an OpenAI-compatible VLM server). not the executor server A process that hosts models: linecaster serve for engines, vLLM or SGLang for VLMs, a service for a page engine. Started by the server blocks ModelServer, ChatModelServer and ServiceServer, which go last in a pipeline. service The server a page engine talks to that is neither linecaster serve nor a chat server: a vendor's page pipeline behind its own HTTP API, in the vendor's image (Falcon-OCR, OXR-1.0), or the vLLM a vendor's package attaches to (surya-ocr). A page preset's serve block names it; ServiceServer starts it. not an operating-system service observer A callback at block boundaries (before and after a unit): taps, sampling, progress, tracing. not a Haystack "hook" boundary step The step the builder puts after a block when a stage has observers: it tells them that each unit left that block and entered the next. It adds no stats. not a block tap An observer that writes the page records as they pass a given block (--tap-after). partial run A run of part of a pipeline: up to a block (--until), or from page records after one (--after). run folder The output folder of a run (OUT): pages/ (the page records), rejects/, logs/, traces/, run.yaml, and the files the writers produce. run record OUT/run.yaml: the pipeline as run (every block's parameters, to_dict()), the recipe, the command line, the executor and the software, with pipeline_sha256 (the hash of the functional parameters). reject A page that failed a check or a step, written to rejects/ with the reason; it stays in the page records with its errors. warm-up What a block loads before its first unit (warm_up()): an engine, a server, a client's secrets. Timed as its own stat. error budget The share of a task's pages a block may fail on before the task fails (--max-page-errors, default 1 % of at least 100 pages). functional parameter, operational parameter A block parameter that can change what a run writes (functional), or only where things are and how the work runs (operational: folders, ports, endpoints, windows, worker counts). pipeline_sha256 covers the functional ones. describe mode Building a pipeline script's blocks in the current process without its engines, for its description and hash (describe_script). not --dry-run, which runs in the script's environment secret reference EnvVar("NAME"): a credential named by its environment variable, read in the task, never stored in a pipeline or a record. trace, span OpenTelemetry's terms: a trace is one page's (or one task's) path through a run, made of spans, one per operation, with times and attributes. not telemetry sample The pages that are traced: a fixed share chosen by page id, plus every page that failed. trace context A page's W3C traceparent (doc.metadata["trace"]), given at the reader's boundary: the page's spans are its children, and a served block sends it with the page's request. not "the current span" task span A span of the task's own work, traced for every task: the task, a block's warm-up, a server start, a reader's file, a writer's flush. gap The time a block had no page in it between its first page and its last: it waited for its input (linecaster traces).

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
What contracts name besides the parts presets produce (PRODUCES in linecaster.catalog.schema: regions, reading_order, lines, baselines, text, words, ...); PARTS holds them all.

Part Meaning image The page image's bytes, as the reader brought them (page-level). metadata The page record's own fields: ids, sequence, the image's record, the metadata (page-level). transcription_file A library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a file's bytes (a document media: ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text; page-level); the TranscriptionConverter reads it into a transcription. line_regions Lines assigned to the layout regions and ordered within them (the LineAssigner). hierarchy Heading levels, headline splits and drop capitals (the Typographer). nfc The as-written layer in one Unicode normalization form (the UnicodeNormalizer). paragraphs The running text recomposed from the rows, with its decisions (the Recomposer). normalized The normalized texts of lines and paragraphs (the CharacterNormalizer). document The DoclingDocument of a page (the Composer) or of an item (Composer(unit="item")).

docs.title: The catalog
docs.text: Term Meaning Not catalog linecaster's register of models, engines, presets, recipes and evidence, in src/linecaster/catalog/data/. catalog entry One registered thing: a model, a preset, a recipe or an evidence record; a YAML file, with a Markdown sidecar for its prose. not a "component", not a "document" step A catalog step: what an engine does, e.g. layout, lines, recognition, tables, formulas, image, normalization, typography, recomposition, composition. A preset belongs to one step. not a block engine Code with a versioned id (kraken.recognition.v1, recomposition.unicode.v1) that implements one step: a class with Options, capabilities, load() and a call per unit. Built-in engines live in the core; engine packages (linecaster-kraken, ...) add more. not saturate's Engine class (its server launcher) strategy An engine of a rule-based step (normalization, typography, recomposition, composition, image). A strategy declares the scripts it covers. script A writing system, named by its ISO 15924 code (Latn, Hebr, Arab): Unicode's Script property. A by-script engine routes each decision to the strategy for the script around it; * stands for every script. not a pipeline script model An upstream artifact with weights (or learned data such as hyphenation patterns), pinned by revision, with its upstream card copied verbatim. not an engine, not a preset, not a VLM adapter preset A named configuration of one engine for one step: engine id, options, capabilities, and the model it loads if any. Referred to as id@edition. page preset A preset whose unit is page: one model reads the whole page (a VLM, or a page engine). launch.py can run one directly. not "a model" page engine An engine of the recognition step whose unit is the page: it reads the whole page and returns its transcription, in the pipeline's process or behind a server (indra.recognition.v1, surya.recognition.v1, and the clients of a vendor's service, falcon.recognition.v1, oxr.recognition.v1). PageRecognizer runs it. not a chat preset (chat.v1) recipe A tested combination: a pipeline id, a preset edition per slot, and options, with whole-run evidence. slot A place in a pipeline script that a preset fills; its name is the step's (--layout, --lines, --recognition, ...). adapter The code that talks to one VLM family over the OpenAI-compatible API: its request, its prompt handling, its parsing (linecaster.adapters). not an engine package evidence A measurement with its source (own run, leaderboard, model card, vendor benchmark), stored as an evidence record. version Upstream's name for a release of a model (v6, 3.5). not an edition revision The exact upstream commit a model is pinned to. edition linecaster's release number of a preset or recipe: kraken-ppocrv6-medium@1. A released edition never changes; its hash covers its YAML. not a version code id The versioned id of an engine or a pipeline: <name>.v<n>. An option added later keeps the id if its default keeps the old behavior. schema id The format of a YAML file: linecaster.preset/1. lock catalog.lock: the hash of every released edition, and the expanded pipeline of every recipe edition.

docs.title: Pages, items and text
docs.text: Term Meaning Not item Any multi-page unit: a book, an issue, a manuscript, a file. Key item_id. not "book" in generic code, flags or docs page One page of an item, with its image and its named transcriptions. page_id is <item_id>_<sequence:04d> unless the source has stable ids of its own. not the step page (there is none) page record A page with its image reference, its transcriptions and its metadata (Page): what a block reads and adds to while the page passes, and what is stored in OUT/pages/ as JSONL or Parquet (everything but the image bytes). not a "page row" item record An item with its pages in order, as the Binder passes it on (doc.metadata["item"], linecaster.blocks.base.item); the item-unit Recomposer, CharacterNormalizer and Composer read it, the item writers write from it, the Splitter turns it back into pages. manifest An item's list of its pages and their files, in order: an IIIF Presentation manifest or a METS document (also inside OAI-PMH). not a BagIt checksum manifest page image The image a page's coordinates refer to (PageImage): its URI, format, size, hash. working image The working-image preset of the ImageConverter: lossless WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB. not a role transcription Everything read from a page by one source (Transcription): regions, lines, words, paragraphs, the document, the steps that made it, and its source.
