Named per page: ocr_new (linecaster's), ocr_original (the library's own), ground_truth. not "OCR" (it also holds HTR and ground truth) region An area of a page with a label (text, title, table, ...) from layout. line One printed or written line: its geometry and, once recognized, its text and words. row The lines of one region that sit side by side at the same height (Line.row), as in typesetting; detection often splits one printed line into several lines on the same row. never a stored record word The finest unit: its text, box and confidence. linecaster has no glyph level. paragraph Running text recomposed from a region's rows, with the decisions that made it. Added by the Recomposer. document A DoclingDocument: the composed structure of a page or an item. Added by the Composer. not a datatrove Document (say "datatrove document"), not a catalog entry step info One entry per step that worked on a transcription (StepInfo): step, engine, preset edition, backend, settings, measurements. measurements Numbers a step records for a page: seconds, tokens, device, finish_reason, in a fixed vocabulary. not trace attributes text variant A named point on the three text dimensions, written per item: verbatim_txt, readable_txt, readable_md. not a "version" character fidelity, flow, scope The three text dimensions: as written → normalized (fidelity); as laid out → flowed (flow); full page → body only (scope). Each transform moves one step on one dimension. not "axes" composition Building a document from regions and paragraphs (the Composer). not "assembly" recomposition Turning lines back into running text: paragraphs, removed division marks, separators, continuation (the Recomposer). not "reflow" (the old name) binding Gathering an item's pages in order into one item (the Binder). splitting Passing an item record's pages on as pages again, with what the item-level steps added (the Splitter). division mark A hyphen the typesetter added where a word was divided at a line end. not a hyphen that belongs to the word decision One choice a recomposition made at a row end, with its reason from a fixed vocabulary: a division mark removed, a hyphen kept, a paragraph break, a continuation. Recorded on the paragraph.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Term Meaning Not engine API What an engine package may import from linecaster besides the data model: linecaster.engines.api (the Engine protocol, Capabilities, the weight helpers). not the HTTP routes of linecaster serve fake engine A deterministic CPU engine of linecaster.testing for tests, one per model step, registered under fake.<step>.v1 by register_fakes() only. never in a catalog preset conformance check check_engine (the engine protocol) or check_block (a block's contract against what it does, its to_dict(), pickling, warm_up() and failed pages), from linecaster.testing. not a parity check marker A pytest marker of linecaster's tests: gpu, network, slow, parity. Tests marked gpu or network skip where the device or the network is missing. CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml: the core's tests and checks on a CPU, on every push and pull request to main. not a workflow

docs.title: Docs and changes
docs.text: Term Meaning Not derivative A project built on linecaster: its own pipelines, blocks or engines (squiddleocr, the EBDC pilot pipeline, the FineBooks pipelines). not a fork generated docs The files linecaster docs writes from code, docstrings and the catalog: the catalog's and the blocks' pages, the README's tables between their markers, the site's index and llms.txt. Never edited by hand; --check fails when one is not current. not the reference docs (docs/reference/, hand-written) block page The generated page of one block (docs/blocks/<family>/<Block>.md): its contract, backends, catalog step and presets, position, options, behavior and example. breaking change A change after which code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference that worked before stops working or means something else (compatibility). upgrade note The entry in CHANGELOG.md for a breaking change: what changed, who is affected, what to do.

docs.title: The print shop
docs.text:
The block names follow the roles of a hot-metal print shop, in the order they work. linecaster makes a new, digital edition of a printed item:

Print shop linecaster Does the linecaster (casts whole lines) LineRecognizer casts the lines anew, as text typographer Typographer determines the hierarchy: headings and their levels, initials, what is text at all compositor Recomposer, Composer recomposes the running text; makes up the page or item document binder Binder binds the pages into the item (the Splitter takes them apart again)

docs.title: Pipelines: contracts and the builder
docs.text: A pipeline is a list of blocks (datatrove PipelineSteps) and composites. Before it runs, the builder (linecaster.runtime.builder) checks the blocks' contracts, expands the composites, and cuts the pipeline into stages. Every pipeline script goes through it (linecaster.runtime.run). Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Every block returns its contract from contract() (linecaster.blocks.base.contract):

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Part:
    name: str                  # a name of PARTS, or "*" (every part)
    transcription: str | None  # ocr_new, ocr_original, ...; None: page-level (image, metadata, transcription_file)
                               # or the item record's

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Contract:
    unit: str                  # "page", "item" (what the input stream carries) or "any" (servers)
    unit_out: str | None       # set when the block changes the stream's unit (binder: page -> item, splitter: back)
    reads: frozenset[Part]
    adds: frozenset[Part]
    replaces: frozenset[Part]
    removes: frozenset[Part]   # parts the block does not pass on (gone for every later block)
    role: str                  # reader, writer, server, model, transform, binder, splitter, validator, composite
  • The vocabulary is PARTS in linecaster.catalog.schema: image, metadata and transcription_file (a library's own transcription delivered with the page, as a document media) (page-level), what presets produce (PRODUCES: regions, reading_order, lines, baselines, text, words, word_confidences, line_confidences, tables, formulas, markdown, html, doctags, layout_json, latex), and line_regions, hierarchy, nfc, document. A part is written transcription:name (ocr_new:lines); ocr_original:* is every part of a transcription.
  • Simple blocks declare class attributes (unit, role, parts_read, parts_added, parts_replaced, parts_removed) that the default contract() of Contracted reads; page-level names stay page-level, the others belong to the block's transcription. Blocks whose parts depend on their options compute contract().
  • Model blocks read the page image (recognition also lines, tables and formulas regions) and add their preset's capabilities.produces: the preset of the InProcess backend (preset), of the Served backend (preset, set by runtime.run.engines) or of the Chat backend; without a preset the engine class's capabilities (read from its source in the repository, else from the class); without either the step's default. The chat recognizers add text too, RegionRecognizer also lines (and replaces lines and text: the transcription's earlier lines are replaced).
  • Readers add image and metadata; ManifestReader(existing_ocr=True) also transcription_file, which the TranscriptionConverter reads (adding ocr_original:*); PageRecordReader what provides= declares (["ocr_new:lines", ...]), or anything (*, reads after it are not checked) when it declares nothing. With fetch_images=False it brings no image.
  • Writers read what they write and add nothing (ImageFilesWriter replaces metadata: the image's URI then names its copy; PageFileWriter: lines for hOCR, ALTO and PAGE, text for md and txt, document for HTML, DocLang and JSON, image for plots). Servers have role server and unit any.
  • The Binder changes the unit from pages to items, the Splitter back: an item record holds its page records, so what the pages carried stays available across either (the checks carry the parts over), apart from the page image's bytes (image: an item record has none) at the binder and the item's document at the splitter.
  • Item-unit blocks (Recomposer(unit="item"), CharacterNormalizer(unit="item"), Composer(unit="item")) read item records: one datatrove document per item, doc.metadata["item"] holding the item id and its page records in order (linecaster.blocks.base.item); they read and add the parts of the pages' transcriptions, the item Composer adds the item's document next to the record. Item writers: ItemTextWriter reads lines for verbatim_txt and paragraphs and normalized for the readable variants, ItemDocumentWriter the document. RecipeStamper has unit any: before an item writer it stamps the pages of each item record.
  • A step without a contract (a plain datatrove step) passes pages and touches no part.
Block Reads Adds Replaces, removes LineAssigner lines, regions line_regions regions, reading_order, lines UnicodeNormalizer text nfc text CharacterNormalizer text normalized Typographer regions, lines hierarchy regions, lines Recomposer regions, lines paragraphs paragraphs (made anew where they exist) Composer regions, lines (and paragraphs when there are) document ImageFetcher metadata image ImageConverter metadata metadata (with keep_bytes also image; without it removes image) TranscriptionConverter metadata, transcription_file (with source="media") <transcription>:* RecipeStamper

docs.title: Block shapes
docs.text:
• Per-unit transform (shape = "unit"): process_page(doc, page) -> page | None; PageBlock owns the loop and the stats. In-process model blocks have this shape.
  • Stream transform (shape = "stream"): overrides run(data) and yields each page when it is done, possibly out of order (served model blocks, PageRecognizer, RegionRecognizer). It reports what happens to each page inside it with notify(doc, event): prepare when a request is built, done when its result came back. The served model blocks share one streaming loop (ModelBlock): a block names its requests (_rows: one per page, one per region for RegionRecognizer), builds and parses each (_request, _parse) and says which pages a finished one completes (_done).
  • Only readers and writers see rank, world_size and files (a test walks every block class, with no exceptions): a block that rejects a page records why on the page, and the RejectWriter names the task's file.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text:
A model block's backend (linecaster.backends) says where its engine runs:

  • InProcess("pkg:Class", **options) (or InProcess.from_preset(ref); a model block given a preset ref, LayoutDetector("single-region@1"), builds one): the engine loads in the worker;
  • Served(endpoint, model=name, ...): linecaster serve (or a server speaking its routes) hosts it, reached through saturate on /v1/linecaster/{step};
  • Chat(preset, endpoint=None, served_name=None, max_window=32, initial_window=4, read_timeout=600.0, api_key=None, headers=None, prefer="page"): a chat preset's VLM behind an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, a hosted endpoint) on /v1/chat/completions; preset is a preset ref, a model's Hugging Face id (its preset with unit prefer) or a configured adapter (chat_model); without an endpoint, the task's ChatModelServer on port 8000. PageRecognizer(backend) and RegionRecognizer(backend, labels=..., pad=None) (pad: the adapter's region_pad, else 8) take it (or a chat preset's ref). PageRecognizer also takes a page engine's InProcess or Served backend (or its preset's ref): a stream transform served, a per-unit transform in-process; it reads the page image and adds text and what the preset produces. A page engine's endpoint option (where its service is) is operational.

The built-in engines (layout.single-region.v1 and the rule-based steps') run in the pipeline's process only: runtime.run.engines keeps a preset of one in-process when the other models are served, and linecaster serve refuses them.

docs.title: The builder
docs.text:
plan = build(blocks, tasks=8, until=None, after=None, taps={"LineAssigner": "OUT/taps/lines"},
             run_folder="OUT", recipe=("squiddle@1", "sha256:..."))
plan.check()          # PipelineConfigError listing every problem
plan.stages           # [Stage(name, tasks, blocks, pipeline)]: one datatrove pipeline each, run in order
plan.graph            # nodes (blocks; composites expanded, their group kept), edges (part -> the block reading it)
plan.mermaid()        # the graph as a Mermaid flowchart: stages and composites as subgraphs
plan.describe()       # stages with each block's contract, the edges, the problems

Checks, all collected: a stage starts with a reader; every part a block reads is added earlier in its stage (or by the stage's reader) and not removed since (removes, even after a reader that provides anything); a part is added by one block only, unless a later block declares it in replaces; units fit (a page block cannot follow an item stream, an item block needs a binder before it); the parts carry across a binder and a splitter (apart from image and the item's document); server blocks go last; a served model block whose endpoint is a server block of its stage (same loopback port) finds its model in that server's list; the alternatives of a group add the same parts, sit next to each other, each with a condition, OTHERWISE last; names given to until, after and taps fit exactly one block.

Order is the given one; the builder checks it and does not reorder. It inserts a TranscriptionConverter (into ocr_original) right after a block that adds transcription_file when no later block reads it, the RecipeStamper before the first writer when the run follows a recipe, a RejectWriter into <run_folder>/rejects before the first writer (or binder) when there is a run folder and the pipeline has none, and moves the server blocks at the end into the stage of the model blocks when it cuts. build(..., max_page_errors=SHARE) sets every page block's error budget.

Branches: branch(block, when=Condition, group=None) gives a block a condition, a picklable predicate on the page record with a describe() (MetadataEquals(key, value), OTHERWISE). The block processes the pages the condition accepts; the others pass unchanged. Blocks with the same group are alternatives: each page goes through the first one whose condition accepts it. A per-unit block gets its pages one by one; any other block one stream of them, the pages it does not take passed on as it yields.

Composites: Composite(name, blocks, contract=None) expands into its blocks (nested composites too); its outward contract is derived (what its blocks read that none of them adds, what they add and replace) unless given. ModularTranscriber(lines, recognition, layout, formulas_separately=False, transcription="ocr_new") is layout ("single-region@1": the page as one region) → lines → line assignment → line recognition; each step a block, a backend or a preset.

Stages: with tasks > 1, the first binder (a block whose stream changes from pages to items) cuts the pipeline, unless the reader already gives each task whole items (ManifestReader, PageRecordReader(item_shards= True)). The first stage writes its page records in item shards into <run_folder>/pages/ (the pipeline's own PageJsonlWriter there, now with item_shards=N, N = tasks unless it set its own); the second starts with PageRecordReader(item_shards=True, fetch_images=False) declaring the parts the first stage added, runs the binder and what follows, as N tasks. A Splitter after the binder needs no cut of its own: the items are whole in the task, so its pages are too. One stage logs to OUT/logs/, two to OUT/logs/pages/ and OUT/logs/items/; the run record lists the stages. Each stage gets its own executor, and the later one depends= on the earlier one:

--on Executors Stages local LocalPipelineExecutor the second starts when the first is complete ray RayGPUExecutor for stages with servers, RayPipelineExecutor for the item stage the same, through depends= hf-jobs JobsExecutor (datatrove's JobsPipelineExecutor with JSON-lines logs; GPUJobsExecutor for multi-GPU flavors on stages with servers) consecutive launches: the second launches when the first's Jobs are complete; both on --flavor

Partial runs (blocks named by their datatrove name, their class name, or a composite's name for its last block):

  • until=BLOCK (--until): the blocks up to and including BLOCK, then a PageJsonlWriter into <run_folder>/pages (and the server blocks);
  • after=BLOCK (--after, with --pages DIR): the pipeline's PageRecordReader, then the blocks after BLOCK; the reader declares the parts the blocks up to BLOCK add;
  • taps={BLOCK: DIR} (--tap-after BLOCK DIR, repeatable): a Tap observer writes every page record as it leaves BLOCK into DIR/<rank>.jsonl.gz.

In this process: run_pages(blocks, docs) checks the blocks and runs them on docs (datatrove documents) as task 0 of 1, without an executor (a leading reader reads its own input after them); run_plan(plan) runs a plan's stages that way. A pipeline script's --page IMAGE OUT runs its pipeline on one image like that, and linecaster page IMAGE OUT [--recipe R | --pipeline ID] [pipeline options] finds the script (the recipe's pipeline, else transcribe_modular.v1) and runs it so.

--dry-run prints the plan (describe() under plan, with the run record) and the Mermaid graph, and fails like a run would when there are problems; a run with problems exits with code 2 before it writes anything.

docs.title: Observers
docs.text:
linecaster.runtime.observers.Observer has on_task_start(rank, world_size), on_warm_up(block, seconds), on_enter(block, doc), on_exit(block, doc, error=None), on_unit(block, doc, event, **attributes) (from stream blocks' notify: prepare and request in saturate's prepare threads, request with a carrier dict for the trace context, done with error, tokens and finish_reason; region for a request per region), on_task_event(block, event, start_ns, end_ns, **attributes) (from Block.report: a reader's file, a writer's flush), on_leave(doc) (a page leaves the stage's last block), on_task_end(error=None) (also when the task fails) and environment() (variables for a server a block starts in the task). When a stage has observers (build(..., observers=[...]), taps, tracing), the builder puts a Boundary after every block: the boundary between block i and i + 1 calls on_exit(i) and on_enter(i + 1) for each page, so a block's time per page includes waiting in a served window; error is the entry the block added to doc.metadata["errors"]. Boundaries are plain callables, not datatrove steps, so they add no stats; a stage without observers has none.

Every stage with a run folder (or an OTLP endpoint) is traced: the builder adds a linecaster.tracing.Tracing observer (build(..., trace_sample=SHARE), --trace-sample; tracing).

docs.title: Warm-up
docs.text: Every block has warm_up() (idempotent): engines load there (InProcess.warm_up()), servers start there (ModelServer, ChatModelServer), a served backend reads its secrets there; blocks with nothing to load keep the no-op. A block's __call__, which datatrove's executors call, warms it up before its run starts: blocks warm up as the stream reaches them, the last one first (the servers before the blocks that call them). The time is the block's own stat, warm_up_seconds (per task), and goes to the observers (on_warm_up(block, seconds)); a page's measured seconds never include loading. An error in a warm-up fails the task (a server that does not start: a ServerError).

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
• Per page. An exception in a per-unit transform's process_page (other than a PipelineConfigError, CatalogError or ServerError, which fail the task) becomes an entry in the page's doc.metadata["errors"]: {"block": class, "step": a model block's step, "preset": its edition or null, "type": the exception's class, "error": the message}; a failed request of a served block is the same with type ServerError; checks (PageValidator, ImageConverter) add field and raw_value. The page goes on as it was.
  • Later model blocks pass it by (skip_on_error, the default for model blocks; stat skipped_after_error), at once: in-process the page leaves the block before the next one enters, served it is put straight onto the block's results (it never waits for the window, nor for the end of the input).
  • Rejects. The RejectWriter writes every page that carries errors to OUT/rejects/<rank>.jsonl, one line per error (key, field, error, raw_value, and the entry's block, step, preset, type), and passes it on: the page records keep failed pages with their errors, so a later pipeline reading them passes them by too.
  • The error budget. A block may fail on max_page_errors of a task's pages (--max-page-errors, default 0.01), judged from the 100th page on: from then, more errors than share × pages fail the task with a PageError (with the default: two failures in the first 100 pages, three in 300). Fewer pages are too few to judge. datatrove reruns a failed task whole.
  • Errors (linecaster.errors): library code raises PipelineConfigError (a pipeline, option or input that cannot work; problems lists them), CatalogError, PageError(page_id, block) and ServerError, all LinecasterErrors, never SystemExit; the linecaster command and a pipeline script's main turn them into exit codes (2: nothing was launched).

docs.title: The run record
docs.text:
OUT/run.yaml (schema linecaster.run-record/1, the pydantic model linecaster.runtime.record.RunRecord, JSON Schema catalog/schemas/run-record-1.json) records the script, the recipe, the command line, the options, where it ran and the software, and:

  • pipeline: per stage its name, tasks and blocks in order, each block as its to_dict() (below) with its contract, composite, group and condition;
  • pipeline_sha256: the hash of the pipeline's functional parameters.

to_dict() gives a block as it was built: {"block": class name, "class": "module:Class", "params": {...}}, every constructor parameter with the value it was given or its default (**kwargs flattened), JSON-compatible: backends as {"backend": "in-process", "engine", "options", "preset", "preset_sha256"}, {"backend": "served", "endpoint", "model", "max_window", ..., "preset", "engine"} or {"backend": "chat", "adapter", "preset", "preset_sha256", "model", "revision", "served_name", "endpoint", "max_window", ...} (a chat adapter's dict plus where its server is), nested blocks as their dicts, secrets as {"env": NAME}, folders as paths, callables as module:name. A block keeps the arguments it was constructed with; live_params names those the builder may change afterwards (a page record reader's provides). A composite's dict is its group: its parameters and its blocks' dicts.

Functional and operational parameters. A parameter is functional when changing it can change what a run writes for a page or an item (its page records, files and texts) or how they are partitioned (item_shards); it is operational when it only changes where things are read and written, how the work is spread and paced, or how a server is reached. pipeline_sha256 covers the functional ones (provenance.functional_pipeline):

Operational (left out) Why folders and file names: data_folder, output_folder, output_filename, image_folder, manifest_folder, ocr_folder, folder, suffix, bucket_by_item, prefix where things are which input files a task reads and how: paths_file, glob_pattern, recursive, limit, skip, shuffle_files, batch_size (a reader's), http (rate limits, the IIIF format asked for), uri_map, progress bars the pages themselves are recorded per page servers and clients: port, host, python, script, vllm, outside_venv, boot_timeout, max_queue, prepare_workers, gpu_memory_utilization, extra_args; an in-process engine's endpoint and timeout (ENGINE_OPERATIONAL: where its service is); a served backend's endpoint, model (the name it is hosted under, unless nothing else names its engine), max_window, initial_window, read_timeout, api_key, headers; a chat backend's served_name and the same (it counts by its adapter, preset edition and hash, model and revision) how a server is started and reached name (datatrove's display name), compression, max_file_size, ImageConverter.keep_bytes presentation, file handling, memory server blocks (ModelServer, ChatModelServer, ServiceServer) as a whole their models count through the blocks they serve the backend (in-process or served) a model block counts by its engine, the engine's options and the preset edition with its hash, wherever it runs

Everything else is functional: block classes and their order, transcription names, engine options, presets and their hashes, the recipe stamp, conditions and groups, writers' formats and options, item_shards. The base list is OPERATIONAL in linecaster.blocks.base.block; a block class adds its own in operational. So a resumed run, a run on another executor or backend, or into another folder has the same hash; another preset, option or block has another.

Resume. A run into an OUT that holds a run record is checked against its newest record (run.yaml, or a later run-<time>.yaml): another pipeline_sha256 is refused with a PipelineConfigError (finished tasks would be skipped and the folder would mix two pipelines' outputs) unless --new-pipeline (the new record is written next to the earlier one and is the one the next resume is checked against); another --tasks is always refused (each task would read other input). The same hash and tasks: a resume, as datatrove's completion markers make it. --dry-run reports the same problems.

Describe mode. linecaster.runtime.run.describe_script(script, argv) builds a pipeline script's plan in the current process without its engines: the script is loaded as a module, its options parsed, presets resolved without checking that their engines are installed, nothing loaded or started. describe_recipe(ref) describes a recipe edition that way (its pipeline script by the recipe's pipeline id, --recipe REF, placeholder folders): what linecaster catalog release records in the lock and verify compares (catalog).

docs.title: Tasks, workers and rate limits
docs.text:
--tasks and --workers are chosen when the command line leaves them open (linecaster.runtime.run.allocate):

Pipeline --tasks --workers with engines 1 every task without engines, with --rate-limit the reader's auto_tasks (from the input), else 1 1 without engines, without --rate-limit the reader's auto_tasks, else 1 one per CPU, at most the tasks

auto_tasks is about 1,000 pages per task for ImageParquetReader and about 5 items per task for ManifestReader (linecaster.blocks.readers.tables.PAGES_PER_TASK, ITEMS_PER_TASK), so a resume repeats little. The harvest (pipelines/harvest.py) asks its reader for one item per task (task_per_item): the tasks divide the items, an item's rows wherever they are in the table (tables.item_runs), so every item is whole in its task and a task that fails costs one item. Its reader also gets reuse_folder (OUT/images): when it reaches an item it lists the item's folder once (an fsspec listing) and reads a page whose image file is already there from the storage instead of fetching it from the source (linecaster.blocks.readers.existing); only pages of interrupted items are read back, so egress stays small. Such a record is complete and says image.extra.reused; the console counts it as done but not in the rate. On a restart the console's size starts with the finished tasks' media_size from datatrove's stats files (linecaster.runtime.local.size_before, read in the background). Parquet tables are divided over the tasks by rows in equal shards, not by files, so a table never needs splitting for a task count. --max-pages N (--parquet, IMAGES; the readers' max_pages) reads the input as if it ended after its first N pages, in the same automatic tasks: a smoke test of the real setup. --limit counts per task, as in datatrove.

--rate-limit holds per worker: each worker process has one fetcher with its limits (HTTPFetcher.shared), so a server sees the workers running at once times the limits; the run states it before it starts (linecaster.runtime.run.rate_note, e.g. rate limits per worker: 150/60, 3/1 · 1 worker → up to 150/min at a server). One worker keeps any rate limit busy: a reader's requests ahead grow while none waits for the limits (linecaster.net.http.prefetched, at most MAX_AHEAD), and the fetcher, with its limits and the window it has grown to, is shared by the tasks a worker runs one after the other (HTTPFetcher.shared).

Proxies. --proxies FILE sends the http(s) requests through a list of proxies with resilient-httpx (the extra resilient-httpx): each attempt through the next proxy in turn; a proxy that fails an attempt (a timeout, a connection or proxy error, a retryable status) is left out for an hour, and the attempt goes out again through another. With no proxy left a page fails (its error budget then stops the task). The file holds one proxy per line, a URL or host:port[:user:pass] as Webshare lists them; the run record keeps its name, and logs show proxies without credentials (linecaster.net.http.redact).

docs.title: The console
docs.text: A local run (--on local, linecaster.runtime.local.LocalExecutor) shows on the terminal: one line naming the pipeline (its blocks, without the builder's boundaries; pages, tasks and workers; what an earlier launch finished), a live progress line (pages done of the total, rate over the last five minutes, size, failed pages, the task, the time left) pinned to the terminal's top row, with everything else scrolling below it (a scroll region, Pinned), a line per finished task and a summary, in human units (linecaster.runtime.console). The Progress observer, which the runtime puts on every stage, counts the pages that leave the pipeline; with several workers each worker process reports its counts to the console about every second. Off a terminal the progress is a log line every 30 s instead. datatrove's own console output (its pipeline listing and stats block per task, the merged stats) goes only to the task logs (OUT/logs/logs/task_<rank>.log, in its full line format) and the stats files, which keep it whole. A launch lists the completion markers once instead of looking them up task by task.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: linecaster.runtime.secrets.EnvVar("NAME") names an environment variable; the value is read in the task (resolve()), never stored: an EnvVar pickles by name, to_dict() writes {"env": "NAME"}. Served(endpoint, model, api_key=EnvVar("NAME"), headers={"X-Team": "ocr", "X-Token": EnvVar("TOKEN")}) (and Chat(preset, endpoint, api_key=..., headers=...) alike) sends Authorization: Bearer <key> and the headers with every request through saturate's AdaptiveClient(headers=...); a key given as text is refused. A missing variable fails the block's warm-up.

docs.title: The item stage
docs.text:
The item-level steps follow a Binder; the usual shape (pipelines/bind.py, and --item-texts of pipelines/transcribe_modular.py):

[PageRecordReader(pages, fetch_images=False, item_shards=True),
 Binder(),                                                  # page records -> item records
 Recomposer("unicode-recomposition@1", unit="item"),        # paragraphs continued across page breaks
 CharacterNormalizer("latin-historic@1", unit="item"),      # normalized lines, paragraphs, table cells
 Composer("docling-composition@1", unit="item"),            # the item's document
 ItemTextWriter(f"{out}/texts"),                            # texts/<variant>/<rank>.jsonl.gz (format="files": <item>.txt|md)
 ItemDocumentWriter(f"{out}/documents", formats=("md", "txt", "json"), by_format=True)]   # documents/<format>/<item>.<ext>

A Splitter after the item-level blocks passes each item's pages on as pages (e.g. to a PageJsonlWriter), with the paragraphs of the item recomposition.

docs.title: Page records
docs.text: Stored page records are rows {"schema": "linecaster.page/2", "id", "text", "page", "errors"} (PageJsonlWriter, PageParquetWriter; PAGE_SCHEMA in linecaster.data.page). PageRecordReader brings older rows to today's format (UPGRADES, keyed by the row's schema, one version at a time): a linecaster.page/1 row names a transcription's steps model (read as steps); a row without schema (the oldest format) names its transcription ocr, read as ocr_new; a .../pages folder without records is read from its sibling rows/ (the folder's earlier name).

docs.title: HF Jobs helpers
docs.text: linecaster.runtime.jobs.dependencies(commit, script=None, engines=True) spells out what a Job installs from a pipeline script's metadata; without a script it raises unless engines=False (linecaster alone). A derivative whose own pipeline needs the engine packages passes ENGINE_SCRIPT (the modular pipeline script of the checkout, pipelines/transcribe_modular.py), whose metadata lists every engine with its sources and pins.

docs.title: Serialization and working images
docs.text: linecaster.formats.{alto,pagexml,hocr} write and read the three XML formats on lxml; linecaster.images.convert turns any page image into the working image. Neither imports datatrove, saturate or an engine.

docs.title: Common rules for ALTO, PAGE and hOCR
docs.text:
1. Native first, extension for the rest. Every value goes into the format's own vocabulary where it has a place. What it cannot hold, or what a reader would infer differently, goes into a small JSON extension on the element: ALTO OtherTag[@TYPE="linecaster"]/@DESCRIPTION referenced by TAGREFS; PAGE UserDefined/UserAttribute[@name="linecaster"]/@value; hOCR @data-linecaster. Writers compute what their own reader would infer and only write the extension when it differs, so ordinary pages carry few (ALTO: line confidences and scores; PAGE: usually only {"polygon": null} for box-only lines). extensions=False writes pure files; they then round-trip only what the format holds natively. Foreign files have no extensions and readers fall back to the inferred values.
  2. Semantic round trip (from_x(to_x(t))): regions, lines and words with their ids, text, geometry, confidences, alternatives, the hyphen flag, region label, raw label, score and heading level, line score, reading_order and row. Not serialized: docling (export only), paragraphs, Line.normalized, extra dicts, the steps' measurements other than datetime, source (readers set kind="converted", format, uri, image size). Readers return regions and lines in document order, which may differ from the original list order; tests compare by id. Provenance round-trips: every StepInfo (step, name, engine, revision, preset, preset hash, recipe, recipe hash, backend, settings; datetime as ALTO processingDateTime and PAGE MetadataItem/@date) is written as ALTO Processing, PAGE MetadataItem type="processingStep" with Labels, and hOCR linecaster-step-<n> metas next to ocr-system and ocr-capabilities (computed from what the file contains). Other tools' provenance is read too (ALTO OCRProcessing, OCR-D PAGE steps, hOCR ocr-system). METS agents per step: linecaster.runtime.provenance.mets_agents.
  3. Writing order. Regions are written by reading_order (regions without one after the others, in list order), each region's lines by reading_order. A line without a region goes before the first region whose first line comes after it; consecutive ones share one block. Readers assign line reading_order = position in document order and row = position in its block, and region reading_order = rank in the format's reading order; the writers record the original value in the extension whenever that differs (gaps, a running head read last, a region without an order), so irregular orders survive too.
  4. Lines without a region. ALTO and PAGE need a block around every line: they get a synthetic TextBlock/TextRegion (id lc_block_<n>, extension {"synthetic": true}) that the reader drops again (with extensions=False it comes back as a text region). In hOCR such lines sit directly in the ocr_page. The synthetic blocks are part of the format's reading order, so consumers that follow it do not lose those lines.
  5. Rounding. ALTO coordinates are floats in the schema: to_alto writes them exactly (shortest repr) by default, precision=0 writes integers. PAGE and hOCR hold integers only: points are rounded half up (floor(v + 0.5), deterministic); boxes are rounded by their corners (x0 = r(x), x1 = r(x + w), w = x1 - x0) so edges agree with the rounded polygons; PAGE clamps negative values at 0 (its schema forbids them). Rounding happens once: a second round trip is the identity (tested).
  6. Confidences. ALTO WC and PAGE TextEquiv/@conf / Coords/@conf are floats in 0..1 and written exactly. hOCR x_wconf is an integer percentage: confidences come back to 0.01. ALTO has no line confidence: a reader derives it as the length-weighted mean of the words' WC (as for foreign files); the writer stores the real line confidence in the extension when it differs from that mean.
  7. Line text vs. words. Words are joined with one space; when a line's text is not that join (double spaces, None with words), the text goes into the extension. A line without words is written as a single ALTO String carrying the line text and confidence (extension {"wordless": true}), as a PAGE TextLine with only a line TextEquiv, as an hOCR line with the text directly in the span. text=None (not recognized) and text="" (recognized as empty) stay distinct in all three.
  8. Output is deterministic: same input, same bytes (PAGE Created/LastChange default to 1970-01-01T00:00:00; pass created= for a real timestamp).
  9. Ids are written as they are. Schema-valid output needs ids that are XML NCNames (letters, digits, _ - ., not starting with a digit); the producers' ids (text_2, orphan_0, ...) are. Ids the writers make up themselves (synthetic blocks, tags, the page) avoid every existing id.
  10. Known limits. Characters XML cannot carry (C0 controls other than tab/newline) make the writers raise lxml's ValueError; text is not silently altered. Language is written to hOCR lang only.
  11. Tests cover the fixture in tests/conftest.py (polygon regions, baselines, box-only lines, empty and unrecognized lines, a region-less line, hyphenation, alternatives), irregular orders, 300 seeded random transcriptions per format (every tenth also validated against the XSD), and foreign files (ALTO v2 mm10, v3 without namespace, eScriptorium v4; PAGE 2010 and Transkribus 2013; Tesseract hOCR and tag-soup HTML).

docs.title: ALTO (writes 4.4, reads v1 to v4)
docs.text:
Transcription ALTO region TextBlock (Illustration TYPE=<label> for picture/chart regions without lines); Shape/Polygon only when the polygon is not the box region label LayoutTag TYPE="label" LABEL=<docling label>, one per distinct label, in TAGREFS raw label LayoutTag TYPE="raw_label" LABEL=<raw> region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/ElementRef (regions with an order + synthetic blocks); without ReadingOrder readers use document order (ALTO's implicit order) line TextLine with BASELINE="x,y x,y ..." (4.2+ points syntax), Shape/Polygon word String (WC, ALTERNATIVE), SP between words; a hyphen word that ends in - ¬ ⸗ ‐ soft hyphen = is split into String + HYP (reader re-joins: word text and line text unchanged) score, heading level, line confidence extension

Reading foreign ALTO: namespaces v1–v4 or none; blocks anywhere under Page (margins, PrintSpace, nested ComposedBlocks, which are transparent); raw label = the LABEL of the first referenced tag (Transkribus StructureTag, eScriptorium OtherTag), Docling label mapped from it; BASELINE as a single number (ALTO < 4.2) becomes a horizontal line across the line box; SUBS_TYPE/SUBS_CONTENT are ignored (the word keeps its CONTENT); missing ids are generated (line_<rank>, <line>_w<k>, block_<n>); GraphicalElements are not read. Units: pixel is read as is; with image_width/image_height and Page/@WIDTH/@HEIGHT every coordinate is scaled to the image (also corrects pixel ALTO made on a master of another size); mm10 and inch1200 without the image size need dpi= (px = v * dpi / 254 resp. / 1200); otherwise from_alto raises ValueError rather than guessing.

docs.title: PAGE (writes 2019-07-15, reads 2009–2019)
docs.text:
Transcription PAGE region TextRegion with @type from the label (below); ImageRegion, ChartRegion, TableRegion, MathsRegion for picture, chart, table, formula regions without lines (PAGE does not allow lines in them) raw label @custom="structure {type:<raw>;}" (Transkribus convention; ; { } \ escaped as \uXXXX) region score / line score Coords/@conf region order ReadingOrder/OrderedGroup/RegionRefIndexed (nested groups read recursively, index sorted) line TextLine: Coords = polygon (the box when there is none, extension {"polygon": null}), Baseline, TextEquiv/@conf; alternatives as TextEquiv/@index 2.. (primary 1) word Word: Coords = box, TextEquiv bbox not in PAGE: readers take the bounds of Coords; the writer stores the box when it differs

Label mapping, Docling → TextRegion/@type: text, paragraph, list_item, handwritten_text, reference → paragraph; title, section_header → heading; page_header → header; page_footer → footer; caption → caption; footnote → footnote; document_index → TOC-entry; others → other (or paragraph). Reading: structure {type:...} wins when it is a known name, then @type: paragraph → text, heading → section_header, header → page_header, footer, page-number, signature-mark, catch-word → page_footer, footnote(-continued)/endnote → footnote, TOC-entry → document_index, list-label → list_item, everything else → text; the raw label is the structure type, else @type, else the element name (TableRegion). The writer adds the Docling label to the extension when the reverse mapping would not return it (e.g. title → heading → section_header). The same name table (_xml.RAW_TO_DOCLING) also maps eScriptorium/SegmOnto zones and PP-DocLayout names. Old PAGE Coords/Point children are read; text on glyphs only is joined into the word.

docs.title: hOCR 1.2
docs.text:
Transcription hOCR region div of class ocr_carea (page_header → ocr_header, page_footer → ocr_footer, picture/chart → ocr_photo, table → ocr_table, formula → ocr_math) with one p.ocr_par; bbox, poly when not the box line span.ocr_line: bbox, baseline slope offset (hOCR's straight line from the box's bottom-left), poly, x_wconf baseline that baseline cannot express (polyline, vertical) also x_bline x1 y1 x2 y2 ... (custom property) word span.ocrx_word: bbox, x_wconf raw label, region score, heading level, hyphen, alternatives extension

Reading foreign hOCR: XHTML or tag-soup HTML (lxml.html fallback); regions are the top-level float/area classes, lines are ocr_line, ocr_textfloat, ocr_caption and ocr_header/ ocr_footer spans inside a region (Tesseract's line classes); word text includes nested <strong>/<em>; image "..." may contain ;.

docs.title: Working images (linecaster.images.convert)
docs.text:
The working format for converted images is lossless WebP at full resolution (the block ImageConverter, preset working-image); lossy output is never produced. Delivered images used as they are (an access derivative) stay as delivered. Pages larger than the size limit go to rejects/.

  • Size limit (check_size): width ≤ 16,383 and height ≤ 16,383 (WebP) and width × height ≤ 2 × PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, read at call time, never changed. 2× is exactly where Pillow's Image.open raises DecompressionBombError; that error is turned into ImageTooLarge with the same kind of reason. Checked from the header (Image.open without load), so oversized pages are never decoded; between 1× and 2× Pillow's warning is silenced and the page converted.
  • Color: embedded ICC → sRGB (LittleCMS, perceptual); a profile that cannot be applied is reported (icc_error) and the plain conversion used. 16-bit grayscale → 8 bit as round(v·255/65535); Pillow reads 16-bit RGB as 8-bit itself. Grayscale/bilevel/palette → RGB. Alpha is composited onto white (alpha_flattened); fully opaque alpha is just dropped. CMYK without a profile: Pillow's conversion. EXIF orientation is not applied (coordinates refer to the stored pixels) but reported as exif_orientation.
  • Encoding: always lossless WebP (VP8L), full resolution, method=0, exact=True; effort (Pillow's quality for lossless) defaults to Pillow's 80.
  • info: format, width, height, source_format, source_mode, pixels_sha256 (sha256 of the decoded 8-bit RGB bytes, row-major, what the WebP decodes to), sha256 (of the WebP), decoder (Pillow x / <source library> y / libwebp z), webp_settings, icc_applied, alpha_flattened; the keys match PageImage where they overlap.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: Every run is traced with OpenTelemetry (linecaster.tracing): spans per task always, spans per page for a sample chosen by page id plus every page that failed. Traces go to the run folder and, when the standard OTEL_* variables say so, to an OTLP endpoint; nothing is sent anywhere else. Terms are the glossary's.

docs.title: What is traced
docs.text:
Task spans, for every task:

Span What it covers Attributes (besides linecaster.block) linecaster.task the task, from its first page to its end (failed: status error, linecaster.error.type) task, tasks, sample, stage, units.failed_exported linecaster.warm_up a block loading its engine or client (warm_up()), per block that loads something block.name, preset, edition, engine, model, backend, server linecaster.server.start a server block's warm-up: starting linecaster serve or vLLM/SGLang until it answers server, model, preset, port linecaster.reader.file a file a reader is through: a Parquet file, a file of page records, a manifest (wall time, while its pages also passed the later blocks) file, pages, seconds.own (the time spent reading) linecaster.writer.flush a page record writer closing its files (a remote file is uploaded then) files

An image folder's file is one page: its reading is the page's, not a task span.

Unit traces, one per page (or item):

Span Parent What it covers linecaster.page (linecaster.item for items a binder makes) none: the trace's root from the reader (or the earliest fetch for it) to the end of the stage's last block linecaster.http.fetch the page each http(s) request a reader made for it: http.host, http.status, http.attempts, http.retries, http.wait_seconds (the rate limits' wait), http.tries (each attempt: a status such as 200 or 429 for a response read whole, 200-cut for one the deadline per attempt cut, no-response for a timeout or a connection or proxy error), http.what (image, ocr) linecaster.block the page one per block, from the boundary before it to the one after it: for a served block it includes the time the page waited in the window linecaster.request.prepare the served block's span building the request (image encoding), in saturate's prepare threads linecaster.request the served block's span from the built request to its result: the wait for a window slot, the HTTP call, retries; tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason linecaster.serve.decode, linecaster.serve.queue, linecaster.serve.model the request in linecaster serve: the image decoded and the transcription read, the wait for the model's worker, the model call (lines, regions, words of its result)

A page's spans are children of its context explicitly, never of "the current span": pages are interleaved in the stream. A page that leaves the stage's blocks through a binder ends its trace there; the items get their own. A page that never reaches the end of the stage (a block dropped it) is ended when the task ends (linecaster.unfinished).

A failed page (an entry added to doc.metadata["errors"] in this stage) has status error on its root and on the block's span, with linecaster.error.type.

Attributes are identifiers and numbers under linecaster.*, never text or images: block (class), block.name (datatrove name), block.family, unit, page.id, item.id, step, preset and edition (of id@edition), engine, model, backend (in-process, served), server (the endpoint), counts on a block's span as the page leaves it (lines, regions, words of the block's transcription), tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, finish_reason, error.type, region (a region recognizer's request). The resource of every span: service.name (linecaster), service.version, host.name, linecaster.process (pipeline, serve), linecaster.run (the run folder's name, or LINECASTER_RUN), linecaster.task, linecaster.tasks, linecaster.stage, linecaster.gpu and linecaster.gpus (from the NVIDIA driver, when there is one); OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES adds to them.

Log records carry trace_id and span_id in extra (JSON lines on Jobs show them): the page a record names by page_id, else the span of the per-unit block running in the thread, else the task's span.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
--trace-sample SHARE (build(..., trace_sample=), default 0.01): a page is sampled when a hash of its id (BLAKE2b, 64 bits) is below SHARE, so the same pages on every rerun and machine, and a larger sample contains a smaller one. 0 traces only failed pages and the task spans; 1 traces every page. A sampled page's record carries its trace id (page.metadata.trace_id), so the page records lead to the trace.

Every page gets a trace context (doc.metadata["trace"]["traceparent"], W3C, flags 01 for a sampled page, 00 otherwise). The spans of an unsampled page are recorded but not sampled and held per page in a span processor (linecaster.tracing.export.PageBuffer) until the page's root ends: if the page failed in the stage they are exported, otherwise dropped. The memory this takes is bounded by the pages in flight: about 3 KB per ended span, one per block and two per request (about 40 KB per page for the twelve blocks of the squiddle recipe). In-process a page or two are in flight; a served block holds at most its window and its result queue (max_window + 4 × max_window pages), so with the default window of 32 and five served blocks about 800 pages, some 30 MB. A page dropped by a block is held until the task ends. linecaster serve records nothing for an unsampled page: a failed unsampled page's trace has the pipeline's spans, not the server's.

docs.title: Where traces go
docs.text:
• The run folder, always: OUT/traces/<rank>.jsonl.gz per task (OUT/traces/<stage>/<rank>.jsonl.gz with several stages), any fsspec folder like the logs; linecaster serve started by a task (ModelServer) writes <rank>.serve.jsonl.gz next to it (the task gives it the file in LINECASTER_TRACES). The format is OpenTelemetry's file exporter format: one ExportTraceServiceRequest per line in the OTLP JSON encoding, gzipped. Spans are written in batches (every 2 s), each flushed to the file, which is closed (uploaded, for a remote folder) when the task ends, also when it fails; a process killed outright loses its last batch, and linecaster traces reads such a file as far as it goes. A rerun of a task replaces its file. linecaster serve closes its file when it is stopped (the first SIGTERM or SIGINT ends it gracefully; its handlers are set again after the engines load, since an engine's library may replace them).
  • An OTLP endpoint, when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT is set (and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER is not none): OTLP over HTTP (protobuf), configured by the standard variables (headers, timeouts). linecaster serve exports there too; ChatModelServer starts vLLM with --otlp-traces-endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf.

Without a run folder (run_pages, tests) and without OTLP nothing is traced.

The trace context and the servers. saturate sends the same headers with every request, so a served block puts the page's traceparent into the request body ("traceparent"), which linecaster serve reads (as it reads the header, if a client sends one). An OpenAI-compatible chat server reads it from the headers only: vLLM continues a traceparent header when started with --otlp-traces-endpoint, so with OTLP configured its spans reach the backend, but as traces of their own, not joined to the pages'.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
linecaster traces OUT [--by block|preset|task] [--slowest N] [--json]

reads OUT/traces/**/*.jsonl.gz (a task still running: what its file has so far) and prints:

  • per block (or preset edition, or task) the duration of its linecaster.block spans over the traced pages (n, p50, p90, p99, errors); for served blocks the split: prepare, request (as the pipeline saw it), and the server's queue, decode and model;
  • the gaps: per block the time it had no page in it between its first page and its last (it waited for its input), when every page was traced (--trace-sample 1);
  • the N slowest traced pages (default 10) with their id, seconds, lines, slowest block and trace id;
  • per task its duration, GPU and sample, the warm-up of each block and the server starts, the reader's files (pages, seconds reading) and the writers' flush.

--json gives the same as data.
